Præterea advertendum, quia (ut ait Hieronymus) prædictis regnis non improperat Deus, quod legem scriptam transgressi sunt : non enim data est eis. Idcirco qui sine lege peccaverunt, sine lege perierunt. Juda vero Deus concessit legem, templum, sacerdotes Leviticos, cærimonias et mandata : ideo de legis et præceptorum transgressione arguitur, et secundum legem damnatur.
paras.en: [[2:5|And I will send a fire into Juda|Et mittam ignem in Juda]], that is, into the cities or the people of the kingdom of Juda, [[2:5|and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem|et devorabit ædes Jerusalem]]: namely when the army of the Chaldeans burned or laid waste the land and people of Juda, and Nabuzardan, the captain of the soldiers, set fire to the temple and the city of Jerusalem[[4 Kings 25:8||]][[4 Kings 25:9||]]. Hence the Lord says through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:20|I will melt you down|Conflabo vos]], [[Ezech 22:21|And will gather you together, and will burn you in the fire of my wrath, and you shall be melted in the midst thereof|et congregabo, et succendam vos in igne furoris mei ; et conflabimini in medio ejus]], [[Ezech 22:22|As silver is melted in the midst of the furnace|sicut conflatur argentum in medio fornacis]]. It should be noted, moreover, that (as Jerome says) God does not reproach the kingdoms mentioned before with having transgressed the written law, for it was not given to them[[Rom 2:14||]]. Therefore [[Rom 2:12|whosoever have sinned without the law shall perish without the law|qui sine lege peccaverunt, sine lege perierunt]]. But to Juda God granted the law, the temple, the Levitical priests, the ceremonies and the commandments: therefore Juda is charged with transgressing the law and the precepts, and is condemned according to the law.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Super tribus sceleribus Israel, et super quatuor non convertam eum, id est, propter peccata decem tribuum, tertio et quarto repetita, non parcam eis, sed hostibus tradam ; pro eo quod vendiderit argento justum, id est, justos et simplices pro pecunia gentibus vicinis in servos vendiderunt. Vel sensus est, quod justorum causam atque judicium subverterunt, munera accipiendo, sicut de quibusdam cantatur in Psalmo : Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem, et facies peccatorum sumitis? Et in Isaia : Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributiones, pupillo non judicant, et causa viduæ non ingreditur ad eos. Et pauperem pro calceamentis, id est, pauperes vendiderunt pro pretio vili, et modice reputant homines Dei imagine ac similitudine insignitos. In quo patet eorum injustitia, violentia, crudelitas, atque cupiditas.
paras.en: [[2:6|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four I will not convert him|Hæc dicit Dominus : Super tribus sceleribus Israel, et super quatuor non convertam eum]], that is, for the sins of the ten tribes, repeated a third and a fourth time, I will not spare them, but will deliver them to their enemies; [[2:6|because he hath sold the just man for silver|pro eo quod vendiderit argento justum]], that is, they sold the just and simple for money as slaves to the neighbouring nations. Or the sense is that they overturned the cause and the judgment of the just by taking bribes, as is sung of certain men in the Psalm: [[Ps 81:2|How long will you judge unjustly: and accept the persons of the wicked?|Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem, et facies peccatorum sumitis?]] And in Isaias: [[Is 1:23|they all love bribes, they run after rewards. They judge not for the fatherless: and the widow's cause cometh not in to them|Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributiones, pupillo non judicant, et causa viduæ non ingreditur ad eos]]. [[2:6|and the poor man for a pair of shoes|Et pauperem pro calceamentis]], that is, they sold the poor for a paltry price, and set little value on men marked with the image and likeness of God. In this their injustice, violence, cruelty and greed are plain to see.

paras.t: Qui impii Israelitæ conterunt super pulverem terræ capita pauperum, id est, pauperes pedibus suis conculcant, atque in terram projectos pessumdant, et viam humilium declinant, id est, cum humilibus et parvis personis ire despiciunt, talesque sibi obviantes abhorrent et vitant. Et filius ac pater ejus ierunt ad puellam. Translatio Septuaginta interpretum continet, Ad eamdem puellam. Unde sensus est, quod socer polluit nurum, violando puellam suo filio desponsatam ; vel crebro patres et filii eisdem commixti sunt feminis : in quo de incestu notantur. Cui simile est quod ad Corinthios scribit Apostolus : Auditur inter vos fornicatio, et talis fornicatio, qualis nec inter gentes, ita ut uxorem patris sui quis habeat. Hæc prohibuit Moyses in Levitico : Turpitudinem, inquit, patris tui non discooperies, et turpitudinem nurus tuæ non revelabis. Ut violarent, id est, inhonorarent, et quantum in ipsis erat, immundum ostenderent, nomen sanctum meum, id est me ipsum. Quemadmodum enim devoti Deum honorando, ostendunt quod ipse sit sanctus, sublimis et magnus, cui in sanctitate, timore ac reverentia obsequuntur ; sic impii Deum inhonorando, quantum in ipsis est, Deum ostendunt non sanctum, quia sic agunt ac si mala Deo placerent, et alios ad Dei inhonorationem inducunt. Propter quod dicit Apostolus : Nomen Dei per vos blasphematur inter gentes. Et per Ezechielem Dominus ait frequenter : Contaminastis nomen sanctum meum ; et sanctificabo nomen sanctum meum, quod per vos pollutum est inter gentes. Hinc ergo devoti dicuntur Deum magnificare, sanctificare et exaltare ; injusti vero, violare et spernere. Porro, vox hæc, ut, magis denotat hoc loco concomitantiam vel sequelam, quam causam : quia opera mala sequitur violatio nominis Dei, quamvis non sit intenta.
paras.en: [[2:7|They|Qui]], that is, the wicked Israelites, [[2:7|bruise the heads of the poor upon the dust of the earth|conterunt super pulverem terræ capita pauperum]], that is, they trample the poor under their feet, and throw them to the ground and crush them, [[2:7|and turn aside the way of the humble|et viam humilium declinant]], that is, they disdain to walk with humble and lowly persons, and loathe and shun such people when they meet them. [[2:7|and the son and his father have gone to the same young woman|Et filius ac pater ejus ierunt ad puellam]]. The translation of the Seventy interpreters has: *To the same young woman*. Hence the sense is that the father-in-law defiled his daughter-in-law, violating the girl betrothed to his son; or that fathers and sons often had intercourse with the same women: in which they are charged with incest. Like this is what the Apostle writes to the Corinthians: It is [[1 Cor 5:1|heard that there is fornication among you and such fornication as the like is not among the heathens: that one should have his father's wife|Auditur inter vos fornicatio, et talis fornicatio, qualis nec inter gentes, ita ut uxorem patris sui quis habeat]]. Moses forbade these things in Leviticus: [[Lev 18:7|Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father|Turpitudinem, inquit, patris tui non discooperies]], he says, and [[Lev 18:15|Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy daughter in law|turpitudinem nurus tuæ non revelabis]]. [[2:7|to profane|Ut violarent]], that is, to dishonour, and as far as lay in them to show as unclean, [[2:7|my holy name|nomen sanctum meum]], that is, myself. For just as the devout, by honouring God, show that he is holy, sublime and great, whom they serve in holiness, fear and reverence; so the wicked, by dishonouring God, show God, as far as lies in them, to be not holy, since they act as if evil deeds pleased God, and lead others to dishonour God. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:24|the name of God through you is blasphemed among the Gentiles|Nomen Dei per vos blasphematur inter gentes]]. And the Lord often says through Ezechiel: Ye have defiled my holy name[[Ezech 20:39||]][[Ezech 36:20||]]; and: [[Ezech 36:23|I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the Gentiles|sanctificabo nomen sanctum meum, quod per vos pollutum est inter gentes]] [Denis reads "my holy name, which was profaned by you among the Gentiles"]. Hence, then, the devout are said to magnify, sanctify and exalt God, but the unjust to profane and despise him. Further, the word *ut* ["to", "so that"] here denotes accompaniment or consequence rather than purpose: for the profanation of God's name follows upon evil works, though it is not intended.

paras.t: Et super vestimentis pignoratis accubuerunt : id est, vestimenta quæ violenter rapuerunt a bonis et his qui cum ipsis ad adoranda idola ire noluerunt, supposuerunt sibi secus loca atque altaria ubi in honorem idolorum fecerunt lasciva convivia. Hæc autem vestimenta per modum prædæ ablata, dicuntur vadimonium seu pignora : quia pro liberatione a morte, dabantur a spoliatis. Dictum est autem in Osee, quomodo pessimi filii Israel posuerunt custodes in monte Thabor et alibi, qui comprehenderent et spoliarent transeuntes versus Jerusalem ad adorandum Deum verum. Et vinum damnatorum, id est emptum de bonis quæ rapuerunt ab his quos damnabant et opprimebant injuste, bibebant in domo dei sui, id est in fanis idolorum, quæ deos putabant.
paras.en: [[2:8|And they sat down upon garments laid to pledge|Et super vestimentis pignoratis accubuerunt]] [the margin adds the Vulgate's words, *juxta omne altare*, "by every altar", which Denis leaves out of the lemma]: that is, the garments they had violently seized from good men, and from those who would not go with them to worship the idols, they spread under themselves beside the places and altars where they held wanton banquets in honour of the idols. These garments, carried off as plunder, are called a security or pledges, because they were given by those who were stripped of them in exchange for their release from death. It has been said in Osee how the wicked children of Israel set watchmen on Mount Thabor and elsewhere, to seize and rob those who were passing towards Jerusalem to worship the true God[[Osee 5:1||]]. [[2:8|and drank the wine of the condemned|Et vinum damnatorum]], that is, wine bought from the goods they had seized from those whom they unjustly condemned and oppressed, [[2:8|in the house of their God|bibebant in domo dei sui]], that is, in the shrines of the idols, which they took for gods.

paras.t: Præterea advertendum, quod aliqui per quatuor peccata Israel intelligunt venditionem Joseph a fratribus suis, adorationem vituli aurei in deserto, persecutionem Prophetarum, et Christi occisionem. Et propter hoc quartum peccatum finaliter derelicti sunt Judæi. De aliis vero tribus emendati fuerunt atque conversi.
paras.en: It should be noted, moreover, that some take the four sins of Israel to be the selling of Joseph by his brothers[[Gen 37:28||]], the adoration of the golden calf in the desert[[Ex 32:6||]], the persecution of the Prophets[[Matt 23:34||]], and the slaying of Christ[[Acts 7:52||]]. And for this fourth sin the Jews were finally forsaken; but of the other three they were amended and converted.

paras.t: Enarratis piaculis Israel, recitat Dominus beneficia sua Israeli collata, ut opposita juxta se collocata, ex mutua comparatione clarius agnoscantur. Ego autem exterminavi Amorrhæum a facie eorum : id est, Sehon regem Amorrhæorum et populum suum, aliosque Chananæos ejeci et interfeci ad introitum filiorum Israel, seu duodecim tribuum. Beneficia namque quæ nunc describuntur, non solum decem tribus data sunt. Cujus altitudo, cedrorum altitudo ejus : id est, magnæ staturæ fuerunt, et tantum eminebant aliis in longitudine, quantum cedri aliis arboribus, quantum ad longum. Propter quod exploratores dixerunt in Numeris : Populus magnus et proceræ staturæ ; semen Enacim vidimus ibi, quibus comparati, quasi locustæ videbamur. Et fortis fuit ipse populus Amorrhæus quasi quercus, quæ est arbor durissima atque fortissima. Et contrivi fructum ejus desuper, et radices ejus subter, id est, superbiam ejus dejeci, principes ejus et semen contrivi, subditos quoque ipsius, et vim generativam in eo destruxi. Loquitur autem Dominus de toto populo illo metaphorice, quasi de arbore una, quæ quum penitus destruitur, rami ejus ac radix vastantur ac corrumpuntur, ut non amplius reparetur aut crescat. Sic Deus Amorrhæos illos dejecit.
paras.en: Having recounted the crimes of Israel, the Lord recalls the benefits he bestowed on Israel, so that, opposites being set side by side, each may be more clearly recognized by comparison with the other. [[2:9|Yet I cast out the Amorrhite before their face|Ego autem exterminavi Amorrhæum a facie eorum]]: that is, I cast out and slew Sehon king of the Amorrhites and his people[[Num 21:24||]], and the other Chanaanites, at the entry of the children of Israel, that is, of the twelve tribes. For the benefits now described were not given to the ten tribes only. [[2:9|whose height was like the height of cedars|Cujus altitudo, cedrorum altitudo ejus]]: that is, they were of great stature, and stood out above others in height as much as cedars above other trees, as regards height. That is why the spies said in Numbers: A people great and of tall stature; we saw there the seed of Enacim[[Num 13:29||]][[Num 13:33||]][[Deut 1:28||]][[Deut 2:21||]], [[Num 13:34|in comparison of whom, we seemed like locusts|quibus comparati, quasi locustæ videbamur]] [Denis joins words of Num 13:33–34 and Deut 1:28 and 2:21, as the margin's references show]. [[2:9|and who was strong as an oak|Et fortis fuit ipse populus Amorrhæus quasi quercus]], that is, that Amorrhite people, for the oak is a very hard and very strong tree. [[2:9|and I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots beneath|Et contrivi fructum ejus desuper, et radices ejus subter]], that is, I cast down his pride, crushed his princes and his offspring, and his subjects too, and destroyed his power of generation. The Lord speaks of that whole people metaphorically, as of one tree, which, when it is utterly destroyed, has its branches and its root laid waste and spoiled, so that it can no more be restored or grow. So did God cast down those Amorrhites.

paras.t: Ego sum qui ascendere vos feci de terra Ægypti et eduxi vos de loco ad locum, præcedendo in die per columnam nubis, et nocte per ignem, in deserto quadraginta annis, ut possideretis terram Amorrhæi. Non servatur hoc loco ordo historiæ, sicut nec frequenter in aliis locis Scripturæ, ubi de Dei laudibus agitur : quod maxime patet in libro Psalmorum, in quo tertius psalmus scriptus est, tractans de persecutione David ab Absalone, et multi alii psalmi sequuntur, loquentes de rebus quæ diu ante contigerunt. Certum est autem, quod Deus eduxit Israel de Ægypto ante quam Amorrhæum præfato modo dejecit.
paras.en: [[2:10|It is I that brought you up out of the land of Egypt|Ego sum qui ascendere vos feci de terra Ægypti]], [[2:10|and I led you|et eduxi vos]] from place to place, going before you by day in the pillar of cloud and by night in the fire[[Ex 13:21||]][[Ex 13:22||]], [[2:10|forty years through the wilderness, that you might possess the land of the Amorrhite|in deserto quadraginta annis, ut possideretis terram Amorrhæi]]. The order of the history is not kept here, as often it is not in other places of Scripture where God's praises are the subject: this is most evident in the book of Psalms, in which the third psalm is written about the persecution of David by Absalom, and many other psalms follow that speak of things which happened long before. Now it is certain that God brought Israel out of Egypt before he cast down the Amorrhite in the manner described.

paras.t: Et suscitavi, id est, de parvo statu gratiose promovi, quosdam de filiis vestris in Prophetas : quales fuerunt Elias et Eliseus ; et de juvenibus vestris suscitavi et feci Nazaræos : qui erant Deo consecrati ex utero, super quorum capita non ascendit novacula, quia non radebantur, nec vinum potabant. Tales fuerunt Samson (ut patet in libro Judicum), et Samuel (primo Regum). Aliqui tamen erant Nazaræi pro toto tempore vitæ suæ ; aliqui, ad tempus determinatum.
paras.en: [[2:11|And I raised up|Et suscitavi]], that is, graciously advanced from a lowly state, some [[2:11|of your sons for prophets|de filiis vestris in Prophetas]], such as were Elias and Eliseus; [[2:11|and of your young men|et de juvenibus vestris]] I raised up and made [[2:11|Nazarites|Nazaræos]]: who were consecrated to God from the womb, upon whose heads no razor came, for they were not shaven, nor did they drink wine[[Num 6:2||]][[Num 6:3||]][[Num 6:4||]][[Num 6:5||]]. Such were Samson (as appears in the book of Judges[[Judg 16:17||]]) and Samuel (in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 1:11||]]). Some, however, were Nazarites for the whole time of their life; others for a fixed time.

paras.t: Numquid non ita est, filii Israel? dicit Dominus. Et propinabatis Nazaræis vinum : quum tamen in lege scriptum sit, ut tempore consecrationis suæ, vinum et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibant, ne curis sæculi aut vitio gulæ a Dei vacatione impediantur. Et Prophetis mandabatis, dicentes : Ne prophetetis. Erant enim incorrigibiles, et eos a quibus redarguebantur, repellebant. Hinc in Isaia scriptum est : Dicunt videntibus, Nolite videre ; et adspicientibus, Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt ; loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores. Horum vitiorum debita subinfertur punitio.
paras.en: [[2:11|Is it not so, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord?|Numquid non ita est, filii Israel? dicit Dominus]] [[2:12|And you will present wine to the Nazarites|Et propinabatis Nazaræis vinum]] [Denis reads *propinabatis*, "you gave", for the Vulgate's future *propinabitis*; so below, *mandabatis*]: although it is written in the law that during the time of their consecration they shall not drink wine or anything that can make drunk[[Num 6:3||]][[Lev 10:9||]], lest they be hindered by the cares of the world or by the vice of gluttony from giving themselves to God. [[2:12|and command the prophets, saying: Prophesy not|Et Prophetis mandabatis, dicentes : Ne prophetetis]]. For they were incorrigible, and drove away those by whom they were rebuked. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 30:10|Who say to the seers: See not: and to them that behold: Behold not for us those things that are right: speak unto us pleasant things, see errors for us|Dicunt videntibus, Nolite videre ; et adspicientibus, Nolite adspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt ; loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores]]. The punishment due to these vices is added next.

paras.t: Ecce ego Deus omnipotens, justus judex, qui nullum malum patior ire inultum, stridebo subter vos, vel, super vos, ut aliqui dicunt, id est, terribiliter vobis minabor, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno : id est, ad tantam calamitatem atque tormenta vos pertraham, quod velut currus fœno gravatus, emittetis altos miserabilesque clamores, quando in manus inciderit Assyriorum. Notandum quoque, quod Propheta hic loquitur de toto populo quasi de uno. Unde non omnia eisdem conveniunt, quamvis quasi de eisdem dicantur.
paras.en: [[2:13|Behold, I|Ecce ego]], almighty God, the just judge, who suffer no evil to go unpunished, [[2:13|will screak under you|stridebo subter vos]], or, *over you*, as some say, that is, I will threaten you terribly, [[2:13|as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay|sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno]]: that is, I will drag you into such calamity and torments that, like a cart weighed down with hay, you will send up loud and pitiful cries, when you fall into the hands of the Assyrians. Note, too, that the Prophet here speaks of the whole people as of one man. Hence not everything fits each of them, though it is said as if of the same persons.

paras.t: Et peribit fuga a veloce, id est, veloces et agiles manus hostium evadere non valebunt, et fortis non obtinebit virtutem suam, id est, viri potentes fortitudinem suam amittent, et robustus non salvabit animam suam, id est vitam, sed occidetur ; et tenens arcum non stabit, id est, sagittarii coram Assyriis cadent, et velox pedibus suis non salvabitur, id est, velociter currendo nequaquam effugiet, et ascensor equi non salvabit animam suam, id est, nec equites vitam suam ab Assyriis liberabunt, sed capientur ; et robustus corde, id est animo constans et audax, inter fortes nudus fugiet in die illa, dicit Dominus, id est, armis et vestimentis cursum impedientibus rejectis, conabitur fugere, quamvis non possit effugere. Hæc autem dicuntur, non quod omnes tales de populo Israel ab Assyriis fuerint capti, vel interfecti : dictum est enim in Osee, quod aliqui evaserunt manus Assyriorum ; sed tam pauci fuerunt, quod comparatione aliorum non computantur. Quod enim modicum est, non reputatur.
paras.en: [[2:14|And flight shall perish from the swift|Et peribit fuga a veloce]], that is, the swift and nimble will not be able to escape the hands of the enemy, [[2:14|and the valiant shall not possess his strength|et fortis non obtinebit virtutem suam]], that is, mighty men will lose their strength, [[2:14|neither shall the strong save his life|et robustus non salvabit animam suam]], that is, his life, but he will be slain; [[2:15|And he that holdeth the bow shall not stand|et tenens arcum non stabit]], that is, the archers will fall before the Assyrians, [[2:15|and the swift of foot shall not escape|et velox pedibus suis non salvabitur]], that is, he will by no means get away by running swiftly, [[2:15|neither shall the rider of the horse save his life|et ascensor equi non salvabit animam suam]], that is, neither will the horsemen deliver their lives from the Assyrians, but they will be taken; [[2:16|And the stout of heart|et robustus corde]], that is, steadfast and bold in spirit, [[2:16|among the valiant shall flee away naked in that day, saith the Lord|inter fortes nudus fugiet in die illa, dicit Dominus]], that is, throwing away the arms and garments that hinder his running, he will try to flee, though he cannot escape. These things are said not because all such men among the people of Israel were taken or slain by the Assyrians, for it was said in Osee that some escaped the hands of the Assyrians[[Osee 14:1||]] [the margin gives Osee xiv, 1, which speaks of Samaria's ruin, not of any escaping]; but they were so few that in comparison with the rest they are not counted. For what is very little is not reckoned.

2.title: Expositio tropologica ejusdem capituli secundi.
2.title_en: Tropological exposition of the same second chapter.

paras.t: Moab interpretatur, ex patre. Filia enim major ipsius Lot, quum esset inverecundior juniore sorore, de suo non erubescens incesto, tale imposuit filio suo (quem habuit ex proprio patre) nomen, quod omnibus innotesceret filium hunc de patre matris suæ progenitum, vocans eum Moab. Per quem hoc loco intelliguntur perversi, qui alios verbo aut exemplis aut aliis modis corrumpunt. De talibus enim loquitur Christus: Vos ex patre diabolo estis; et Joannes in prima sua epistola, Qui peccat, ex diabolo est. Denique Idumæa interpretatur, terrena. Rex ergo Idumæorum, est rector propriæ carnis et sensualium affectionum: qui dominatur animo suo, et carnem suam crucifigit cum vitiis et concupiscentiis, implens illud Apostoli ad Romanos: Obsecro vos, fratres, per misericordiam Dei, ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem. Unde et alibi dicit: Hæc est voluntas Dei, sanctificatio vestra, ut sciat unusquisque vestrum possidere vas suum in honore, et non in passione desiderii.
paras.en: Moab is interpreted *from the father*. For the elder daughter of Lot, being more shameless than her younger sister and not blushing at her incest, gave the son she had by her own father such a name as would make known to all that this son was begotten of his mother's father, calling him Moab[[Gen 19:37||]]. By him are understood here the perverse, who corrupt others by word, or by example, or in other ways. For of such Christ says: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]; and John in his first epistle: [[1 John 3:8|He that committeth sin is of the devil|Qui peccat, ex diabolo est]]. Next, Idumea is interpreted *earthly*. The king of the Idumeans, then, is he who rules his own flesh and the affections of the senses: who is master of his own spirit, and crucifies his flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]], fulfilling that saying of the Apostle to the Romans: [[Rom 12:1|I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God|Obsecro vos, fratres, per misericordiam Dei, ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem]]. Hence he says elsewhere also: [[1 Thess 4:3|For this is the will of God, your sanctification|Hæc est voluntas Dei, sanctificatio vestra]], [[1 Thess 4:4|That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour|ut sciat unusquisque vestrum possidere vas suum in honore]], [[1 Thess 4:5|Not in the passion of lust|et non in passione desiderii]].

paras.t: Tunc ergo Moab incendit ossa regis Idumææ usque ad cinerem, dum perversus aliquis hominis virtuosi spiritualia ossa, id est virtutes, in nihilum redigit, inducendo eum ad culpam mortalem. De talibus Dominus ait ad Ezechielem: Subversores sunt tecum. Et Paulus in Actibus: Ex vobis ipsis exsurgent lupi rapaces, non parcentes gregi. Et Christus in Evangelio: Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces; et rursus, Omnes quotquot venerunt, fures fuerunt et latrones. Isti mortificant animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificant animas quæ non vivunt, dum impios laudant, et justos condemnant.
paras.en: Moab, then, [[2:1|hath burnt the bones of the king of Edom even to ashes|incendit ossa regis Idumææ usque ad cinerem]] when some perverse man brings to nothing the spiritual bones, that is, the virtues, of a virtuous man, by leading him into mortal sin. Of such the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 2:6|destroyers|Subversores]] are with thee. And Paul in the Acts: Out of your own selves shall arise [[Acts 20:29|ravening wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock|Ex vobis ipsis exsurgent lupi rapaces, non parcentes gregi]] [the words "out of your own selves shall arise" are from the next verse, Acts 20:30, which Denis joins to v. 29]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]]; and again, [[John 10:8|All others, as many as have come, are thieves and robbers|Omnes quotquot venerunt, fures fuerunt et latrones]]. These [[Ezech 13:19|kill souls which should not die|mortificant animas quæ non moriuntur]], and [[Ezech 13:19|save souls alive which should not live|vivificant animas quæ non vivunt]], when they praise the wicked and condemn the just.

paras.t: Et mittam ignem æternæ damnationis in Moab, id est in hujusmodi subversores, de quibus verificatur illud Isaiæ ac Jeremiæ: Audivimus superbiam Moab; superbus est valde. Quid enim superbius, quam alios ad illa inducere quæ Deus prohibuit?
paras.en: [[2:2|And I will send a fire|Et mittam ignem]] of eternal damnation [[2:2|into Moab|in Moab]], that is, into such destroyers, in whom is verified that saying of Isaias and of Jeremias: [[Is 16:6|We have heard of the pride of Moab, he is exceeding proud|Audivimus superbiam Moab; superbus est valde]][[Jer 48:29||]]. For what is prouder than to lead others into the things God has forbidden?

paras.t: Et devorabit ædes Carioth, id est corpora congregationum hujuscemodi plebis, juxta illud Judith: Deus omnipotens vindicabit in eis, in die judicii visitabit eos; dabit ignem et vermes in carnem ipsorum, ut urantur ac sentiant usque in sempiternum. Et in Psalmo: Cadent super eos carbones; in ignem dejicies eos. Carioth autem interpretatum est civitas, per quam collectio hominum designatur. Corpora vero nostra, sunt animarum nostrarum ædes seu habitacula. Unde et Petrus: Scio, inquit, quia velox est depositio tabernaculi mei.
paras.en: And [[2:2|it shall devour the houses of Carioth|devorabit ædes Carioth]], that is, the bodies of the gatherings of such a people, according to that saying of Judith: [[Jdt 16:20|the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, in the day of judgment he will visit them|Deus omnipotens vindicabit in eis, in die judicii visitabit eos]]; [[Jdt 16:21|he will give fire, and worms into their flesh, that they may burn, and may feel for ever|dabit ignem et vermes in carnem ipsorum, ut urantur ac sentiant usque in sempiternum]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 139:11|Burning coals shall fall upon them; thou wilt cast them down into the fire|Cadent super eos carbones; in ignem dejicies eos]]. Now Carioth is interpreted *city*, by which a gathering of men is signified. And our bodies are the houses or dwellings of our souls. Hence Peter also: [[2 Pet 1:14|Being assured|Scio]], he says, [[2 Pet 1:14|that the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand|quia velox est depositio tabernaculi mei]].

paras.t: Et morietur morte æternæ reprobationis Moab iste seu populus tam malus et fallax, in sonitu et clangore tubæ, id est in sententia verborum Christi dicentis, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum; et in tuba de qua dicit Apostolus, Canet tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti; itemque, Quoniam ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo. Hæc enim tuba erit reprobis morte amarior, quamvis per eam suscitentur ad vitam, et vitam infeliciorem, secundum quod ait Salvator: Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filii Dei.
paras.en: And this Moab, that is, a people so wicked and deceitful, [[2:2|shall die|Et morietur]] the death of eternal reprobation [[2:2|with a noise, with the sound of the trumpet|in sonitu et clangore tubæ]]: that is, at the sentence of the words of Christ, who says, [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]; and at the trumpet of which the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 15:52|the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall rise again incorruptible|Canet tuba, et mortui resurgent incorrupti]]; and again, [[1 Thess 4:15|For the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment and with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God|Quoniam ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce archangeli et in tuba Dei]] [the margin gives 1 Thess. iv, 16, the verse's number in the Vulgate]. For this trumpet will be more bitter than death to the reprobate, though by it they are raised to life, and to a more unhappy life, according to the Saviour's words: [[John 5:28|the hour cometh wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God|Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filii Dei]].

paras.t: Et disperdam judicem de medio ejus, id est, superiores et principes talium condemnabo: quatenus judicium gravissimum fiat in his qui præsunt, et potentes potenter patiantur tormenta.
paras.en: [[2:3|And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof|Et disperdam judicem de medio ejus]], that is, I will condemn the superiors and princes of such men: so that [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|judicium gravissimum fiat in his qui præsunt]], and [[Wis 6:7|the mighty shall be mightily tormented|potentes potenter patiantur tormenta]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Juda, et super quatuor non convertam eum, id est, Ecclesiæ Christianorum, propter sua scelera toties repetita, non parcam; eo quod abjecerunt legem Domini, et mandata ejus non custodierunt, id est, evangelicam legem et Christi mandata non impleverunt ingrati beneficiis Dei: quibus melius esset ignorasse viam veritatis, quam agnitam abjecisse. Deceperunt enim eos idola sua, videlicet aurum, argentum, venter, venus, ac ceteræ imagines delectabiles, resque deliciosæ ac formæ suaves, quas magis amant et attendunt quam Deum. De quibus in libro Sapientiæ legitur: Creaturæ factæ sunt in odium et in tentationem animæ hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium.
paras.en: [[2:4|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Juda, and for four I will not convert him|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Juda, et super quatuor non convertam eum]]: that is, I will not spare the Church of the Christians, for its crimes so often repeated; [[2:4|because he hath cast away the law of the Lord, and hath not kept his commandments|eo quod abjecerunt legem Domini, et mandata ejus non custodierunt]], that is, they have not fulfilled the Gospel law and the commandments of Christ, being ungrateful for the benefits of God: for whom it had been better not to have known the way of truth than, having known it, to cast it away[[2 Pet 2:21||]]. For [[2:4|their idols have caused them to err|Deceperunt enim eos idola sua]]: namely gold, silver, the belly, lust, and the other delightful images, and dainty things, and sweet forms, which they love and heed more than God. Of which we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 14:11|the creatures of God are turned to an abomination, and a temptation to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise|Creaturæ factæ sunt in odium et in tentationem animæ hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium]].

paras.t: Juda autem interpretatur confessio: per quem hic figurantur Christiani fide informi, qui ore, non moribus Domino confitentur. De quibus asseritur: Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me.
paras.en: Now Juda is interpreted *confession*: by him are figured here the Christians of unformed faith [that is, faith without charity, which assents to the truth but does not live by it], who confess the Lord with the mouth and not by their conduct[[Tit 1:16||]]. Of whom it is said: [[Matt 15:8|This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me|Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me]][[Is 29:13||]].

paras.t: Et mittam ignem infernalem in Juda, id est in prædictam ecclesiam malignorum, et devorabit ædes Jerusalem, id est corpora illorum Christianorum qui conformantur in vitiis illi Jerusalem super quam Dominus flevit; cui et dixit: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quæ occidis Prophetas. Sunt enim plurimi nomine Christiani, qui zelatores justitiæ jugiter persequuntur.
paras.en: [[2:5|And I will send a fire|Et mittam ignem]] of hell [[2:5|into Juda|in Juda]], that is, into the aforesaid church of the wicked, [[2:5|and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem|et devorabit ædes Jerusalem]], that is, the bodies of those Christians who are made like in their vices to that Jerusalem over which the Lord wept[[Luke 19:41||]]; to which he also said: [[Matt 23:37|Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets|Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quæ occidis Prophetas]]. For there are very many, Christians in name, who continually persecute those zealous for justice.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Israel, etc. Per hoc significatur finalis damnatio Christianorum qui quamvis cœlestia, æterna ac divina cognoscant per fidem et scientiam acquisitam; nihilominus rebus temporalibus, mundanis atque carnalibus hærent et immerguntur, non pensantes illud Apostoli: Quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram.
paras.en: [[2:6|Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Israel|Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Israel]], etc. By this is signified the final damnation of those Christians who, though they know heavenly, eternal and divine things by faith and by acquired knowledge, nonetheless cling to temporal, worldly and carnal things and are sunk in them, not weighing that saying of the Apostle: [[Col 3:2|Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth.|Quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram]].

paras.t: Isti vendunt pro argento justum, dum pro fulgore sæcularis eloquentiæ vel mundanæ sapientiæ ostendendo aut præmiando, tradunt aut fallunt rectos corde, et pauperem pro calceamentis, dum pauperes opprimunt, quatenus opera sua vitiosa ac mortua, quæ recte per calceamenta signantur, excusent atque justificent. Sunt enim multi astuti et vani, qui simplicium et bonorum laudabilem vitam corrodunt, ne comparatione illorum, ipsorum vita sordescat. Istud quoque accipi potest secundum sensum in præcedenti articulo positum, de his qui propter pecuniam et vile emolumentum, causam justorum subvertunt, et pauperes opprimunt. Quocontra Moyses et Samuel profitentur, se a populo non munera accepisse, nec quempiam afflixisse.
paras.en: These sell [[2:6|the just man for silver|pro argento justum]] when, for the glitter of worldly eloquence or worldly wisdom, to display it or to be rewarded for it, they betray or deceive the upright of heart; [[2:6|and the poor man for a pair of shoes|et pauperem pro calceamentis]], when they oppress the poor so as to excuse and justify their own vicious and dead works, which are rightly signified by shoes. For there are many crafty and vain men who gnaw at the praiseworthy life of the simple and the good, lest their own life look shabby by comparison with theirs. This can also be taken in the sense set down in the preceding article, of those who for money and some vile gain overthrow the cause of the just and oppress the poor. Against which Moses and Samuel declare that they had taken no gifts from the people, nor afflicted any man[[Num 16:15||]][[1 Kings 12:3||]].

paras.t: Et viam humilium declinant. Tales sunt superbi, qui quum sint magni in oculis suis, inferioribus sociari dedignantur. Quocontra ait Scriptura: Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus. Et Christus: Ego, ait, in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat. Porro qui veraciter sapiens est, humiles et abjectos, pauperes et simplices cordialiter veneratur, et sibi ipsi in proprio præfert corde: non ignorans quod pauperes et infirma atque abjecta mundi, et ea quæ non sunt, elegerit Deus; et item, quod Christus talibus se assimilaverit, juxta quod ait in Psalmo, Ego sum pauper et dolens. Filius ac pater ejus ierunt ad puellam. Utinam talis incestus non esset in Christianis.
paras.en: And they [[2:7|turn aside the way of the humble|viam humilium declinant]]. Such are the proud, who, being great in their own eyes, disdain to keep company with those beneath them. Against which the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things|Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus]]. And Christ: [[Luke 22:27|I|Ego]], he says, [[Luke 22:27|am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]. But he who is truly wise reveres from the heart the humble and the outcast, the poor and the simple, and in his own heart prefers them to himself: not unaware that God hath chosen the poor and the weak and contemptible things of the world, and the things that are not[[1 Cor 1:27||]][[1 Cor 1:28||]]; and also that Christ made himself like such men, as he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:30|I am poor and sorrowful|Ego sum pauper et dolens]]. And [[2:7|the son and his father have gone to the same young woman|Filius ac pater ejus ierunt ad puellam]]. Would that such incest were not found among Christians!

paras.t: Et super vestimentis pignoratis accubuerunt. Hoc agunt usurarii et prædatores. Et vinum damnatorum bibebant. Hoc utique faciunt, qui infirmioribus imponunt aliqua crimina, propter quæ extorquent ab eis denarios, aliter eos damnarent, aut læderent, sive occiderent; et pro pretio tali, optati vini voluptate fruuntur. De quibus verificatur illud in Deuteronomii cantico: Fel draconum vinum eorum, et venenum aspidum insanabile.
paras.en: [[2:8|And they sat down upon garments laid to pledge|Et super vestimentis pignoratis accubuerunt]]. This usurers and plunderers do. And they [[2:8|drank the wine of the condemned|Et vinum damnatorum bibebant]]. This is done by those who lay some crimes to the charge of weaker men, and for them extort money from them, or else they would condemn them, or harm them, or kill them; and with such a price they enjoy the pleasure of the wine they longed for. In them is verified that saying in the canticle of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:33|Their wine is the gall of dragons, and the venom of asps, which is incurable|Fel draconum vinum eorum, et venenum aspidum insanabile]].

paras.t: Hæc itaque mala operati sunt Christiani. Sed quid fecerit eis Christus, subjungit. Ego autem exterminavi Amorrhæum, id est diabolum, a facie eorum, id est ab oculis cordis, quos excæcavit diabolus antequam illuminarentur a Christo. Salvator namque fortem armatum vicit, ligavit, et vasa ejus diripuit. Propter quod ait in Joanne: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Amorrhæus interpretatur, amarus, vel loquens, aut famosus: per quod significatur diabolus, hostis noster acerbissimus, crudelissimus, et omnium nequitiarum amaritudine adimpletus, jugiter mala inspirans, et fallaciter loquens, famosus propter malitiæ magnitudinem.
paras.en: These evils, then, the Christians have done. But what Christ has done for them he adds next. [[2:9|Yet I cast out the Amorrhite|Ego autem exterminavi Amorrhæum]], that is, the devil, [[2:9|before their face|a facie eorum]], that is, from the eyes of the heart, which the devil had blinded before they were enlightened by Christ. For the Saviour overcame the strong man armed, bound him, and rifled his goods[[Luke 11:21||]][[Luke 11:22||]][[Matt 12:29||]]. Wherefore he says in John: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. Amorrhite is interpreted *bitter*, or *speaking*, or *notorious*: by which is signified the devil, our most bitter and most cruel enemy, filled with the bitterness of all wickedness, ever breathing evil into us and speaking deceitfully, notorious for the greatness of his malice.

paras.t: Cujus altitudo, cedrorum altitudo ejus: quia in naturalibus valde excellens est, quæ in ipso integra (secundum Dionysium) permanserunt; imo principe dæmonum nullus angelus in naturalibus donis sublimior est. Ad quod pertinere potest illud Ezechielis: Cedri non fuerunt altiores illo in paradiso Dei. Et fortis ipse quasi quercus. Non enim est potestas super terram, quæ comparatur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret, ut dicitur ad Job. Unde et Christus appellat eum fortem armatum. Non ergo simus securi, incircumspecti, aut intimorati, aut propriis viribus innitentes, sed misericordiæ Christi. Quomodo enim caro fragilis, homo mortalis, huic quercui prævaleret, a qua videtur, et quam videre non potest?
paras.en: [[2:9|whose height was like the height of cedars|Cujus altitudo, cedrorum altitudo ejus]]: because he is very excellent in his natural gifts, which (according to Dionysius) remained whole in him; indeed no angel is higher in natural gifts than the prince of the demons. To this may belong that saying of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 31:8|The cedars in the paradise of God were not higher than he|Cedri non fuerunt altiores illo in paradiso Dei]]. And [[2:9|who was strong as an oak|Et fortis ipse quasi quercus]]. For, as is said to Job, [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one|Non enim est potestas super terram, quæ comparatur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret]]. Hence Christ also calls him [[Luke 11:21|a strong man armed|fortem armatum]]. Let us not, then, be secure, heedless or fearless, or rely on our own strength, but on the mercy of Christ. For how should frail flesh, mortal man, prevail against this oak, by which he is seen and which he cannot see?

paras.t: Et contrivi fructum ejus desuper, et radices ejus subter, id est, opera ejus destruxi, rapui et converti, omnemque superbiam ejus devici. Unde in prima epistola Joannis legitur: In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli. Et Salvator: Ego, inquit, si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum. Christus ergo vicit diabolum. Et nos eum virtute Christi conterimus, dummodo virtus dominicæ passionis seu meritum et gratia Christi nobis communicetur, applicetur, seu infundatur ad hoc. Quod fit, si caritate et jugi oratione conjungimur Christo.
paras.en: And [[2:9|I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots beneath|contrivi fructum ejus desuper, et radices ejus subter]], that is, I destroyed his works, I snatched them away and converted them, and overcame all his pride. Hence we read in the first epistle of John: [[1 John 3:8|For this purpose the Son of God appeared, that he might destroy the works of the devil|In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli]]. And the Saviour: [[John 12:32|And I|Ego]], he says, [[John 12:32|if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. Christ, then, has overcome the devil. And we too crush him by the power of Christ, provided the power of the Lord's passion, or the merit and grace of Christ, is communicated, applied or poured into us for this. Which comes about if we are joined to Christ by charity and by unceasing prayer.

paras.t: Ego sum qui ascendere vos feci de terra Ægypti, id est, de sæculari conversatione per gratiam vos retraxi, et ad amorem cœlestium corda vestra erexi: quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam. Et eduxi vos in deserto sæculi hujus, de virtute in virtutem, quadraginta annis, qui secundum Hieronymum, sunt numerus pœnitentiæ et doloris, per quem tempus pœnitendi signatur.
paras.en: [[2:10|It is I that brought you up out of the land of Egypt|Ego sum qui ascendere vos feci de terra Ægypti]], that is, by grace I drew you back from worldly ways of life, and lifted up your hearts to the love of heavenly things: as the Apostle says of Christ, [[Gal 1:4|that he might deliver us from this present wicked world|Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam]]. And [[2:10|I led you|Et eduxi vos]] [[2:10|through the wilderness|in deserto]] of this world, [[Ps 83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]], [[2:10|forty years|quadraginta annis]]: which, according to Jerome, are the number of penance and sorrow, by which the time for doing penance is signified.

paras.t: Et suscitavi de filiis vestris in Prophetas. Multis enim Christianis contulit Christus gratiam prophetiæ. Et de juvenibus vestris Nazaræos, id est sanctificatos, quales præcipue sunt, qui ab adolescentia jugum Dei super se portant, atque in innocentia permanentes, renuntiant sæculo, ingredientesque claustra, Deo in omni sobrietate ac puritate ministrant: quales fuerunt S. Bernardus, B. Thomas, et alii multi, qui creduntur nunquam peccasse mortaliter. Numquid non ita est, filii Israel? id est, nonne beneficia ista præstiti vobis, o Christiani?
paras.en: [[2:11|And I raised up of your sons for prophets|Et suscitavi de filiis vestris in Prophetas]]. For Christ has granted the grace of prophecy to many Christians. And [[2:11|of your young men for Nazarites|Et de juvenibus vestris Nazaræos]], that is, men made holy: such as are above all those who bear the yoke of God upon them from their youth[[Lam 3:27||]][[Matt 11:29||]], and, remaining in innocence, renounce the world, and entering the cloister, serve God in all sobriety and purity: such were St. Bernard, Bl. Thomas and many others, who are believed never to have sinned mortally. [[2:11|Is it not so, O ye children of Israel|Numquid non ita est, filii Israel]]? that is, have I not shown you these benefits, O Christians?

paras.t: Et propinabatis Nazaræis vinum. Hoc agunt, qui prædictos carnali pietate aut venenata pravitate conantur ab abstinentiæ et sobrietatis rigore avertere, ut mollius vivant. Et Prophetis mandabatis dicentes: Ne prophetetis. Hoc faciunt, qui a prædicatoribus et doctoribus verbum Dei audire, et increpari non volunt: qui dicunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus.
paras.en: [[2:12|And you will present wine to the Nazarites|Et propinabatis Nazaræis vinum]]. This is done by those who, out of a fleshly kindness or a poisonous wickedness, try to turn the men just named away from the rigour of abstinence and sobriety, so that they may live more softly. And [[2:12|command the prophets, saying: Prophesy not|Et Prophetis mandabatis dicentes: Ne prophetetis]]. This is done by those who will not hear the word of God from preachers and doctors, nor be rebuked: who say to God, [[Job 21:14|Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways|Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus]].

paras.t: Ecce ego stridebo super vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno: id est, terribiliter increpabo et judicabo; et sicut parturiens loquar, dissipabo, et absorbebo simul.
paras.en: [[2:13|Behold, I will screak under you as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay|Ecce ego stridebo super vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno]] [Denis reads *super vos*, "over you"; the Vulgate has *subter vos*, "under you"]: that is, I will rebuke and judge terribly; and [[Is 42:14|I will speak now as a woman in labour: I will destroy, and swallow up at once|sicut parturiens loquar, dissipabo, et absorbebo simul]].

paras.t: Et peribit fuga a veloce, et fortis non obtinebit virtutem suam, et robustus non salvabit animam suam: id est, nullus judicium meum subterfugere poterit; nec sua virtute, velocitate, aut sapientia poterit quis salvari. Non enim in tibiis viri beneplacitum erit Deo; et, Non salvatur rex per multam virtutem; et, Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua. Propterea apud Jeremiam contestatus est Dominus: Non glorietur sapiens in sapientia sua, et non glorietur fortis in fortitudine sua, et non glorietur dives in divitiis suis; sed in hoc glorietur qui gloriatur, scire et nosse me.
paras.en: [[2:14|And flight shall perish from the swift, and the valiant shall not possess his strength, neither shall the strong save his life|Et peribit fuga a veloce, et fortis non obtinebit virtutem suam, et robustus non salvabit animam suam]]: that is, no one will be able to escape my judgment; nor will anyone be able to be saved by his own strength, swiftness or wisdom. For God will not [[Ps 146:10|take pleasure in the legs of a man|in tibiis viri beneplacitum erit Deo]]; and, [[Ps 32:16|The king is not saved by a great army|Non salvatur rex per multam virtutem]]; and, [[Jer 10:14|Every man is become a fool for knowledge|Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua]]. Therefore the Lord solemnly declared in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:23|Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches|Non glorietur sapiens in sapientia sua, et non glorietur fortis in fortitudine sua, et non glorietur dives in divitiis suis]]; [[Jer 9:24|But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me|sed in hoc glorietur qui gloriatur, scire et nosse me]].

paras.t: Et tenens arcum non stabit, id est, dolosus et insidiator peribit: quoniam simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei, qui apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum.
paras.en: [[2:15|And he that holdeth the bow shall not stand|Et tenens arcum non stabit]], that is, the deceitful man and the one who lies in wait shall perish: because, as it is written, [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei]], [[Job 5:13|Who catcheth the wise in their craftiness|qui apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum]].

3.title: Expositio litteralis capituli tertii: Audite verbum quod locutus est Dominus.
3.title_en: Literal exposition of the third chapter: Hear the word that the Lord hath spoken.

paras.t: Excitat sanctus Propheta in hujus capituli exordio auditores ad considerationem sollicitam. Non enim superficiali, intimorato, vagoque animo audienda sunt verba Dei sublimis, sed cum reverentia, metu et caritate. Audite verbum quod locutus est Dominus ad me super vos, id est de vobis, filii Israel. Et ne per filios Israel intelligerent decem tribus dumtaxat, subjunctum est: super omnem cognationem quam eduxi de terra Ægypti, id est super duodecim tribus. Mutatur autem persona loquentis, quum dicitur, Eduxi, quum ante de Domino fit sermo in tertia persona. Dicens:
paras.en: At the opening of this chapter the holy Prophet rouses his hearers to careful attention. For the words of the most high God are not to be heard with a shallow, fearless and wandering mind, but with reverence, fear and charity. [[3:1|Hear the word that the Lord hath spoken|Audite verbum quod locutus est Dominus]] to me [[3:1|concerning you|super vos]], that is, about you, [[3:1|O ye children of Israel|filii Israel]]. And lest by the children of Israel they should understand the ten tribes only, there is added: [[3:1|concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt|super omnem cognationem quam eduxi de terra Ægypti]], that is, concerning the twelve tribes. Now the person of the speaker changes when it says, [[3:1|I brought up|Eduxi]], since before this the Lord was spoken of in the third person. [[3:1|saying|Dicens]]:

paras.t: Tantummodo vos cognovi, id est, vos solos cognovi notitia approbationis, vosque in populum peculiarem elegi, et magna ac specialia beneficia præstiti, ex omnibus cognationibus terræ, id est præ ceteris gentibus, quemadmodum fertur in Psalmo: Non fecit taliter omni nationi; et in Deuteronomio: Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram, etc., quia dilexit vos Dominus. Unde et secundo libro Regum fassus est David: Quæ est gens ut populus tuus Israel in terra, propter quam ivit Deus, ut redimeret eam sibi in populum? Et firmasti populum tuum Israel in populum sempiternum. Verumtamen non puto præinducta verba Amos sic intelligenda, quasi tempore Israeliticæ plebis et veteris Testamenti, vel quando in deserto pergebant, non fuerint in toto mundo aliqui homines boni et prædestinati, Deoque cogniti modo præfato, nisi populus Israel, quum juxta Dionysium, multi gentilium ad Deum reducti sint ministerio angelorum. Sed ideo dicta sunt hæc, quoniam Deus non elegit tunc aliquam nationem seu integram plebem, nisi filios Israel. Decuit enim populum illum, de quo voluit Deus incarnari, speciali gratia decorari. Porro per nationem seu integram plebem, intelligo populum patriæ cujuslibet universum. Sic enim Moyses loquitur in Deuteronomio, dicens quod filii Israel erant omnibus populis pauciores.
paras.en: [[3:2|You only have I known|Tantummodo vos cognovi]], that is, you alone have I known with the knowledge of approval [that is, the knowledge by which God knows those He approves and chooses as His own, not mere awareness], and you I have chosen for a peculiar people, and on you I have bestowed great and special benefits, [[3:2|of all the families of the earth|ex omnibus cognationibus terræ]], that is, above the other nations; as is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 147:9|He hath not done in like manner to every nation|Non fecit taliter omni nationi]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 20, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 147:9]; and in Deuteronomy: The Lord [[Deut 7:6|hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]], etc., [[Deut 7:8|because the Lord hath loved you|quia dilexit vos Dominus]]. Hence David also confessed in the second book of Kings: [[2 Kings 7:23|what nation is there upon earth, as thy people Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself|Quæ est gens ut populus tuus Israel in terra, propter quam ivit Deus, ut redimeret eam sibi in populum?]]? And [[2 Kings 7:24|thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be an everlasting people|firmasti populum tuum Israel in populum sempiternum]]. Yet I do not think the words of Amos quoted above are to be understood as though, in the time of the Israelite people and of the Old Testament, or when they were journeying in the desert, there were in the whole world no good and predestined men, known to God in the way just described, except the people of Israel; for according to Dionysius many of the gentiles were brought back to God by the ministry of the angels. But these things were said because God did not then choose any nation or whole people except the children of Israel. For it was fitting that the people of which God willed to become incarnate should be adorned with a special grace. By a nation or whole people, moreover, I understand the entire people of any country. For so Moses speaks in Deuteronomy, saying that the children of Israel were fewer than all peoples[[Deut 7:7||]].

paras.t: Idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras. Loquitur Propheta de toto populo Israel, id est de præteritis et tempore suo præsentibus, quasi de eisdem numero. Sed ad diversos necesse est verba ejus referri, quoniam sensus est: Quia vos præ ceteris cognovi, elegi, et beneficiis decoravi, ideo propter ingratitudinem vestram gravius vos affligam, et omnia peccata vestra ulciscar, tradendo vos Assyriis atque Chaldæis. Cui enim plus datum est, plus requiretur ab eo. Servus quoque sciens voluntatem domini sui, et non faciens, plagis vapulabit multis, teste Christo in Evangelio. Certum est autem, quod Dominus non tantum cognovit hoc modo eos quibus locutus est Amos. Et illos quos Deus tam specialiter elegit ac novit, non tam graviter castigavit, nec hostibus tradidit. Quæritur ergo, quomodo de istis injustis Dominus dixerit, Visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras: quum supra in Osee locutus sit, Non visitabo super filias vestras, quum fuerint fornicatæ. Et per Ezechielem de populo isto testatur: Zelus meus recessit a te, non irascar tibi amplius.
paras.en: [[3:2|therefore will I visit upon you all your iniquities|Idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras]]. The Prophet speaks of the whole people of Israel, that is, of those gone before and of those living in his own time, as though they were one and the same in number. But his words must be referred to different persons, for the sense is: Because I have known, chosen and adorned you with benefits above the rest, therefore for your ingratitude I will afflict you more heavily, and avenge all your sins, by delivering you to the Assyrians and the Chaldeans. For [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|Cui enim plus datum est, plus requiretur ab eo]]. [[Luke 12:47|that servant, who knew the will of his lord|Servus quoque sciens voluntatem domini sui]], and doing it not, [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]], as Christ witnesses in the Gospel. Now it is certain that the Lord did not know in this way only those to whom Amos spoke; and those whom God so specially chose and knew He did not chastise so heavily, nor deliver to their enemies. The question is therefore asked how the Lord said of these unjust men, [[3:2|will I visit upon you all your iniquities|visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras]]: since above, in Osee, He said, [[Osee 4:14|I will not visit upon your daughters, when they shall commit fornication|Non visitabo super filias vestras, quum fuerint fornicatæ]]; and through Ezechiel He testifies of this people: [[Ezech 16:42|my jealousy shall depart from thee|Zelus meus recessit a te]], [[Ezech 16:42|be angry no more|non irascar tibi amplius]].

paras.t: Et respondendum, quod visitatio Dei est duplex, videlicet consolationis et punitionis. Visitatio autem punitionis est duplex, videlicet paternæ correctionis (de qua legitur: Quem diligit Dominus, corripit; flagellat autem omnem filium quem recipit), et judicialis damnationis atque pœnalis derelictionis, quæ frequenter incipit in præsenti, et perpetuatur in futuro. Et de ista potest intelligi quod ait nunc Dominus, Visitabo super vos. Multos namque filiorum Israel, maxime decem tribuum, tradidit hostibus, et nihilo minus reliquit eos in idololatria ceterisque indurari peccatis, sicque æternaliter eos damnavit. In Ezechiele vero et Osee loquitur Dominus de visitatione primo modo accepta. De talibus enim reprobis, qui non visitantur a Deo per virgam paternam, ipse ait in Psalmo: Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum. — Verumtamen verba Dei hic posita, possunt accipi de visitatione paternæ correptionis in præsenti, ut sit sensus: Quia vos præ ceteris cognovi, dilexi, elegi; ideo non parcam vobis in præsenti, sed omnia vitia vestra nunc vindicabo, ut cessetis a malo. Ego enim quos amo, arguo et castigo. Nam ad hoc tradidit eos Dominus hostibus, ut qui per divina beneficia non corrigebantur, per humanæ crudelitatis tormenta emendarentur. Hinc secundo Machabæorum libro habetur: Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoris ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium. Rursusque: Non sicut in aliis nationibus, patienter Dominus exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies venerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat; ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet. Propter quod nunquam quidem a nobis misericordiam suam amovet; corripiens vero, in adversis populum suum non derelinquit.
paras.en: The answer is that God's visitation is twofold, namely of consolation and of punishment. And the visitation of punishment is twofold: that of fatherly correction (of which we read: [[Prov 3:12|whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth|Quem diligit Dominus, corripit]]; [[Heb 12:6|he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth|flagellat autem omnem filium quem recipit]]), and that of judicial condemnation and penal abandonment [that is, God's leaving the obstinate sinner to himself as a punishment], which often begins in the present and is made everlasting in the future. And it is of this latter that what the Lord now says can be understood, [[3:2|will I visit upon you|Visitabo super vos]]. For many of the children of Israel, above all of the ten tribes, He delivered to their enemies, and nevertheless left them to harden in idolatry and their other sins, and so condemned them eternally. But in Ezechiel and Osee the Lord speaks of visitation taken in the first way. For of such reprobates, who are not visited by God with the fatherly rod, He Himself says in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:13|I let them go according to the desires of their heart|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum]]. — Yet the words of God set down here can also be taken of the visitation of fatherly correction in the present, so that the sense is: Because I have known, loved and chosen you above the rest, therefore I will not spare you in the present, but will now punish all your vices, that you may cease from evil. For [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love, I rebuke and chastise|Ego enim quos amo, arguo et castigo]]. For to this end the Lord delivered them to their enemies, that those who were not corrected by the divine benefits might be amended by the torments of human cruelty. Hence in the second book of Machabees we have: [[2 Mach 6:13|For it is a token of great goodness, when sinners are not suffered to go on in their ways for a long time, but are presently punished|Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoris ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium]]. And again: [[2 Mach 6:14|not as with other nations|Non sicut in aliis nationibus]], [[2 Mach 6:14|whom the Lord patiently expecteth, that when the day of judgment shall come, he may punish them in the fulness of their sins|patienter Dominus exspectat, ut eas, quum judicii dies venerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat]]; [[2 Mach 6:15|Doth he also deal with us, so as to suffer our sins to come to their height, and then take vengeance on us|ita et in nobis statuit, ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, ita demum in nos vindicet]]. [[2 Mach 6:16|And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us: but though he chastise his people with adversity he forsaketh them not|Propter quod nunquam quidem a nobis misericordiam suam amovet; corripiens vero, in adversis populum suum non derelinquit]].

paras.t: Consequenter inducit Amos sex exempla, ad ostendendum quod ultio populi a Deo illata, et per Prophetas annuntiata, sit justa: quatenus sicut exempla illa non fiunt, nisi certa causa exstiterit, ita non erit tribulatio, nisi per divinam justitiam rationabiliter inducatur seu dispensetur.
paras.en: Next Amos brings in six examples, to show that the punishment of the people, brought by God and announced through the Prophets, is just: so that, as the things in those examples do not happen unless there is a definite cause, so there will be no tribulation unless it is brought on or dispensed with good reason by the divine justice.

paras.t: Primum exemplum est: Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis, id est, nisi ex consensu vel rationabili causa, aut ex amicitia? quasi dicat, Non. Hoc communiter verum est; interdum tamen contingit, quod alius cogat alium ad proficiscendum secum. Sed Propheta loquitur secundum communem cursum. Per hanc autem convenientiam duorum simul euntium, mystice designatur concordia Dei et Prophetæ ex Dei ore loquentis.
paras.en: The first example is: [[3:3|Shall two walk together except they be agreed|Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis]], that is, unless by consent, or for some reasonable cause, or out of friendship? As if to say: No. This is commonly true; though sometimes it happens that one man compels another to travel with him. But the Prophet speaks according to the common course of things. Now by this agreement of two going together is mystically signified the concord of God and of the Prophet who speaks from the mouth of God.

paras.t: Secundum exemplum est: Numquid rugiet leo in saltu, id est inter arbores silvestres, nisi habuerit prædam, id est, nisi quum viderit aut adeptus fuerit animal quo vescatur? Quum enim patitur famem, mox ut viderit bestiam, dat rugitum: quo audito, territa bestia figit gradum, et capitur. Mystice, per rugitum leonis potest intelligi comminatio Christi (qui est leo de tribu Juda) per Prophetam: ad quam comminationem sequitur impiorum punitio, quemadmodum ad rugitum leonis prædæ voratio. Quidam tamen per leonem intelligunt dæmonem, qui tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret, semperque sitit animarum damnationem, et rugit ut eas deglutiat. — Tertium exemplum est, et redit in idem cum secundo: Numquid dabit catulus leonis vocem de cubili suo, id est de antro quo latitat, nisi aliquid apprehenderit, id est, nisi prædam cernat aut ceperit? quasi dicat, Non. Catulus iste potest intelligi vel Christus Filius Dei Patris, vel potestas adversa, sicut de leone jam dictum est.
paras.en: The second example is: [[3:4|Will a lion roar in the forest|Numquid rugiet leo in saltu]], that is, among the trees of the wood, [[3:4|if he have no prey|nisi habuerit prædam]], that is, unless he has seen or caught an animal to feed on? For when he suffers hunger, as soon as he sees a beast he gives a roar; and on hearing it the terrified beast stands rooted to the spot and is taken. Mystically, by the lion's roar can be understood the threatening of Christ (who is [[Apoc 5:5|the lion of the tribe of Juda|leo de tribu Juda]]) through the Prophet: upon which threatening follows the punishment of the wicked, as the devouring of the prey follows upon the lion's roar. Some, however, understand by the lion the devil, who [[1 Pet 5:8|as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|tanquam leo rugiens circuit quærens quem devoret]], and ever thirsts for the damnation of souls, and roars to swallow them up. — The third example comes back to the same thing as the second: [[3:4|will the lion's whelp cry out of his den|Numquid dabit catulus leonis vocem de cubili suo]], that is, from the cave in which he lies hid, [[3:4|if he have taken nothing|nisi aliquid apprehenderit]], that is, unless he sees or has caught prey? As if to say: No. This whelp can be understood either as Christ, the Son of God the Father, or as the adverse power, as was just said of the lion.

paras.t: Quartum exemplum est: Numquid cadet avis in laqueum terræ, id est in rete super terram expansum, absque aucupe, id est sine artificio aucupis, qui fallit capitque volucres? Quidam aucupem accipiunt dæmonem, qui habentes alas virtutum et contemplationis interdum illaqueat, fallit, et ad peccati inducit ruinam. Alii autem per aucupem intelligunt Deum, qui impios comprehendit in laqueo pœnæ, juxta illud in Psalmo: Pluit super peccatores laqueos. Aliquando autem homines cadunt in laqueum culpæ propria inclinatione aut pravitate. Nam ut Origenes testatur, quamvis non essent diaboli, adhuc homines concupiscentiis pulsarentur. Dæmones tamen frequenter se miscent. — Quintum exemplum est: Numquid auferetur laqueus de terra, antequam quid ceperit? id est, rete ad capiendum aves expansum, non tollitur nisi aliquid comprehendat. Hoc communiter ita est. Per quod designatur, quod Deus non frustra aliquid inchoat, nec laqueos tormentorum impiis præparatos aufert, sed in eos projicit impœnitentes. Dæmon quoque non tollit laqueos tentationum, nisi ceperit aut vicerit aliquem.
paras.en: The fourth example is: [[3:5|Will the bird fall into the snare upon the earth|Numquid cadet avis in laqueum terræ]], that is, into a net spread out upon the ground, [[3:5|if there be no fowler|absque aucupe]], that is, without the craft of the fowler, who deceives and takes the birds? Some take the fowler to be the devil, who sometimes ensnares those that have the wings of the virtues and of contemplation, deceives them, and brings them down to the ruin of sin. Others understand by the fowler God, who catches the wicked in the snare of punishment, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 10:7|He shall rain snares upon sinners|Pluit super peccatores laqueos]]. Sometimes, however, men fall into the snare of guilt by their own inclination or depravity. For, as Origen testifies, even if there were no devils, men would still be assailed by concupiscences; yet the demons frequently mingle themselves in. — The fifth example is: [[3:5|Shall the snare be taken up from the earth, before it hath taken somewhat?|Numquid auferetur laqueus de terra, antequam quid ceperit?]] That is, a net spread out for catching birds is not taken up unless it catches something. This is commonly so. By which is signified that God does not begin anything in vain, nor does He take away the snares of torment prepared for the wicked, but casts the impenitent into them. The demon, too, does not take away the snares of temptation unless he has caught or overcome someone.

paras.t: Sextum exemplum est: Si clanget tuba in civitate, et populus non expavescet? id est, tuba non clanget in urbibus, adversariorum adventum insinuans, quin cives trepidabunt. Per quod designatur, quod in domo Ecclesiæ constituti, terreri debent audita voce sacræ Scripturæ, vel denuntiationis propheticæ, quæ significatur per tubam.
paras.en: The sixth example is: [[3:6|Shall the trumpet sound in a city, and the people not be afraid?|Si clanget tuba in civitate, et populus non expavescet?]] That is, the trumpet will not sound in cities, announcing the approach of enemies, without the citizens trembling. By which is signified that those set in the house of the Church ought to be struck with fear on hearing the voice of holy Scripture, or of the prophetic warning, which is signified by the trumpet.

paras.t: Hæc omnia introducta sunt ad significandum quam rationabile sit quod infertur: Si erit malum in civitate, id est, malum pœnæ seu justa punitio non erit in populo, quod Dominus non fecit, id est, non induxit, seu fieri ordinaverit aut permiserit in culpæ vindictam, aut aliam rationabilem causam, quatenus inordinatio culpæ ordinetur per inflictionem pœnæ? Quod fit, dum peccator qui propriam voluntatem contra Dei justitiam secutus est, cogitur per justitiam Dei sustinere quæ propria abhorret voluntas. De hoc malo pœnæ Dominus ait apud Isaiam: Ego Dominus, formans lucem, et creans tenebras, faciens pacem et creans malum; et Christus in Evangelio, Sufficit diei malitia sua. Est autem triplex malum, videlicet malum naturæ, ut monstruositas, malum culpæ, et malum pœnæ. Quibus aliqui addunt quartum malum, scilicet malum fortunæ, quod tamen ad malum pœnæ reducitur.
paras.en: All these things were brought in to show how reasonable is the conclusion drawn: [[3:6|Shall there be evil in a city|Si erit malum in civitate]], that is, there will be no evil of punishment, or just chastisement, among the people, [[3:6|which the Lord hath not done|quod Dominus non fecit]], that is, has not brought on, or ordained to be done, or permitted, in vengeance for guilt or for some other reasonable cause, so that the disorder of guilt may be set in order by the infliction of punishment. This happens when the sinner who has followed his own will against God's justice is compelled by God's justice to endure what his own will abhors. Of this evil of punishment the Lord says in Isaias: I the Lord, [[Is 45:7|I form the light, and create darkness, I make peace, and create evil|formans lucem, et creans tenebras, faciens pacem et creans malum]] [the passage has no margin reference]; and Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 6:34|Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof|Sufficit diei malitia sua]] [Latin *malitia*, here the same word-family as *malum*, "evil"]. Now evil is threefold, namely the evil of nature, such as monstrosity, the evil of guilt, and the evil of punishment. To these some add a fourth, namely the evil of fortune, which however is reduced to the evil of punishment.

paras.t: Quia non faciet Dominus verbum, id est factum notabile, necessarium vel utile sciri hominibus. Verbum autem frequenter pro re significata per verbum accipitur, quemadmodum Ezechias ait: Non fuit verbum in domo mea, quod non ostenderim eis. Quandoque vero accipitur pro interiori verbo seu conceptu mentali; aliquando autem pro verbo vocali. Nisi revelaverit secretum suum, id est factum tale, communi plebi incognitum, et naturaliter impræcognoscibile, qualia sunt futura contingentia, ad servos suos Prophetas: qui sunt amici Dei, ideo secreta sua revelat eis, tanquam familiaribus et amicis. Secundum Hieronymum, istud non est intelligendum de omnibus quæ Deus facit in cœlo, vel ante jam fecit, sed quæ in terra facturus est. Et puto quod maxime intelligatur de his quæ bonum communitatis concernunt. Sic enim mysteria Christi et Ecclesiæ, gestaque novi Testamenti prænuntiavit Patribus veteris Testamenti. Processum quoque et statum militantis Ecclesiæ prænuntiavit Apostolis, præsertim Joanni in Apocalypsi. Tempore quoque legis naturæ revelavit Noe futurum diluvium, Abrahæ et Lot subversionem Sodomæ. Jacob quoque in Genesi filiis suis ait: Congregamini, ut quæ ventura sunt in novissimis diebus, annuntiem vobis. Verum non singula singulis revelavit Prophetis, sed aliquibus plura, aliis pauciora. Divisiones enim gratiarum sunt, idem autem Spiritus, secundum Apostolum. Porro in his patet clementia et providentia Dei. Ideo enim futura supplicia primo Prophetis, deinde per eos prænuntiat populo, ut emendetur, et ab imminentibus eripiatur tormentis. In quo ostenditur Deus habere providentiam actuum humanorum, et omnia remunerare.
paras.en: [[3:7|For the Lord God doth nothing|Quia non faciet Dominus verbum]] [literally "the Lord will not do a *word*"], that is, a notable deed, one necessary or useful for men to know. For *word* is often taken for the thing signified by the word, as Ezechias says: [[Is 39:4|there was not any thing|Non fuit verbum]] in my house [[Is 39:4|which I have not shewn them|quod non ostenderim eis]] [no margin reference; the words are closest to Is 39:4, where the Vulgate has *res*, "thing", for Denis's *verbum*; the same story is at 4 Kings 20:15]. Sometimes, however, it is taken for the inner word or mental concept, and sometimes for the spoken word. [[3:7|without revealing his secret|Nisi revelaverit secretum suum]], that is, such a deed as is unknown to the common people and cannot naturally be foreknown, such as future contingents [that is, future events that depend on free choice or chance and so are not fixed by their causes], [[3:7|to his servants the prophets|ad servos suos Prophetas]]: who are God's friends, and so He reveals His secrets to them as to His intimates and friends. According to Jerome, this is not to be understood of all that God does in heaven, or has already done before, but of what He is going to do on earth. And I think it is understood above all of the things that concern the common good. For thus He foretold to the Fathers of the Old Testament the mysteries of Christ and of the Church and the deeds of the New Testament; He also foretold to the Apostles the course and state of the Church militant, especially to John in the Apocalypse. In the time of the law of nature, too, He revealed to Noe the coming flood[[Gen 6:7||]], and to Abraham and Lot the overthrow of Sodom[[Gen 18:20||]][[Gen 19:13||]]. Jacob, too, says to his sons in Genesis: [[Gen 49:1|Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days|Congregamini, ut quæ ventura sunt in novissimis diebus, annuntiem vobis]]. Yet He did not reveal everything to every Prophet, but more to some, less to others. For [[1 Cor 12:4|there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit|Divisiones enim gratiarum sunt, idem autem Spiritus]], according to the Apostle. In these things, moreover, the clemency and providence of God are plain. For He foretells future punishments first to the Prophets, then through them to the people, so that it may amend and be delivered from the torments that threaten it. In which it is shown that God has providence over human acts, and repays all things.

paras.t: Leo rugiet, quis non timebit? Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetabit? id est, si ad rugitum leonis homines et jumenta concutiuntur timore, multo amplius Deo jubente Vatibus ut prophetent, dignum est ut obediant. Itaque, Dominus Deus locutus est, id est, Prophetis annuntiavit occulta, et jussit ut ea patefaciant populo: quis eorum quibus Deus taliter est locutus, non prophetabit? id est, justum omnino est ut prophetent. Secundum Glossam, Amos iste quoniam pastor fuit, solitus timere leonem, timorem omnipotentis Dei, leonis rugitui comparat.
paras.en: [[3:8|The lion shall roar, who will not fear|Leo rugiet, quis non timebit]]? [[3:8|The Lord God hath spoken, who shall not prophesy?|Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetabit?]] That is, if at the lion's roar men and beasts are shaken with fear, much more, when God commands the seers to prophesy, is it fitting that they obey. And so: *The Lord God hath spoken*, that is, He has announced hidden things to the Prophets and commanded them to make them known to the people: *who* of those to whom God has so spoken *shall not prophesy*? That is, it is altogether right that they prophesy. According to the Gloss, this Amos, since he was a shepherd[[Amos 1:1||]] accustomed to fear the lion, compares the fear of almighty God to the roar of a lion.

paras.t: Consequenter Deus volens universis judiciorum suorum contra Israel æquitatem ostendere, ait: Auditum facite, id est, manifestate, o Prophetæ, vel alii a Prophetis edocti, in ædibus Azoti, id est in domibus urbis Philistinorum sic dictæ, et in ædibus terræ Ægypti; et dicite: Congregamini, id est, convenite, o Azotii atque Ægyptii, super montes Samariæ. Potest per Samariam intelligi ipsa metropolis decem tribuum, vel tota provincia montibus plena.
