For, as Jeremias testifies, [[Jer 17:6|he shall be|Erit enim]] [[Jer 17:6|like tamaric in the desert|sicut myricæ in deserto]]. Hence Christ says in John: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras tanquam palmes, et arescet]]. And the penitent says: [[Ps 101:5|I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered|Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum]].

paras.t: Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates, id est illi super quos non plui, ad civitatem unam complutam, ut biberent aquam, id est, gratiæ et sapientiæ ejus participes fierent, verbumque Dei audirent, et non sunt satiatæ. Istud accipi potest de pœnitentibus, qui non satiantur, vel quia non tantam gratiam et perfectionem consequuntur ut cupiunt, vel quia nihil gratiæ gratum facientis et donorum Spiritus Sancti participant, eo quod non vere pœniteant, et timore aut necessitate magis quam amore et voluntate hæc faciunt. Interdum quoque pluit Deus super unum, et non super alium, per nubes de quibus loquitur Isaias, Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant? id est per prædicatores et viros divinos, qui verbo tonant, miraculis coruscant, pietate obumbrant, doctrina fecundant: quando videlicet aliquibus juste verbum Dei subtrahitur, quod aliis misericorditer annuntiatur, quemadmodum Dominus ait ad Ezechielem: Fili hominis, linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est. Faciamus ergo quod Christus ait discipulis: Rogate dominum messis, ut mittat operarios in messem suam.
paras.en: [[4:8|And two and three cities went|Et venerunt duæ et tres civitates]], that is, those upon whom I rained not, [[4:8|to one city|ad civitatem unam]] that was rained upon, [[4:8|to drink water|ut biberent aquam]], that is, to become partakers of its grace and wisdom and to hear the word of God, [[4:8|and were not filled|et non sunt satiatæ]]. This can be taken of penitents who are not filled, either because they do not obtain as much grace and perfection as they desire, or because they have no share in sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God] and the gifts of the Holy Ghost, since they do not truly repent, and do these things from fear or necessity rather than from love and good will. Sometimes too God rains upon one and not upon another through the clouds of which Isaias speaks, [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant]]? that is, through preachers and men of God, who thunder with the word, flash with miracles, overshadow with piety, make fruitful with doctrine: namely when the word of God is justly withdrawn from some which is mercifully proclaimed to others, as the Lord says to Ezechiel: Son of man, [[Ezech 3:26|I will make thy tongue stick fast to the roof of thy mouth, and thou shalt be dumb, and not as a man that reproveth: because they are a provoking house|linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est]]. Let us do, then, what Christ said to his disciples: [[Luke 10:2|Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest that he send labourers into his harvest|Rogate dominum messis, ut mittat operarios in messem suam]].

paras.t: Percussi vos permissive, o reprobi, in vento urente, id est ardore libidinis vel doctrina ventosa et corruptiva, et in aurigine, id est ira et invidia, quæ sanguinis ruborem variant in pallorem, et fructum seminis animæ, quod est verbum Dei, corrumpunt. Percussi multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum, id est cordium, in quibus flores virtutum, gramina contemplationum, et botri fructuum Spiritus Sancti merito pullularent. Horum enim corda percutiuntur, dum a Deo relinquuntur, arescunt, vitiisque subduntur. Oliveta vestra et ficeta, id est opera misericordiæ et suavitatis internæ vel habitus virtuosos, ex quibus procedunt hujusmodi actus, quemadmodum fructus prodeunt ex arboribus, comedit eruca, id est mordax ac pungitiva invidia, quæ omnia vastat, si admittatur: non enim compati aut auxiliari permittit.
paras.en: [[4:9|I struck you|Percussi vos]], by permission, O reprobate, [[4:9|with a burning wind|in vento urente]], that is, with the heat of lust or with windy and corrupting doctrine, [[4:9|and with mildew|et in aurigine]], that is, with anger and envy, which change the redness of the blood into pallor, and corrupt the fruit of the soul's seed, which is the word of God[[Luke 8:11||]]. I struck [[4:9|your many gardens, and your vineyards|multitudinem hortorum vestrorum et vinearum]], that is, your hearts, in which the flowers of the virtues, the grasses of contemplation, and the clusters of the fruits of the Holy Ghost should rightly have sprung up. For the hearts of these are struck when they are forsaken by God, wither, and are made subject to vices. [[4:9|your olive groves, and fig groves|Oliveta vestra et ficeta]], that is, the works of mercy and of inward sweetness, or the virtuous habits from which such acts proceed, as fruits come forth from trees, [[4:9|the palmerworm hath eaten up|comedit eruca]], that is, biting and stinging envy, which lays all waste if it is let in: for it does not allow one to pity or to help.

paras.t: Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti: id est, quum ambularetis in operibus carnis et sæculi, vita gratiæ vos privavi, vel corporaliter castigavi. Percussi in gladio juvenes vestros. Gladius spiritus est verbum Dei. Qui ergo in juventute ex auditu verborum Dei corrigitur, gladio salubriter verberatur. Usque ad captivitatem equorum, id est refrenationem lascivorum motuum corporis. Hæc quoque aliter accipi possunt, sed propter causam pertranseo.
paras.en: [[4:10|I sent death upon you in the way of Egypt|Misi in vos mortem in via Ægypti]]: that is, when you walked in the works of the flesh and of the world, I deprived you of the life of grace, or chastised you in body. [[4:10|I slew your young men with the sword|Percussi in gladio juvenes vestros]]. The [[Eph 6:17|sword of the Spirit|Gladius spiritus]] is [[Eph 6:17|the word of God|verbum Dei]]. He then who in youth is corrected by hearing the words of God is wholesomely smitten with the sword. [[4:10|even to the captivity of your horses|Usque ad captivitatem equorum]], that is, to the bridling of the wanton movements of the body. These things can also be taken otherwise, but for good reason I pass over it.

paras.t: Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham, id est, igne concupiscentiæ et sulfure fœtidissimæ voluptatis prorsus permisi vos perire, quantum ad spirituale esse gratiæ gratificantis, et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio, quantum ad hoc quod nondum pœnas tartarei ignis incidistis. Et non redistis ad me: in quo patet incorrigibilitas vestra. De talibus Dominus ait ad Jeremiam: Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?
paras.en: [[4:11|I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha|Subverti vos sicut subvertit Deus Sodomam et Gomorrham]], that is, I let you perish utterly by the fire of concupiscence and the brimstone of most foul pleasure, as regards the spiritual being of sanctifying grace, [[4:11|and you were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning|et facti estis quasi torris raptus de incendio]], inasmuch as you have not yet fallen into the pains of the fire of hell. [[4:11|yet you returned not to me|Et non redistis ad me]]: in which your incorrigibility is plain. Of such the Lord says to Jeremias: [[Jer 8:5|Why then is this people in Jerusalem turned away with a stubborn revolting?|Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?]]?

paras.t: Quia ecce formans montes, id est, angelos sanctos in sublimitate naturæ et gratiæ atque in beatifica fruitione constituens. Vel, montes, id est Apostolos et imitatores eorum in arce virtutum reponens, quorum conversatio est in cœlis; et sicut exaltantur cœli a terra, ita exaltatur nobilis angelica cœliformisque vita eorum, ab ignobili, confusa et injusta malorum Christianorum conversatione, de qualibus dicitur, Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur. Et creans ventum, id est eos qui velocissime cuncta terrena transcendunt.
paras.en: [[4:13|For behold he that formeth the mountains|Quia ecce formans montes]], that is, establishing the holy angels in the height of nature and of grace and in the beatific enjoyment. Or, the mountains, that is, the Apostles and their imitators, setting them in the citadel of the virtues, whose [[Phil 3:20|conversation is in heaven|conversatio est in cœlis]]; and [[Is 55:9|as the heavens are exalted above the earth|sicut exaltantur cœli a terra]], so is their noble, angelic and heavenly life exalted above the ignoble, disordered and unjust conversation of bad Christians, of whom it is said, [[Jer 17:13|they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]]. [[4:13|and createth the wind|Et creans ventum]], that is, those who most swiftly pass beyond all earthly things.

paras.t: Faciens matutinam nebulam, id est, symbolicarum revelationum obscuritate in primis mentem involvens, antequam ad anagogicæ contemplationis perveniat puritatem. Ita fit sæpe. Hæc ergo obscuritas, per nebulam quæ mane operit terram, significatur. Non enim possibile est aliter nobis lucere divinum radium, nisi variis sensibilium formarum velaminibus circumtectum. Et gradiens super excelsa terræ, id est, in mentibus contemplativis atque theoricis ambulans, cum quibus esse, sunt deliciæ meæ. Ecce tanta est conventio, communio atque concordia Dei cum servulis suis devotis atque humilibus. Cum exsistentibus est, cum stantibus stat, cum habitantibus habitat, cum gradientibus graditur, cum ascendentibus et descendentibus ascendit atque descendit. Hinc ait ad Jacob in Genesi: Ego descendam tecum in Ægyptum. Et Jacob loquens de ipso: Deus, inquit, qui socius fuit itineris mei. Dat enim suis virtutem ad omnia ista, eosque in cunctis gratiose deducit. Nec hoc solum, sed ipsi quoque sunt, manent, stant, ambulant, ascendunt atque descendunt in ipso, id est secundum voluntatem, et per gratiam ejus.
paras.en: [[4:13|he that maketh the morning mist|Faciens matutinam nebulam]], that is, first wrapping the mind in the obscurity of symbolic revelations before it comes to the purity of anagogical contemplation [that is, contemplation that rises to heavenly things]. So it often happens. This obscurity, then, is signified by the mist that covers the earth in the morning. For it is not possible for the divine ray to shine on us otherwise than veiled about with the various coverings of sensible forms. [[4:13|and walketh upon the high places of the earth|Et gradiens super excelsa terræ]], that is, walking in contemplative and speculative minds, with whom [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be|esse, sunt deliciæ meæ]]. See how great is the agreement, fellowship and concord of God with his devout and humble little servants. With those who exist he is, with those who stand he stands, with those who dwell he dwells, with those who walk he walks, with those who go up and go down he goes up and goes down. Hence he says to Jacob in Genesis: [[Gen 46:4|I will go down with thee|Ego descendam tecum]] into Egypt. And Jacob, speaking of him: God, he says, who [[Gen 35:3|accompained me in my journey|socius fuit itineris mei]]. For he gives his own the strength for all these things, and graciously leads them in all. And not only this, but they too are, remain, stand, walk, go up and go down in him, that is, according to his will, and through his grace.

5.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli quinti: Audite verbum istud, etc.
5.title_en: Literal explanation of the fifth chapter: Hear ye this word, etc.

paras.t: Hoc loco ostenditur irreparabilis decem tribuum vastitas. Audite, o decem tribus, verbum istud, quod ego Amos levo super vos, id est, ex magno affectu de vobis annuntio, planctum, id est planctuosum seu lamentabile: quia cum fletu et compassione vestram calamitatem prædico, vosque deplango, quemadmodum Samuel Saulem, et Christus civitatem Jerusalem. Nec mirum, si Amos Israelita Israelem deplangat, quum Isaias futuram miseriam seu captivitatem Babylonis et Moab tam dire defleverit, ut patet in libro ipsius. Qui etiam duas tribus deplorans: Nolite, inquit, incumbere ut consolemini me super vastitate filiæ populi mei.
paras.en: In this place the irreparable devastation of the ten tribes is shown. [[5:1|Hear ye|Audite]], O ten tribes, [[5:1|this word, which I|verbum istud, quod ego]], Amos, [[5:1|take up concerning you|levo super vos]], that is, which out of great affection I announce concerning you, [[5:1|for a lamentation|planctum]], that is, full of wailing or lamentable: for with weeping and compassion I foretell your calamity, and I bewail you, as Samuel bewailed Saul[[1 Kings 15:35||]], and Christ the city of Jerusalem[[Luke 19:41||]]. Nor is it any wonder if Amos, an Israelite, bewails Israel, since Isaias wept so grievously over the misery to come, or captivity, of Babylon[[Is 13:1||]][[Is 21:1||]] and of Moab[[Is 15:1||]][[Is 16:1||]], as is plain in his book [the margin gives Is. xiii, xxi; xv, xvi: whole chapters]. He too, bewailing the two tribes, says: [[Is 22:4|labour not|Nolite]], he says, [[Is 22:4|to comfort me, for the devastation of the daughter of my people|incumbere ut consolemini me super vastitate filiæ populi mei]].

paras.t: Deinde verba planctus ponuntur. Domus Israel, id est familia decem tribuum, cecidit per culpam et pœnam. Cecidit enim per idololatriam aliaque peccata a pristina gratia. Et per tribulationes, pressuras et captivitates sibi illatas, a præhabita corruit prosperitate, præsertim a tempore Hazaelis regis Syriæ, qui contrivit quasi in tritura areæ Israelem; et deinde ab Assyriis. Et non adjiciet ut resurgat per pœnitentiam a culpa ac idololatria, vel per victoriam seu reditum a captivitate Assyriaca ad prosperitatem priorem. Tamen in fine sæculi decem tribus convertentur.
paras.en: Next the words of the lament are set down. [[5:1|The house of Israel|Domus Israel]], that is, the family of the ten tribes, [[5:1|is fallen|cecidit]] by guilt and by punishment. For through idolatry and other sins it fell from its former grace. And through the tribulations, oppressions and captivities brought upon it, it fell from the prosperity it had had before, especially from the time of Hazael king of Syria, who crushed Israel as it were [[4 Kings 13:7|by threshing in the barnfloor|in tritura areæ]], and afterwards at the hands of the Assyrians. [[5:1|and it shall rise no more|Et non adjiciet ut resurgat]] [literally "it shall not add to rise again"], by penance from its guilt and idolatry, or by victory, or by a return from the Assyrian captivity to its former prosperity. Yet at the end of the world the ten tribes will be converted.

paras.t: Virgo Israel, id est, plebs Israelitica, quæ virgo vocatur: primo, quia in Patriarchis et Prophetis ac justis Deo exstitit desponsata, quamvis isti qui erant tempore Amos, animi integritatem ac puritatem perdiderint, multipliciterque fornicarentur a Deo; secundo, ad insinuandum puritatem naturæ secundum se consideratæ. Hinc et de populo Babylonis scriptum est in Isaia: Sede in pulvere, virgo filia Babylon. Et utroque modo ait Jeremias de populo Juda: Quoniam contritione magna contrita est virgo filia populi mei. Itaque, Virgo Israel projecta est in terram suam, id est, in proprio territorio ab hostibus victa et conculcata, vel ad peccata inducta; non est qui suscitet eam, id est, ad pristinum statum reducat, Deum precibus mitigando, vel hostes Assyrios debellando. Quamvis enim hic Amos et Prophetæ sibi contemporanei orarent pro populo isto, eumque instruerent, noluerunt tamen se ad gratiam habilitare, sed econtrario occiderunt Prophetas. De talibus Dominus, ostendens se inexorabilem, quantum ad aliquos, ait ad Jeremiam: Non assumas laudem et orationem pro eis. Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum.
paras.en: [[5:2|The virgin of Israel|Virgo Israel]], that is, the Israelite people, which is called a virgin: first, because in the patriarchs and prophets and the just it was espoused to God, although those who lived in the time of Amos had lost integrity and purity of soul, and committed fornication against God in many ways; secondly, to suggest the purity of nature considered in itself. Hence of the people of Babylon too it is written in Isaias: [[Is 47:1|sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon|Sede in pulvere, virgo filia Babylon]]. And in both senses Jeremias says of the people of Juda: [[Jer 14:17|because the virgin daughter of my people is afflicted with a great affliction|Quoniam contritione magna contrita est virgo filia populi mei]]. So then, [[5:2|The virgin of Israel is cast down upon her land|Virgo Israel projecta est in terram suam]], that is, conquered and trampled by her enemies in her own territory, or led into sins; [[5:2|there is none to raise her up|non est qui suscitet eam]], that is, to bring her back to her former state, by appeasing God with prayers or by vanquishing the Assyrian enemies. For although Amos here and the prophets of his time prayed for this people and instructed it, they would not make themselves fit for grace, but on the contrary killed the prophets. Of such the Lord, showing himself inexorable as regards some, says to Jeremias: [[Jer 7:16|nor take to thee praise and supplication for them|Non assumas laudem et orationem pro eis]]. [[Jer 15:1|If Moses and Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not towards this people|Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum]].

paras.t: Quia hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Urbs de qua egrediebantur mille, relinquentur in ea centum; et de qua egrediebantur centum, relinquentur in ea decem: id est, tanta erit pressura decem tribuum, quod decima pars eorum vix remanebit; in domo Israel, id est in universo populo decem tribuum, ita quod omnes civitates earum tam graviter vastabuntur. Numeros autem præfatos, videlicet mille, centum, decem, non oportet præcise accipere, sed ad insinuandum paucitatem evadentium, quemadmodum dictum est supra: Quomodo si eruat pastor duo crura aut extremum auriculæ de ore leonis, sic eruentur filii Israel. Quidam autem dicunt hoc factum in primo adventu Assyriorum, tempore Phul vel Theglathphalsar regum Assyriorum, videlicet, quod tunc decima pars Israel mansit. Sed in secundo ultimoque adventu sub Salmanasar etiam decimatio capta est, paucissimis tamen exceptis.
paras.en: [[5:3|For thus saith the Lord God: The city, out of which came forth a thousand, there shall be left in it a hundred: and out of which there came a hundred, there shall be left in it ten|Quia hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Urbs de qua egrediebantur mille, relinquentur in ea centum; et de qua egrediebantur centum, relinquentur in ea decem]]: that is, so great will be the oppression of the ten tribes that scarcely a tenth part of them will remain; [[5:3|in the house of Israel|in domo Israel]], that is, in the whole people of the ten tribes, so that all their cities will be laid waste so heavily. Now the numbers given, namely a thousand, a hundred, ten, are not to be taken exactly; they serve to suggest how few will escape, as was said above: [[Amos 3:12|As if a shepherd should get out of the lion's mouth two legs, or the tip of the ear: so shall the children of Israel be taken out|Quomodo si eruat pastor duo crura aut extremum auriculæ de ore leonis, sic eruentur filii Israel]]. Some say that this was done at the first coming of the Assyrians, in the time of Phul[[4 Kings 15:19||]] or Theglathphalsar[[4 Kings 15:29||]], kings of the Assyrians: that is, that a tenth part of Israel then remained. But at the second and last coming, under Salmanasar[[4 Kings 17:6||]], even the tenth was taken, though a very few were spared.

paras.t: Quia hæc dicit Dominus Deus domui Israel, id est plebi tribuum decem: Quærite me per veram pœnitentiam et perseverantiam sanctam, et vivetis, vita naturæ, evadendo manus hostiles, vita gratiæ in præsenti, et vita gloriæ in futuro. Hinc fertur in Psalmo: Quærite Deum, et vivet anima vestra.
paras.en: [[5:4|For thus saith the Lord to the house of Israel|Quia hæc dicit Dominus Deus domui Israel]], that is, to the people of the ten tribes: [[5:4|Seek ye me|Quærite me]] by true penance and holy perseverance, [[5:4|and you shall live|et vivetis]]: the life of nature, by escaping the hands of the enemy; the life of grace in the present; and the life of glory in the future. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:33|seek ye God, and your soul shall live|Quærite Deum, et vivet anima vestra]].

paras.t: Et nolite quærere Bethel, id est vitulum aureum positum in oppido Bethel; et in Galgalam, id est in locum sic dictum, nolite intrare, ut ibi idola invocetis. Est autem Galgala, secundum Glossam, civitas in fine duarum decemque tribuum sita. Et in Bersabee urbem duarum tribuum, sitam in fine regni tribus Juda: unde frequenter legitur, A Dan usque Bersabee; non transibitis, id est, non transeatis propter idololatriam ibi exercendam, quia in aliquibus locis regni Juda jam idololatria viguit. Quia Galgala captiva ducetur, id est, populus Galgalæ ab Assyriis capietur, et Bethel inutilis erit, id est, cives urbis illius et vitulus aureus non poterunt vos salvare: quia et urbs Bethel fuit devicta. De Bersabee autem nunc tacet, quoniam decem tribubus captis, non fuit destructa.
paras.en: [[5:5|But seek not Bethel|Et nolite quærere Bethel]], that is, the golden calf set up in the town of Bethel[[3 Kings 12:29||]]; and [[5:5|into Galgal|et in Galgalam]], that is, into the place so called, [[5:5|go not|nolite intrare]], to call upon idols there. Now Galgala, according to the Gloss, is a city lying on the border between the two tribes and the ten. [[5:5|to Bersabee|Et in Bersabee]], a city of the two tribes, lying on the border of the kingdom of the tribe of Juda (whence we often read, [[Judg 20:1|from Dan to Bersabee|A Dan usque Bersabee]][[1 Kings 3:20||]][[2 Kings 3:10||]]), [[5:5|neither shall you pass over|non transibitis]], that is, do not cross over to practise idolatry there, for in some places of the kingdom of Juda idolatry was already flourishing[[4 Kings 17:19||]]. [[5:5|for Galgal shall go into captivity|Quia Galgala captiva ducetur]], that is, the people of Galgala will be taken by the Assyrians, [[5:5|and Bethel shall be unprofitable|et Bethel inutilis erit]], that is, the citizens of that city and the golden calf will not be able to save you: for the city of Bethel too was conquered. Of Bersabee he says nothing now, because when the ten tribes were taken it was not destroyed.

paras.t: Quærite Dominum, ejus misericordiam, auxilium et salutem jugiter invocando, et vivite, uniti fonti vitæ, ne forte comburatur, id est, igne tribulationis et captivitatis incendatur et consumatur, ut ignis, qui ardendo deficit, deficiente combustionis materia, domus Joseph, id est plebis decem tribuum, quæ significatur per Joseph, quasi per principaliorem inter Patriarchas a quibus decem tribus exortæ sunt. Joseph enim data sunt primogenita, eo quod Ruben violasset torum patris sui, ut dicitur primo Paralipomenon libro. Vel ideo nomine Joseph decem tribus significantur, quia Jeroboam filius Nabat, primus rex decem tribuum, erat de semine Joseph per Ephraim. Unde Osee per Ephraim sæpe decem tribus, ut dictum est supra, expressit.
paras.en: [[5:6|Seek ye the Lord|Quærite Dominum]], calling unceasingly upon his mercy, help and salvation, [[5:6|and live|et vivite]], united to the fountain of life, [[5:6|lest the house of Joseph be burnt|ne forte comburatur]], that is, be kindled and consumed by the fire of tribulation and captivity, [[5:6|with fire|ut ignis]] [Denis reads *ut ignis* as "like a fire"], which in burning dies away when the matter for burning fails; [[5:6|the house of Joseph|domus Joseph]], that is, of the people of the ten tribes, who are signified by Joseph as by the chief among the patriarchs from whom the ten tribes sprang. For the birthright was given to Joseph, because Ruben had [[1 Par 5:1|defiled his father's bed|violasset torum patris sui]][[Gen 35:22||]], as is said in the first book of Paralipomenon. Or else the ten tribes are signified by the name of Joseph because Jeroboam the son of Nabat[[3 Kings 11:26||]], the first king of the ten tribes, was of the seed of Joseph through Ephraim. Hence Osee often expressed the ten tribes by Ephraim, as was said above.

paras.t: Et devorabit ignis iste domum Joseph, et non erit qui exstinguat Bethel, id est, a præinducto igne eripiat urbem Bethel et vitulum ejus, nisi quæsieritis Dominum, quem qui quærit, invenit. His verbis dedit Deus decem tribubus pœnitentiæ locum.
paras.en: [[5:6|and it shall devour|Et devorabit]], this fire, the house of Joseph, [[5:6|and there shall be none to quench Bethel|et non erit qui exstinguat Bethel]], that is, to snatch the city of Bethel and its calf from the fire spoken of before, unless you seek the Lord, whom [[Luke 11:10|he that seeketh findeth|qui quærit, invenit]]. By these words God gave the ten tribes room for penance.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta redarguit plebem hanc, et maxime judices ejus. Qui convertitis in absinthium judicium, id est, veritatem judicii ex sua natura dulcem ac delectabilem, sicut et omnes actus virtutis, convertitis in amaritudinem falsitatis, pauperum et innocentium judicia pervertendo: quod et illis amarissimum est. Est autem absinthius amarissima herba. Et justitiam in terra relinquitis, id est cultum divinum et Deum, qui est increata justitia; justitiam quoque commutativam, quæ in emptionibus venditionibusque consistit, et distributivam, quæ reddit unicuique quod suum est. De talibus scriptum est in Isaia: Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, et bonum malum, ponentes dulce in amarum, et amarum in dulce. Reliquistis ergo per idololatriam, increatam justitiam seu justum Deum, de quo subditur:
paras.en: Then the prophet rebukes this people, and above all its judges. [[5:7|You that turn judgment into wormwood|Qui convertitis in absinthium judicium]], that is, you turn the truth of judgment, which by its nature is sweet and delightful, as are all acts of virtue, into the bitterness of falsehood, by perverting the judgments of the poor and the innocent: which is most bitter to them as well. Now wormwood is a most bitter herb. [[5:7|and forsake justice in the land|Et justitiam in terra relinquitis]], that is, the worship of God, and God, who is uncreated justice; and also commutative justice, which consists in buying and selling, and distributive justice, which renders to each what is his. Of such it is written in Isaias: [[Is 5:20|Woe to you that call evil good, and good evil|Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, et bonum malum]], [[Is 5:20|that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter|ponentes dulce in amarum, et amarum in dulce]] [Denis leaves out the middle of the verse and gives the last pair the other way round: "putting sweet for bitter, and bitter for sweet"]. You have forsaken, then, by idolatry, the uncreated justice, that is, the just God, of whom it is added:

paras.t: Facientem Arcturum et Orionem. Arcturus, secundum Glossam, habet septem stellas, quem vocant aliqui Ursam majorem. Estque constellatio gyrans circa polum septentrionalem. Porro Orion, secundum Hieronymum, hieme oritur, et suo ortu tempestates signat ac excitat. Dicuntque aliqui, quod sit constellatio clara, partim in signo Tauri, et partim in signo Geminorum consistens. De horum expositione verborum pluribus scripsi super illud Job: Qui facit Arcturum et Oriona et Hyadas et interiora austri. Denique pro Orione, Symmachus transtulit, Stellas; Theodotion, Vesperum. Hebræus vero qui Hieronymum in divinis instruxit Scripturis, ut ipsemet refert Hieronymus, dixit verbum Hebraicum, pro quo positum est nomen Orionis, significare splendorem, sicque per Orionem generaliter intelligenda esse astra splendentia. Utitur autem Propheta nominibus a gentilibus institutis, magis quam Hebraicis, quoniam magis consueta intelligibilioraque erant.
paras.en: [[5:8|that maketh Arcturus, and Orion|Facientem Arcturum et Orionem]]. Arcturus, according to the Gloss, has seven stars; some call it the Great Bear. It is a constellation that turns about the northern pole. Orion, according to Jerome, rises in winter, and by its rising signals and stirs up storms. And some say that it is a bright constellation, lying partly in the sign of Taurus and partly in the sign of Gemini. I have written more fully on the explanation of these words on that passage of Job: [[Job 9:9|Who maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and Hyades, and the inner parts of the south|Qui facit Arcturum et Oriona et Hyadas et interiora austri]]. Lastly, for Orion Symmachus translated "Stars"; Theodotion, "Evening star" [*Vesperum*, that is, Hesperus]. But the Hebrew who instructed Jerome in the divine Scriptures, as Jerome himself relates, said that the Hebrew word for which the name of Orion was put means *splendour*, and so by Orion the shining stars in general are to be understood. The prophet uses names devised by the gentiles rather than Hebrew ones, because they were more customary and more intelligible.

paras.t: Et convertentem in mane tenebras, id est, post caliginem noctis facit auroram succedere, et diem in noctem mutantem, id est, diei facit succedere noctem, cujus ordinatione perseverat dies. Temporum enim dat tempora, ut allevet fastidium. Idcirco cantatur in Hymnis: Qui temperas rerum vices. Et iterum: Lucis diurnæ tempora Successibus determinans. Qui vocat aquas maris, id est, calore solis elevat eas in aere, et liquat ac excolat eas in dulcem humorem, et effundit eas guttatim super faciem, id est planitiem, terræ. Educit enim nubes ab extremo terræ. Qui operit cœlum nubibus, et parat terræ pluviam. De quo scriptum est in Job: Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum; et in Jeremia, Dante eo vocem, multiplicantur aquæ in cœlo. Dominus nomen ejus: quia nomen Domini competit ei soli per auctoritatem, et secundum perfectam rationem dominii: quoniam ipse solus propria potestate est universorum dominator liberrimus, ad quem omnis creatura refertur et comparatur sicut minister ad dominum, instrumentum ad artificem, subditus ad præsidem. Ideo ait per Isaiam: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo.
paras.en: [[5:8|and that turneth darkness into morning|Et convertentem in mane tenebras]], that is, after the gloom of night he makes the dawn follow, [[5:8|and that changeth day into night|et diem in noctem mutantem]], that is, he makes night follow day, he by whose [[Ps 118:91|ordinance the day goeth on|ordinatione perseverat dies]]. For he gives the times their turns, to relieve weariness [a phrase from St Ambrose's hymn *Æterne rerum conditor*: *temporum das tempora, ut alleves fastidium*]. Therefore it is sung in the hymns: Thou who orderest the changes of things. And again: Marking out the hours of daylight by their succession [the first from the hymn at Sext, *Rector potens, verax Deus*; the second from the hymn at None, *Rerum Deus tenax vigor*]. [[5:8|that calleth the waters of the sea|Qui vocat aquas maris]], that is, by the heat of the sun he raises them into the air, and melts and refines them into sweet moisture, [[5:8|and poureth them out|et effundit eas]] drop by drop [*guttatim*: this word is in Denis's text, not in the Vulgate] [[5:8|upon the face|super faciem]], that is, the surface, [[5:8|of the earth|terræ]]. For he [[Ps 134:7|bringeth up clouds from the end of the earth|Educit enim nubes ab extremo terræ]]; he [[Ps 146:8|covereth the heaven with clouds, and prepareth rain for the earth|operit cœlum nubibus, et parat terræ pluviam]]. Of him it is written in Job: [[Job 26:8|He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together|Qui ligat aquas in nubibus, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum]]; and in Jeremias: [[Jer 51:16|When he uttereth his voice the waters are multiplied in heaven|Dante eo vocem, multiplicantur aquæ in cœlo]] [the margin gives Jer. ii, 16; the words are those of Jer 51:16]. [[5:8|The Lord is his name|Dominus nomen ejus]]: because the name of Lord belongs to him alone by authority, and according to the perfect notion of lordship: since he alone, by his own power, is the wholly free ruler of all things, to whom every creature is referred and compared as a servant to his lord, an instrument to the craftsman, a subject to the governor. Therefore he says through Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo]].

paras.t: Qui subridet vastitatem super robustum, id est, robustis juste subsannando seu irridendo, minatur pressuram seu punitionem, et depopulationem super potentem affert, id est, potentibus inducit direptionem, deprædationem seu destructionem: quod hic ad litteram dicitur de regno ac populo Israel, quibus vastitatem ab Assyriis per Prophetas minabatur, et per Assyrios intulit. Verum, ut alibi scriptum est, Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens. Sed nunc de potentibus sua potentia abutentibus sermo est, quibus Deus vastitatem minatur, in Sapientiæ libro dicens: Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet; potentes enim potenter tormenta patientur; et, Fortioribus fortior instat cruciatus. Itemque in Psalmo: Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos, et Dominus subsannabit eos. Isaias quoque ait: Visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli in excelso, et super reges terræ.
paras.en: [[5:9|He that with a smile bringeth destruction upon the strong|Qui subridet vastitatem super robustum]], that is, justly mocking or deriding the strong, he threatens them with oppression or punishment, [[5:9|and waste upon the mighty|et depopulationem super potentem affert]], that is, he brings plundering, pillage or destruction upon the mighty: which is said here literally of the kingdom and people of Israel, whom he threatened through the prophets with devastation by the Assyrians, and upon whom he brought it through the Assyrians. Yet, as is written elsewhere, [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens]]. But here the talk is of the mighty who abuse their might, whom God threatens with devastation, saying in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]; [[Wis 6:7|the mighty shall be mightily tormented|potentes enim potenter tormenta patientur]]; and: [[Wis 6:9|a greater punishment is ready for the more mighty|Fortioribus fortior instat cruciatus]]. And again in the Psalm: [[Ps 2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: and the Lord shall deride them|Qui habitat in cœlis irridebit eos, et Dominus subsannabit eos]]. Isaias too says: [[Is 24:21|the Lord shall visit upon the host of heaven on high, and upon the kings of the earth|Visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli in excelso, et super reges terræ]].

paras.t: Odio habuerunt decem tribus in porta corripientem, id est judices justos et Prophetas, qui in portis urbium delinquentes reprehenderunt caritative ac juste; et loquentem perfecte, id est viros sapientes efficaciterque docentes, abominati sunt. Hoc faciunt homines protervi, arrogantes, incorrigibiles. Quod quam perversum sit, patet ex eo quod scriptum est in Proverbiorum libro: Viro qui dura cervice corripientem contemnit, repentinus superveniet interitus. Et alio loco: Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, glorificabitur. Hinc iterum ait: Argue sapientem, et diliget te; doce justum, et festinabit accipere. Loquitur autem perfecte, qui facit quod docet, et verba distincte ac intelligibiliter profert.
paras.en: [[5:10|They have hated|Odio habuerunt]] (the ten tribes) [[5:10|him that rebuketh in the gate|in porta corripientem]], that is, just judges and prophets, who in the gates of the cities reproved wrongdoers with charity and justice; and [[5:10|him that speaketh perfectly|et loquentem perfecte]], that is, wise men who teach to good effect, [[5:10|have abhorred|abominati sunt]]. This is what froward, arrogant and incorrigible men do. How perverse it is appears from what is written in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 29:1|The man that with a stiff neck despiseth him that reproveth him, shall suddenly be destroyed|Viro qui dura cervice corripientem contemnit, repentinus superveniet interitus]]. And in another place: [[Prov 13:18|Poverty and shame to him that refuseth instruction: but he that yieldeth to reproof shall be glorified|Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, glorificabitur]]. Hence again he says: [[Prov 9:8|Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee|Argue sapientem, et diliget te]]; [[Prov 9:9|Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it|doce justum, et festinabit accipere]]. Now he speaks perfectly who does what he teaches, and utters his words distinctly and intelligibly.

paras.t: Idcirco, pro eo quod diripiebatis pauperem, id est, pauperes spoliastis, illos præcipue qui pergebant Jerusalem adorare in templo Deum verum, et prædam electam tollebatis ab eo, id est ea quæ meliora erant, et vobis magis placentia; domos quadro lapide, id est ex lapidibus politis, quadratis, sive marmoreis, ædificabitis. De hoc habetur in Isaia: Sciet populus Ephraim et habitantes Samariam in magnitudine cordis, dicentes: Lateres ceciderunt, sed quadris lapidibus ædificabimus. Et non habitabitis in eis diu, qui jam ab Assyriis capiemini. Vineas amantissimas, id est pulchras et vobis carissimas, plantabitis, et non bibetis vinum earum, id est capti ab hostibus, qui omnia bona vestra diripient, eo quod pauperes spoliastis.
paras.en: [[5:11|Therefore because you robbed the poor|Idcirco, pro eo quod diripiebatis pauperem]], that is, you despoiled the poor, above all those who went to Jerusalem to worship the true God in the temple, [[5:11|and took the choice prey from him|et prædam electam tollebatis ab eo]], that is, the things that were better and more pleasing to you: [[5:11|houses with square stone|domos quadro lapide]], that is, of polished, squared or marble stones, [[5:11|you shall build|ædificabitis]]. Of this we read in Isaias: [[Is 9:9|And all the people of Ephraim shall know, and the inhabitants of Samaria that say in the pride and haughtiness of their heart|Sciet populus Ephraim et habitantes Samariam in magnitudine cordis, dicentes]]: [[Is 9:10|The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with square stones|Lateres ceciderunt, sed quadris lapidibus ædificabimus]]. [[5:11|and shall not dwell in them|Et non habitabitis in eis]] for long, you who will soon be taken by the Assyrians. [[5:11|most delightful vineyards|Vineas amantissimas]], that is, fair and very dear to you, [[5:11|you shall plant|plantabitis]], [[5:11|and shall not drink the wine of them|et non bibetis vinum earum]], that is, since you will be taken by your enemies, who will plunder all your goods, because you despoiled the poor.

paras.t: Quia cognovi multa scelera vestra, id est idololatriam et peccata annexa, et fortia peccata vestra, id est violentiam in egenos. Vel peccata dicuntur fortia, id est, iram Dei graviter provocantia. Non ergo propter idololatriam tantum vos punio, sed ob alia quoque peccata. Vel peccata dicta sunt fortia, quia ex vehementi passione procedunt. Quidam enim toto impetu feruntur in malum. Denique cognitio interdum accipitur pro notitia approbationis, sicque Deus dicitur non cognoscere malos et mala, juxta illud in Osee: Principes exstiterunt, et non cognovi; et in Evangelio, Amen dico vobis, quia nescio vos. Sicque affirmat Apostolus: Si quis ignorat, ignorabitur. Interdum vero cognitio sumitur pro quacumque scientia sive notitia: et sic, omnia nuda et aperta sunt oculis ejus. Atque hoc modo cognoscit peccata nostra Deus infallibilis judex, juxta illud in Psalmo: Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Agnoscit autem Deus peccata et mala, seu privativa, non per ideam propriam, sed per ideam, rationem seu speciem virtutis ac boni oppositi.
paras.en: [[5:12|Because I know your manifold crimes|Quia cognovi multa scelera vestra]], that is, idolatry and the sins joined to it, [[5:12|and your grievous sins|et fortia peccata vestra]] [*fortia*, literally "strong", which the explanations that follow turn on], that is, violence against the needy. Or the sins are called strong, that is, heavily provoking the wrath of God: so I do not punish you for idolatry alone, but for other sins as well. Or the sins are called strong because they proceed from vehement passion: for some men are borne into evil with all their force. Lastly, knowing is sometimes taken for the knowledge of approval, and so God is said not to know the wicked and wicked things, according to that in Osee: [[Osee 8:4|they have been princes, and I knew not|Principes exstiterunt, et non cognovi]]; and in the Gospel: [[Matt 25:12|Amen I say to you, I know you not|Amen dico vobis, quia nescio vos]]. And so the Apostle affirms: [[1 Cor 14:38|if any man know not, he shall not be known|Si quis ignorat, ignorabitur]]. But sometimes knowing is taken for any knowledge or awareness whatever; and in this sense [[Heb 4:13|all things are naked and open to his eyes|omnia nuda et aperta sunt oculis ejus]]. And in this way God, the infallible judge, knows our sins, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:6|my offences are not hidden from thee|Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]]. Now God knows sins and evils, that is, privations [*privativa*: since evil is a lack of some good, there is no idea of it of its own in God's mind], not by an idea of their own, but by the idea, notion or species of the opposite virtue and good.

paras.t: Hostes justi, id est, vos principes et judices decem tribuum, hostes estis justi, id est justorum hominum vel justitiæ, accipientes munus, id est dona pro subversione justitiæ et oppressione justorum. De talibus ait Jeremias: A minori usque ad majorem omnes avaritiæ student; et Psalmista, Dextera eorum repleta est muneribus. Et pauperes in porta, ubi fiebat determinatio causarum, opprimentes injuste, excæcati muneribus divitum. Solebant enim in veteri Testamento judices Israel sedere in portis civitatum ad judicandum, ut invenirentur in promptu; et ne rustici ad judicium venientes, insolito civium terrerentur adspectu; et item, ne cives longius tendere cogerentur.
paras.en: [[5:12|enemies of the just|Hostes justi]], that is, you princes and judges of the ten tribes are enemies of the just, that is, of just men or of justice, [[5:12|taking bribes|accipientes munus]], that is, gifts for the overthrow of justice and the oppression of the just. Of such Jeremias says: [[Jer 6:13|from the least of them even to the greatest, all are given to covetousness|A minori usque ad majorem omnes avaritiæ student]][[Jer 8:10||]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 25:10|their right hand is filled with gifts|Dextera eorum repleta est muneribus]]. And [[5:12|the poor in the gate|pauperes in porta]], where cases were decided, [[5:12|oppressing|opprimentes]] unjustly, blinded by the gifts of the rich. For in the Old Testament the judges of Israel used to sit in the gates of the cities to judge, so as to be readily found; and so that country folk coming to judgment should not be frightened by the unaccustomed sight of the townsmen; and again, so that the townsmen should not be obliged to go any farther.

paras.t: Ideo prudens in tempore illo tacebit, quia tempus malum est. Hoc tripliciter elucidatur: Primo, quod pauperes in portis oppressi, injuriamque perpessi, si fuerint circumspecti, tacebunt, non murmurantes, accusantes aut reclamantes; quia tempus malum est, id est, pro tempore illo regnantes ac judicantes, injusti fuerunt, nec erat possibile ad æquum pervenire judicium, sicque utilius fuit silere quam contradicere. Secundo, quod prudentes atque Prophetæ in tempore illo, quando hostilis exercitus urbes jam cinxit, tacerent a populi increpatione, quia captivitas inevitabiliter immineret. Tertio, quod tacerent propter incorrigibilitatem populi, quia quanto plus increpabatur, tanto impatientior deteriorque fiebat: quia, ut Sapiens ait, Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit; et, Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit. Idcirco in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem. Tempus autem malum vocatur, non in se, sed propter mala quæ fiunt in eo. Unde et Jacob ait in Genesi: Dies peregrinationis meæ parvi et mali.
paras.en: [[5:13|Therefore the prudent shall keep silence at that time|Ideo prudens in tempore illo tacebit]], [[5:13|for it is an evil time|quia tempus malum est]]. This is explained in three ways. First, that the poor, oppressed in the gates and suffering wrong, will, if they are circumspect, keep silence, not murmuring, accusing or protesting; [[5:13|for it is an evil time|quia tempus malum est]]: that is, those who reigned and judged at that time were unjust, and it was not possible to obtain a fair judgment, and so it was more profitable to be silent than to speak against them. Second, that the prudent and the Prophets at that time, when the enemy army had already surrounded the cities, would cease from rebuking the people, because the captivity was inevitably at hand. Third, that they would keep silence because of the incorrigibility of the people, since the more it was rebuked, the more impatient and the worse it became; for, as the Wise Man says, [[Prov 15:12|A corrupt man loveth not one that reproveth him|Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit]]; and, [[Prov 9:7|He that teacheth a scorner, doth an injury to himself|Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit]]. Therefore it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:6|Where there is no hearing, pour not out words|Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem]]. Now the time is called evil, not in itself, but because of the evils that are done in it. Hence Jacob too says in Genesis: [[Gen 47:9|The days of my pilgrimage|Dies peregrinationis meæ]] are [[Gen 47:9|few, and evil|parvi et mali]].

paras.t: Jam dixit Propheta, quod prudens in tempore illo jam dicto tacebit. Ideo nunc ante tempus captivitatis admonet eos. Quærite bonum virtutum, id est judicium atque justitiam, latriæ actus et misericordiæ opera, et non malum vitiorum. Qui autem ex proposito peccant, quærunt malum, quoniam quasi de industria perpetrant prava, quemadmodum scriptum est in Psalmo: Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso. Ut vivatis per gratiam, et mortem ab Assyriis imminentem evadatis. Et erit Dominus Deus exercituum vobiscum, per gratiosam inhabitationem et protectionem ab hostibus, sicut dixistis idola vestra esse vobiscum; vel, Sicut dixistis, id est, orastis ac desiderastis. Simul enim coluerunt Deum et idola decem tribus, saltem pro magna parte, ut dictum est. Vel, Sicut dixistis, id est, jactastis Deum esse vobiscum, eo quod sitis de semine Abraham. Gloriabantur enim de carnalis propagationis nobilitate, non de morum ac fidei imitatione. Ergo quia de Abraham descenderunt, putabant se propter carnis originem defensandos a Deo. Tales erant et Judæi quibus ait Salvator: Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite. Et Præcursor ejus: Ne velitis dicere, Patrem habemus Abraham. Facite ergo dignos fructus pœnitentiæ.
paras.en: The Prophet has just said that the prudent will keep silence at the time just spoken of. Therefore he now admonishes them before the time of the captivity: [[5:14|Seek ye good|Quærite bonum]] of the virtues, that is, judgment and justice, acts of latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone] and works of mercy, [[5:14|and not evil|et non malum]] of the vices. Now those who sin of set purpose seek evil, since they commit wicked deeds as it were deliberately, as it is written in the Psalm: [[Ps 35:2|The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin|Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso]]. [[5:14|that you may live|Ut vivatis]] by grace, and escape the death that threatens you from the Assyrians. [[5:14|and the Lord the God of hosts will be with you|Et erit Dominus Deus exercituum vobiscum]], by his gracious indwelling and his protection from your enemies, [[5:14|as you have said|sicut dixistis]] that your idols are with you. Or, [[5:14|as you have said|Sicut dixistis]], that is, as you have prayed and desired: for the ten tribes, at least for the most part, worshipped God and the idols together, as has been said. Or, [[5:14|as you have said|Sicut dixistis]], that is, as you have boasted that God is with you because you are of the seed of Abraham. For they gloried in the nobility of their descent according to the flesh, not in imitating his manners and his faith. So because they were descended from Abraham, they thought that God would defend them on account of their fleshly origin. Such too were the Jews to whom the Saviour says: [[John 8:39|If you be the children of Abraham, do the works of Abraham|Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite]]. And his Forerunner: [[Matt 3:9|think not to say|Ne velitis dicere]], [[Matt 3:9|We have Abraham for our father|Patrem habemus Abraham]]. [[Matt 3:8|Bring forth therefore fruit worthy of penance|Facite ergo dignos fructus pœnitentiæ]].

paras.t: Odite malum culpæ in se et propter se. Peccator autem non est odiendus in se, et quantum ad naturam, sed quantum ad vitium. Et diligite bonum virtutum. Primo enim oportet a malo recedere per detestationem peccati, et deinde diligere ac agere bonum: quia a malo declinare, et facere bonum, sunt quasi duæ partes integrales justitiæ. Et constituite in porta judicium, id est judices justos; vel, justum judicium exercete in portis civitatum, quemadmodum in Deuteronomio Moyses jussit. Si forte misereatur Dominus Deus exercituum reliquiis Joseph, id est residuo decem tribuum, quod nondum manus incidit hostium. Cur autem decem tribus per Joseph designentur, jam dictum est. Hoc quoque quod ait, Si forte, non dubitative, sed assertive legendum. Loquitur autem sic, non propter mutabilitatem aut ambiguitatem exsistentem in Deo, sed in hominibus. Dubium vero non est, quin Deus misereatur omnibus qui odiunt malum et diligunt bonum: quos tamen non semper a temporali eripit tribulatione seu captivitate, quia non expedit eorum saluti. Si tamen filii Israel ita fecissent, forsitan a captivitate eos eripuisset, quamvis frequenter dixerit eos capiendos. Sic namque ait ad duas tribus in Jeremia: Bonas facite vias vestras, et habitabo vobiscum.
paras.en: [[5:15|Hate evil|Odite malum]]: the evil of guilt, in itself and for its own sake. The sinner, however, is not to be hated in himself and as to his nature, but as to his vice. [[5:15|and love good|Et diligite bonum]] of the virtues. For first one must withdraw from evil by detesting sin, and then love and do good; for to decline from evil and to do good[[Ps 33:15||]][[Ps 36:27||]][[1 Pet 3:11||]] are as it were the two integral parts of justice. [[5:15|and establish judgment in the gate|Et constituite in porta judicium]], that is, just judges; or, exercise just judgment in the gates of the cities, as Moses commanded in Deuteronomy[[Deut 16:18||]]. [[5:15|it may be the Lord the God of hosts may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph|Si forte misereatur Dominus Deus exercituum reliquiis Joseph]], that is, on the residue of the ten tribes, which has not yet fallen into the hands of the enemy. Why the ten tribes are signified by Joseph has been said already. And this that he says, [[5:15|it may be|Si forte]], is to be read not as doubting but as asserting. He speaks thus not because of any changeableness or uncertainty that exists in God, but in men. For there is no doubt that God has mercy on all who hate evil and love good; yet he does not always rescue them from temporal tribulation or captivity, since that is not expedient for their salvation. Yet if the children of Israel had done so, perhaps he would have rescued them from captivity, although he often said that they would be taken. For so he says to the two tribes in Jeremias: [[Jer 7:3|Make your ways|Bonas facite vias vestras]] good, [[Jer 7:3|and I will dwell with you|et habitabo vobiscum]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam præinducta mala fecistis, nec salutaribus monitis acquiescere voluistis: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus exercituum dominator, Dominus potestate, Deus natura, dominator actu: In omnibus plateis civitatum vestrarum erit planctus; et in cunctis quæ foris sunt, id est vicis, villis, castellis, dicetur a populo vestro, Væ, væ, id est dolor interior atque exterior, quando videlicet Assyrii venerint, et terram vastaverint. Et vocabunt agricolam ad luctum et ad planctum, id est, eos qui circa rusticana et exteriora occupantur, vocabunt, ut cessantes a talibus, jam nunc fletibus vacent. Hoc fecerunt filii Israel quando ab Assyriis pressi sunt. Et ad planctum vocabunt eos qui sciunt plangere, id est, artem habent plangendi, puta tibicines, qui carmen lugubre præcinendo, alios ad lacrimas provocant. Diversæ enim melodiæ, diversas in animo concitant passiones seu affectiones. Erat autem consuetudo Judæis, tales habere in defunctorum ædibus atque exsequiis. Unde in Evangelio legitur, quod Christus ingressus Jairi archisynagogi domum, suscitaturus ejus filiam, vidit tibicines.
paras.en: But since you have done the evils set out above, and would not heed wholesome warnings, [[5:16|Therefore thus saith the Lord the God of hosts the sovereign Lord|Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus exercituum dominator]]: Lord in power, God in nature, sovereign in act: [[5:16|In every street|In omnibus plateis]] of your cities [[5:16|there shall be wailing|erit planctus]] [the printed text reads *plantus*, a slip for *planctus*]; [[5:16|and in all places that are without|et in cunctis quæ foris sunt]], that is, in the hamlets, farms and fortified places, [[5:16|they shall say|dicetur]] (by your people): [[5:16|Alas, alas|Væ, væ]], that is, grief within and without, namely when the Assyrians come and lay waste the land. [[5:16|and they shall call the husbandman to mourning|Et vocabunt agricolam ad luctum]] and to lamentation: that is, they shall call those who are busied with the work of the countryside and things outside, so that, leaving such work, they may now give themselves to weeping. The children of Israel did this when they were hard pressed by the Assyrians. [[5:16|and such as are skilful in lamentation to lament|Et ad planctum vocabunt eos qui sciunt plangere]], that is, those who have the art of lamenting, for instance the pipers, who by playing a mournful song before others move them to tears. For different melodies stir up different passions or affections in the soul. And it was the custom among the Jews to have such men in the houses of the dead and at funerals. Hence we read in the Gospel that Christ, entering the house of Jairus the ruler of the synagogue to raise his daughter, saw the minstrels[[Matt 9:23||]].

paras.t: Et in omnibus viis (alias vineis), in quibus cadetis vel captivi ducemini, erit planctus, quia vos ipsi lugebitis; quia pertransibo in medio tui, dicit Dominus, id est, in vobis non remanebo, nec habitabo per opem et gratiam, sed transibo, exercendo vindictam vosque derelinquendo. Dicit vero Hieronymus, quod ubicumque in Scripturis dicitur Deus pertransire, insinuatur punitio.
paras.en: [[5:17|And in all|Et in omnibus]] ways (another reading: [[5:17|vineyards|vineis]]), in which you will fall or be led captive, [[5:17|there shall be wailing|erit planctus]], for you yourselves will mourn; [[5:17|because I will pass through in the midst of thee, saith the Lord|quia pertransibo in medio tui, dicit Dominus]], that is, I will not remain among you, nor dwell with you by my help and grace, but will pass through, taking vengeance and forsaking you. And Jerome says that wherever in the Scriptures God is said to pass through, punishment is signified.

paras.t: Væ desiderantibus diem Domini. Locus iste a diversis diversimode explanatur. Sed primo ponenda est expositio Hieronymi, quam Glossa et alii communiter assequuntur. Itaque, secundum Hieronymum, Propheta nunc ad utrumque regnum, videlicet Juda et decem tribuum, dirigit verbum, ut sit sensus: Væ erroris ac tribulationis imminet desiderantibus diem Domini, id est tempus captivitatis suæ ab Assyriis vel Chaldæis. Judæi enim nonnulli audientes magna promitti a Deo per Prophetas, danda post reditum a captivitate, optabant diem captivitatis accelerari, ut citius obtinerent bona promissa post captivitatem præstanda. Quamvis enim captivitatem secundum se pensatam abhorrerent, tamen ut erat via ad prosperitatem majorem, optaverant eam. Quod autem in hoc erraverunt, ostendit Propheta. Ut quid (Ad quid) eam vobis optatis? id est, cur cupitis eam? quasi dicat, Inutiliter facitis hoc. Nam dies Domini ista, tenebræ, et non lux, id est, tempus captivitatis adversum et triste erit vobis, quum venerit, non luminosum, id est prosperum et jucundum. Putabant enim captivitatem citius finiendam, et ea finita, mox implenda esse divina promissa. Quæ tamen secundum verum intellectum Scripturæ, intelligenda erant pro tempore Christi, ut est illud Isaiæ: Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta.
paras.en: [[5:18|Woe to them that desire the day of the Lord|Væ desiderantibus diem Domini]]. This passage is explained in different ways by different authors. But first we must set down the exposition of Jerome, which the Gloss and others commonly follow. According to Jerome, then, the Prophet now directs his word to both kingdoms, that is, Juda and the ten tribes, so that the sense is: a woe of error and of tribulation hangs over [[5:18|them that desire the day of the Lord|desiderantibus diem Domini]], that is, the time of their captivity by the Assyrians or the Chaldeans. For some of the Jews, hearing that great things were promised by God through the Prophets, to be given after the return from captivity, wished the day of the captivity to be hastened, so that they might sooner obtain the good things promised for after the captivity. For although they shrank from the captivity considered in itself, yet they had wished for it inasmuch as it was the way to greater prosperity. That they erred in this the Prophet shows: [[5:18|to what end|Ut quid]] (another reading: *Ad quid*) [[5:18|is it for you|eam vobis optatis]] [Denis's text reads *eam vobis optatis*, "do you wish it for yourselves"]? That is, why do you desire it? As if to say, You do this to no purpose. For [[5:18|the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light|dies Domini ista, tenebræ, et non lux]]: that is, the time of the captivity will be adverse and sad for you when it comes, not full of light, that is, prosperous and pleasant. For they thought that the captivity would soon be ended, and that once it was ended the divine promises would at once be fulfilled. Yet according to the true understanding of Scripture these were to be understood of the time of Christ, as is that of Isaias: [[Is 32:18|my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]].

paras.t: Multum ergo errabant, nec adepturi erant quod speraverunt, sed venturum fuit eis quod subditur: Quomodo si fugiat vir a facie leonis, et occurrat ei ursus, sic fiet vobis. Per leonem autem intelligitur Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis, qui afflixit duas tribus. Decem vero tribus afflixit rex Assur. Porro per ursum intelligitur Assuerus rex Persarum atque Medorum, qui post Nabuchodonosor captos tenebat Judæos, et ad tempus satis afflixit, quando suggerente Aman, præcepit una omnes die interfici. Et ingrediatur domum, et innitatur manu sua super parietem, et mordeat eum coluber: id est, sic fiet vobis, ut postquam a captivitate Babylonica reversi fueritis in propriam terram, et templum construxeritis, atque in eo quiescere cœperitis, sicut quiescit qui lassus manu sua innititur muro, tunc mordebit vos coluber, id est Antiochus rex: qui velut serpens sedit in Terra sancta, opprimens crudelissime plebem Judaicam, in qua multi fuerunt ex decem tribubus.
paras.en: They erred greatly, then, and were not going to obtain what they hoped for; rather, what follows was to come upon them: [[5:19|As if a man should flee from the face of a lion, and a bear should meet him|Quomodo si fugiat vir a facie leonis, et occurrat ei ursus]], so shall it be with you. By the lion is understood Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, who afflicted the two tribes; the ten tribes the king of Assyria afflicted. And by the bear is understood Assuerus king of the Persians and Medes, who after Nabuchodonosor held the Jews captive, and for a time afflicted them sorely, when at the suggestion of Aman[[Esth 3:8||]] he commanded that all should be killed on one day[[Esth 3:13||]]. [[5:19|or enter into the house, and lean with his hand upon the wall, and a serpent should bite him|Et ingrediatur domum, et innitatur manu sua super parietem, et mordeat eum coluber]]: that is, so shall it be with you, that after you have returned from the Babylonian captivity into your own land, and built the temple, and begun to rest in it, as one who is weary rests leaning with his hand on a wall, then the serpent will bite you: that is, king Antiochus, who like a serpent sat in the Holy Land, most cruelly oppressing the Jewish people, among whom were many of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Huic expositioni quidam opponit, quod reges Juda, sacerdotes ac principes, simul cum vulgo persequebantur Jeremiam, eo quod captivitatem instantem prædixit: non ergo eam desiderabant. Itaque dicit, quod Propheta hic loquitur contra illusores, qui comminationes propheticas non reputabant veras, sed illudendo quasi optando dixerunt: Veniat dies quam prænuntiatis. Sic enim in Isaia dixisse feruntur: Manda, remanda; manda, remanda, etc.; et in Ezechiele, In tempora longa iste prophetat; itemque in Jeremia, Ubi est verbum Domini? Veniat. Sic ergo est sensus: Væ desiderantibus diem Domini, id est per modum optantis ironice dicentibus, Veniat tempus vindictæ prænuntiatum.
paras.en: Against this exposition someone objects that the kings of Juda, the priests and the princes, together with the common people, persecuted Jeremias because he foretold the coming captivity[[Jer 26:7||]][[Jer 38:4||]]: therefore they did not desire it. And so he says that the Prophet is speaking here against the mockers, who did not think the prophetic threats true, but said in mockery, as though wishing it: Let the day come that you foretell. For so they are said to have spoken in Isaias: [[Is 28:10|command, command again; command, command again|Manda, remanda; manda, remanda]], etc.; and in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 12:27|this man prophesieth of times afar off|In tempora longa iste prophetat]]; and likewise in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:15|Where is the word of the Lord? let it come|Ubi est verbum Domini? Veniat]]. So the sense is: [[5:18|Woe to them that desire the day of the Lord|Væ desiderantibus diem Domini]], that is, to those who say ironically, in the manner of one who wishes it, Let the time of vengeance that was foretold come.

paras.t: Quod autem expositio ista sit frivola, liquet ex eo quod Propheta per veram rationem reprobat desiderium adventus diei Domini, scilicet captivitatis. Veraciter ergo desideraverunt hanc diem. Instantia demum de Jeremia facillime solvitur, quia ut patet in libro Jeremiæ, principes quandoque erant pro Jeremia, et etiam populus, ne occideretur. Et quamvis non fuissent pro eo, argumentum tamen præinductum nil obtineret: quia Propheta non dicit quod omnes vel multi diem præfatam optabant; sed indeterminate locutus est, Væ desiderantibus, etc.
paras.en: That this exposition is frivolous, however, is clear from the fact that the Prophet reproves the desire for the coming of the day of the Lord, that is, of the captivity, with a real reason. Therefore they truly desired this day. Then the objection [*instantia*, that is, a counter-argument raised in disputation] about Jeremias is very easily answered, for, as is plain in the book of Jeremias, the princes were at times on Jeremias's side, and the people too, so that he should not be killed[[Jer 26:16||]] [the margin also gives Jer. xxviii, 7 and following; that chapter tells of Hananias, and the rescue of Jeremias by Abdemelech is at Jer 38:7 and following, perhaps the place meant]. And even if they had not been on his side, the argument brought forward would still prove nothing, because the Prophet does not say that all or many wished for the said day, but he spoke indefinitely: [[5:18|Woe to them that desire|Væ desiderantibus]], etc.

paras.t: Imo adhuc ostendit desiderabilem non fuisse hanc diem: Numquid non tenebræ dies Domini, et non lux? et caligo, et non splendor in ea? id est, tempus vastitatis vestræ etiam tempore Antiochi erit prorsus dolorosum, durum, gravissimum, nil habens de luce prosperitatis vel splendore consolationis: quemadmodum in libro Machabæorum describitur.
paras.en: Indeed, he shows further that this day was not to be desired: [[5:20|Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness, and not light: and obscurity, and no brightness in it?|Numquid non tenebræ dies Domini, et non lux? et caligo, et non splendor in ea?]]. That is, the time of your devastation, even in the time of Antiochus, will be altogether sorrowful, hard and most grievous, having nothing of the light of prosperity or the brightness of consolation, as is described in the book of Machabees[[1 Mach 2:1||]].

paras.t: Et ne Judæi in suis cærimonialibus spem haberent, addidit Dominus: Odi et projeci festivitates vestras, id est, celebrationes festorum legalium non acceptavi a vobis, sed velut opera vitiosa despexi; et non capiam odorem cœtuum vestrorum, id est, sacrificia quæ turbæ vestræ offerunt mihi, non acceptabo. Unde subjungitur: Quod si obtuleritis mihi, holocautomata et munera vestra non suscipiam, id est, grata mihi non erunt, nec meritoria; et vota pinguium vestrorum, id est oblationes votivas de carnibus pinguium pecorum factas, non respiciam per approbationem. Hæc autem idcirco dicuntur, quoniam sacrificiis et celebrationibus festivis istorum tot scelera erant admixta, quod Deo non placuerunt, sed potius displicuerunt. Opus enim Dei fecerunt tam irreverenter. Et secundum Hieronymum, etiam cum Deo coluerunt et idola.
paras.en: And lest the Jews should put their hope in their ceremonies, the Lord added: [[5:21|I hate, and have rejected your festivities|Odi et projeci festivitates vestras]], that is, I have not accepted from you the celebrations of the feasts of the Law, but have despised them as sinful works; [[5:21|and I will not receive the odour of your assemblies|et non capiam odorem cœtuum vestrorum]], that is, I will not accept the sacrifices that your crowds offer me. Hence it is added: [[5:22|And if you offer me holocausts, and your gifts, I will not receive them|Quod si obtuleritis mihi, holocautomata et munera vestra non suscipiam]], that is, they will not be pleasing to me, nor meritorious; and [[5:22|the vows of your fat beasts|et vota pinguium vestrorum]], that is, the votive offerings made of the flesh of fat cattle, [[5:22|neither will I regard|non respiciam]] with approval. These things are said because so many crimes were mixed with these men's sacrifices and festal celebrations that they did not please God, but rather displeased him. For they did the work of God so irreverently. And, according to Jerome, they also worshipped idols together with God.

paras.t: Aufer a me, id est, cessa mihi offerre, o populus regni Juda, et qui ex decem tribubus ei vos copulastis, tumultum carminum tuorum, id est indevotam ac inordinatam decantationem laudum divinarum, quas ex Scripturis mihi in templo offertis; et cantica lyræ tuæ, id est musicorum instrumentorum, non audiam. Non enim est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris; et, Peccatori dixit Deus, Quare tu enarras justitias meas? Et, Qui declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis. Hæc tamen non ita dicuntur, quod iniqui debeant penitus a divina laude et persolutione Horarum ac precibus cohiberi, sed ut studeant se emendare, et sciant se per tam imperfecta obsequia non posse salvari. Aliqui quoque actus divinæ laudis ac servitutis, ex speciali mandato requirunt ut in caritate et devotione persolvantur, ut celebratio, sermocinatio, etc.
paras.en: [[5:23|Take away from me|Aufer a me]], that is, cease to offer me, O people of the kingdom of Juda, and you of the ten tribes who have joined yourselves to it, [[5:23|the tumult of thy songs|tumultum carminum tuorum]], that is, the undevout and disordered chanting of the divine praises which you offer me from the Scriptures in the temple; and [[5:23|the canticles of thy harp|et cantica lyræ tuæ]] (that is, of musical instruments) [[5:23|I will not hear|non audiam]]. For [[Ecclus 15:9|Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner|Non enim est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris]]; and, [[Ps 49:16|to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare my justices|Peccatori dixit Deus, Quare tu enarras justitias meas]]? And, [[Prov 28:9|He that turneth away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination|Qui declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis]]. Yet these things are not said to mean that the wicked ought to be wholly kept from the divine praise, the recitation of the Hours and prayers, but that they should strive to amend themselves, and know that they cannot be saved by such imperfect service. Some acts of divine praise and service also, by a special command, require that they be performed in charity and devotion, such as the celebration of Mass, preaching, etc.

paras.t: Et revelabitur quasi aqua, id est, omnibus clare et copiose ostendetur, judicium tuum, id est damnatio seu vindicta tibi nunc infligenda; et justitia, id est æquitas Dei, quasi torrens fortis, id est, delebit te quemadmodum aqua impetuosa rapit et aufert ea quæ apprehendit.
paras.en: [[5:24|But judgment shall be revealed as water|Et revelabitur quasi aqua]], that is, shall be shown to all clearly and abundantly, thy [[5:24|judgment|judicium]], that is, the condemnation or vengeance now to be inflicted on thee; [[5:24|and justice|et justitia]], that is, the equity of God, [[5:24|as a mighty torrent|quasi torrens fortis]]: that is, it will destroy thee, as rushing water sweeps up and carries away whatever it seizes.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur, quod sacrificia legalia non erant per se accepta, nec absolute ad salutem necessaria, quia sine illis aliquando placuit Israel Deo. Numquid hostias et sacrificium obtulistis mihi in deserto quadraginta annis, domus Israel? quasi dicat, Non. Hoc autem duobus potest modis intelligi. Hieronymus enim circa hunc locum sic ait: Ex hoc discimus, omnes hostias et sacrificia quæ in deserto obtulit Israel, non Deo obtulisse, sed Moloch regi suo, id est Lucifero. Dicit demum Hieronymus, et habetur in Glossa: Ex quo tempore factum est caput vituli aurei in deserto, omnia quæ fecerunt vel obtulerunt filii Israel, non Deo, sed idolis fecisse monstrantur. Quod si leguntur postea aliqua Deo obtulisse, non voluntate, sed metu pœnarum offerebant, et ob interfectionem eorum qui propter idololatriam sunt occisi. Dominus autem non tam ea quæ offeruntur, quam voluntatem suscipit offerentium.
paras.en: Next it is shown that the sacrifices of the Law were not acceptable in themselves, nor absolutely necessary to salvation, since without them Israel once pleased God. [[5:25|Did you offer victims and sacrifices to me in the desert for forty years, O house of Israel?|Numquid hostias et sacrificium obtulistis mihi in deserto quadraginta annis, domus Israel?]]. As if to say, No. This can be understood in two ways. For Jerome says on this place: From this we learn that all the victims and sacrifices which Israel offered in the desert it offered not to God but to Moloch its king, that is, to Lucifer. Jerome says further, and it is found in the Gloss: From the time that the head of the golden calf was made in the desert, all that the children of Israel did or offered is shown to have been done not for God but for idols. And if we read that afterwards they offered some things to God, they offered them not willingly but for fear of punishment, and because of the slaying of those who were killed for idolatry. But the Lord accepts not so much the things that are offered as the will of those who offer them.

paras.t: Et portastis tabernaculum factum a Moyse per manum artificum electorum, Moloch regi vestro, id est ad honorem idoli vestri. Moloch autem fuit idolum Ammonitarum: quod interpretatur rex, significatque Luciferum, seu stellam matutinam, quam multi Sarracenorum usque nunc colunt, quia præ ceteris videtur splendidior, major et mirabilior. Portastis quoque et imaginem idolorum vestrorum, videlicet sidus dei vestri, id est imaginem astri seu stellæ matutinæ, quam coluistis pro Deo, quæ idola fecistis vobis ad adorandum ea, et ad vestram ruinam. Ejusdem autem falsi dei habuerunt plures imagines, quilibet scilicet suam.
paras.en: [[5:26|you carried a tabernacle|Et portastis tabernaculum]], made by Moses through the hands of chosen craftsmen, [[5:26|for your Moloch|Moloch regi vestro]] [Denis's text reads *Moloch regi vestro*, "for Moloch your king"], that is, in honour of your idol. Now Moloch was the idol of the Ammonites; the name is interpreted *king*, and it signifies Lucifer, or the morning star, which many of the Saracens worship to this day, because it seems brighter, greater and more wonderful than the others. You carried also [[5:26|the image of your idols|et imaginem idolorum vestrorum]], namely [[5:26|the star of your god|sidus dei vestri]], that is, the image of a star, the morning star, which you worshipped as God, [[5:26|which you made to yourselves|quæ idola fecistis vobis]] to adore them, and to your own ruin. And they had several images of the same false god, each man, that is, his own.

paras.t: Præterea huic expositioni alii apparenter objiciunt, quod idololatræ adoratores vituli, fuerunt in deserto prostrati, similiter illi qui adoraverunt Beelphegor. Ideo non apparet quod alii tanto tempore venerabantur idola, vel secum tulerint ea, præsertim quum nulla inde in libris Moysis mentio fiat. Rursus, in fabricatione arcæ et tabernaculi, filii Israel multa Deo devota promptaque mente obtulisse leguntur in Exodo. In libro quoque Numerorum aliqua Deo immolasse leguntur, videlicet duodecim principes in dedicatione tabernaculi. Et in consecratione Aaron filiorumque ejus sacrificia offerebantur. Hi ergo exponunt prædicta hoc modo, quod filii Israel in deserto non obtulerunt hostias Deo secundum legis præcepta, sicut nec circumcidebatur, quia in utroque Deus per Moysen dispensavit cum eis. Istud vero non sic intelligitur, quod nullas penitus obtulerunt hostias, sed quia tam paucas et raras, quod non reputatur. Quod enim modicum est, pro nihilo æstimatur. Huic dicto videtur favere, quod Dominus ait in Jeremia: Non sum locutus cum patribus vestris, nec præcepi eis in die qua eduxi vos de terra Ægypti, de verbo holocautomatum, etc.
paras.en: Moreover, others plausibly object to this exposition that the idolaters who worshipped the calf were struck down in the desert[[Ex 32:27||]][[Ex 32:28||]][[Num 14:36||]][[Num 14:37||]][[Heb 3:17||]], and likewise those who worshipped Beelphegor[[Num 25:9||]]. Hence it does not appear that the others worshipped idols for so long a time, or carried them about with them, especially since no mention of it is made in the books of Moses. Again, at the making of the ark and the tabernacle, the children of Israel are read in Exodus to have offered many things to God with devout and ready mind[[Ex 36:3||]]. In the book of Numbers too some are read to have sacrificed to God, namely the twelve princes at the dedication of the tabernacle. And at the consecration of Aaron and his sons sacrifices were offered[[Lev 8:1||]]. These, then, expound the words in this way: that the children of Israel in the desert did not offer victims to God according to the precepts of the Law, just as there was no circumcising either, since in both God dispensed them through Moses. This is not to be understood as if they offered no victims at all, but that they offered so few and so seldom that it is not counted; for what is very little is reckoned as nothing. In favour of this saying seems to be what the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 7:22|I spoke not to your fathers, and I commanded them not, in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt|Non sum locutus cum patribus vestris, nec præcepi eis in die qua eduxi vos de terra Ægypti]], [[Jer 7:22|concerning the matter of burnt offerings|de verbo holocautomatum]], etc.

paras.t: Porro quod subditur, Et portastis tabernaculum Moloch regi vestro, etc., non referunt ad verba immediate præcedentia, nec ad quadraginta annos in solitudine, sed ad ea quæ paulo ante præhabita sunt de terrore diei Domini. Ut sit sensus: Quia tam horribilis erit dies vestræ captivitatis, et tanta mala fecistis, ideo et portastis, id est portabitis, tabernaculum Moloch regi vestro. Dicunt enim, quod Assyrii posuerunt idola decem tribuum super collum earum, quando in captivitatem eas ducebant: ut sic appareret, quod dii earum eis prodesse non poterant contra Assyrios.
paras.en: Then what follows, [[5:26|But you carried a tabernacle for your Moloch|Et portastis tabernaculum Moloch regi vestro]], etc., they do not refer to the words immediately before, nor to the forty years in the wilderness, but to what was said a little earlier about the terror of the day of the Lord. So that the sense is: Because the day of your captivity will be so horrible, and you have done such great evils, therefore [[5:26|you carried|portastis]], that is, you shall carry, [[5:26|a tabernacle for your Moloch|tabernaculum Moloch regi vestro]]. For they say that the Assyrians put the idols of the ten tribes on their necks when they were leading them into captivity, so that it might thus appear that their gods could not help them against the Assyrians.

paras.t: Et migrare, id est in captivitatem duci, vos faciam trans Damascum, id est ultra Syriam, cujus metropolis est Damascus, usque in Babyloniam. Ducebantur enim per Syriam in Chaldæam. Dicit Dominus per me Amos prophetam suum, Deus exercituum nomen ejus, id est, Deus cælestium agminum, seu Deus omnipotens est nomen ipsius.
paras.en: [[5:27|And I will cause you to go into captivity|Et migrare]], that is, to be led into captivity, [[5:27|beyond Damascus|vos faciam trans Damascum]] [Denis's Latin reads *Et migrare … vos faciam trans Damascum*, "I will make you migrate beyond Damascus"], that is, beyond Syria, whose capital is Damascus, as far as Babylonia: for they were led through Syria into Chaldea. [[5:27|saith the Lord|Dicit Dominus]] through me, Amos his prophet, [[5:27|the God of hosts is his name|Deus exercituum nomen ejus]], that is, God of the heavenly armies, or God almighty, is his name.

paras.t: Hieronymus vero ad suæ expositionis confirmationem adducit verba Stephani in Actibus: Convertit autem Deus et tradidit illos servire militiæ cœli, sicut scriptum est in libro Prophetarum: Numquid victimas et hostias obtulistis mihi quadraginta annis in deserto, filii Israel? Et suscepistis tabernaculum Moloch, et sidus dei vestri Rempham, figuras quas fecistis adorare eas; et transferam vos trans Babylonem. Pro eo quod Amos disseruit, Trans Damascum; Stephanus allegavit, Trans Babylonem, ad sensum potius quam ad verba respiciens. Sensus tamen (ut patuit) redit ad idem.
