Solent namque Christus atque Apostoli, alii quoque majores discipuli, allegare Scripturas veteris Testamenti quantum ad veritatis sententiam, magis quam sequi formam verborum. Per Rempham vero, intelligit præinductum Luciferum.
paras.en: Jerome, however, in confirmation of his exposition, brings forward the words of Stephen in the Acts: [[Acts 7:42|God turned and gave them up to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the books of the prophets|Convertit autem Deus et tradidit illos servire militiæ cœli, sicut scriptum est in libro Prophetarum]]: [[Acts 7:42|Did you offer victims and sacrifices to me for forty years, in the desert, O house of Israel?|Numquid victimas et hostias obtulistis mihi quadraginta annis in deserto, filii Israel?]] [Denis's text reads *filii Israel*, "O children of Israel"]. [[Acts 7:43|And you took unto you the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Rempham, figures which you made to adore them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon|Et suscepistis tabernaculum Moloch, et sidus dei vestri Rempham, figuras quas fecistis adorare eas; et transferam vos trans Babylonem]]. Where Amos set down [[5:27|beyond Damascus|Trans Damascum]], Stephen cited [[Acts 7:43|beyond Babylon|Trans Babylonem]], looking to the sense rather than to the words. Yet the sense (as has been shown) comes to the same. For Christ and the Apostles, and other greater disciples too, are accustomed to cite the Scriptures of the Old Testament according to the meaning of their truth, rather than to follow the form of the words. And by Rempham he understands the Lucifer spoken of above.

paras.t: Postremo, quæ harum expositionum sit verior, et qualiter concordari possit una cum alia, sapientis lectoris committo judicio.
paras.en: Lastly, which of these expositions is the truer, and how one can be reconciled with the other, I leave to the judgment of the wise reader.

paras.t: Loquens demum sanctus Propheta in persona cujuslibet viri perfecti seu virtuosi, Deum proximumque ardenter amantis, et de errore ac vitiis proximorum, magis autem de divinæ majestatis inhonoratione, cordialiter contristati, ait: Audite verbum istud, quod ego levo super vos, o impœnitentes et duri, excæcati, et periculose securi, planctum: id est, lamentabilem sermonem, quem de vestra transgressione ac damnatione enuntio, auscultate, ut et propria pericula attendentes, cessetis inaniter gloriari, discatisque vos ipsos deflere. Talis fuit Paulus, qui ait: Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? Quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror? Itemque Psalmista, qui profitetur: Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei. Sic deflentur, qui ignorant cur defleantur: qui tanto miserabiliores sunt, quo suam infelicitatem minus cognoscunt, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi alicui dicitur: Quomodo dicis, Quia dives sum, et nescis quia tu es miser, et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus, et nudus?
paras.en: Lastly the holy Prophet, speaking in the person of any perfect or virtuous man who loves God and his neighbour ardently and is grieved to the heart at the error and vices of his neighbours, but still more at the dishonour done to the divine majesty, says: [[5:1|Hear ye this word, which I take up concerning you|Audite verbum istud, quod ego levo super vos]], O you impenitent and hard of heart, blinded and dangerously secure, [[5:1|for a lamentation|planctum]]: that is, hearken to the mournful discourse which I utter concerning your transgression and damnation, so that, attending to your own dangers, you may cease to glory in vain and may learn to weep for yourselves. Such was Paul, who says: [[2 Cor 11:29|Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not on fire?|Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? Quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror?]] And such too the Psalmist, who declares: [[Ps 118:139|My zeal hath made me pine away: because my enemies forgot thy words|Tabescere me fecit zelus meus, quia obliti sunt verba tua inimici mei]] Thus they are wept over who do not know why they are wept over; and they are the more wretched the less they know their unhappiness, as is said to someone in the Apocalypse: How sayest thou, [[Apoc 3:17|I am rich|Quia dives sum]], [[Apoc 3:17|and knowest not that thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|et nescis quia tu es miser, et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus, et nudus?]]?

paras.t: Domus Israel, id est Ecclesia, cecidit, peccando, et a primitivo suo fervore multum deficiendo, ab altitudine perfectionis ruendo, et quæ sua sunt, non quæ Christi, quærendo. Non adjiciet ut resurgat. Hoc, quantum ad recidivantes, impœnitentes et reprobos, certum est: de quibus dicit Apostolus, Impii proficient in pejus. Et hoc diabolicum est, quia in malo perseverare, dæmoniacum rite censetur. Ideo dicit Scriptura: Non tardes converti ad Dominum, et ne differas de die in diem: subito enim veniet ira illius.
paras.en: [[5:1|The house of Israel|Domus Israel]], that is, the Church, [[5:1|is fallen|cecidit]]: by sinning, by falling far short of her first fervour, by tumbling from the height of perfection, and by seeking [[Phil 2:21|the things that are their own not the things that are Jesus Christ's|quæ sua sunt, non quæ Christi]]. [[5:1|And it shall rise no more|Non adjiciet ut resurgat]]. This is certain as regards the relapsing, the impenitent and the reprobate, of whom the Apostle says: The wicked [[2 Tim 3:13|shall grow worse and worse|proficient in pejus]]. And this is devilish, for to persevere in evil is rightly accounted demonic. Therefore the Scripture says: [[Ecclus 5:8|Delay not to be converted to the Lord, and defer it not from day to day|Non tardes converti ad Dominum, et ne differas de die in diem]]: [[Ecclus 5:9|For his wrath shall come on a sudden|subito enim veniet ira illius]].

paras.t: Virgo Israel, id est anima quondam contemplativa, vel fide et caritate Deo sponsata, et animi integritate præfulgida, projecta est in terram suam, id est in legem peccati, et carne allecta, in carnales concupiscentias devoluta, et sensualitati subjecta, dæmonibus subdita. Tali animæ loquitur Isaias: Excutere de pulvere; et Apostolus, Quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram. Denique, Beati mites, quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram. Non est qui suscitet eam propria potestate a somno peccati, a torpore acediæ, a gravamine culpæ, nisi ipse Deus eam medullitus tangat, afficiat, et convertat. Aliter enim in vanum foris prædicatur, nisi Spiritus Sanctus intus per unctionem loquatur. Eum quoque quem despicit Deus, corrigere nullus potest. Quod specialiter de hæreticis verum est. Propter quod ad Titum scribit Apostolus: Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita, sciens quia subversus est, qui hujusmodi est, et delinquit proprio judicio condemnatus.
paras.en: [[5:2|The virgin of Israel|Virgo Israel]], that is, the soul once contemplative, or espoused to God by faith and charity and shining with integrity of mind, [[5:2|is cast down upon her land|projecta est in terram suam]], that is, into the law of sin: enticed by the flesh, rolled down into carnal concupiscences, made subject to sensuality, subdued to the demons. To such a soul Isaias says: [[Is 52:2|Shake thyself from the dust|Excutere de pulvere]]; and the Apostle: [[Col 3:2|Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth|Quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram]]. And again: [[Matt 5:4|Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land|Beati mites, quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram]] [in the Latin the same word, *terra*, as the prophet's "her land"]. [[5:2|There is none to raise her up|Non est qui suscitet eam]] by her own power from the sleep of sin, from the torpor of acedia [that is, spiritual sloth, a weariness and sadness toward the things of God], from the weight of guilt, unless God himself touch her to the marrow, move her, and convert her. For otherwise preaching without is in vain, unless the Holy Spirit speak within by his anointing. Moreover, [[Eccles 7:14|no man can correct whom he hath despised|Eum quoque quem despicit Deus, corrigere nullus potest]], that is, God. This is true especially of heretics. That is why the Apostle writes to Titus: [[Tit 3:10|A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid|Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita]]: [[Tit 3:11|Knowing that he that is such an one is subverted and sinneth, being condemned by his own judgment|sciens quia subversus est, qui hujusmodi est, et delinquit proprio judicio condemnatus]].

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus: Urbs de qua egrediebantur mille, relinquentur in ea centum; et de qua egrediebantur centum, relinquentur in ea decem in domo Israel, id est in Ecclesia. Istud cernimus in ea impletum: quia nunc vix pro decima parte tot sunt, qui fide, caritate et opere egrediantur de Ecclesia, de claustris et congregationibus, loquendo de bono egressu, id est virtuoso processu idoneoque profectu, quot olim egredi consueverunt, quando calor sanguinis Christi adhuc fervebat, et operabatur in cordibus Christianorum.
paras.en: [[5:3|thus saith the Lord God: The city, out of which came forth a thousand, there shall be left in it a hundred: and out of which there came a hundred, there shall be left in it ten, in the house of Israel|Hæc dicit Dominus: Urbs de qua egrediebantur mille, relinquentur in ea centum; et de qua egrediebantur centum, relinquentur in ea decem in domo Israel]], that is, in the Church. This we see fulfilled in her: for now there are scarcely a tenth part as many who go forth from the Church, from cloisters and congregations, by faith, charity and work (speaking of a good going forth, that is, of virtuous advance and fitting progress), as once were wont to go forth, when the heat of the blood of Christ was still glowing and working in the hearts of Christians.

paras.t: Quia hæc dicit Dominus domui Israel, id est congregationi fidelium: Quærite me, non qualitercumque, sed taliter quomodo dignum et æquum est tale ac tantum bonum quæri, desiderari, rogare, utpote jugiter et ferventer, imo pro posse tanto instantius atque ferventius, quanto infinitum bonum, omni bono finito desiderabilius amabiliusque consistit, et vivetis per gratiam: de qua vita ait Salvator in Joanne, Nisi manducaveritis carnem Filii hominis, non habebitis vitam in vobis. Omnis autem qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur.
paras.en: [[5:4|For thus saith the Lord to the house of Israel|Quia hæc dicit Dominus domui Israel]], that is, to the congregation of the faithful: [[5:4|Seek ye me|Quærite me]], not in any manner whatever, but in such a way as it is fitting and right that so great a good be sought, desired and asked for: that is, constantly and fervently, nay, as far as you can, all the more urgently and fervently as the infinite good is more desirable and more lovable than every finite good; [[5:4|and you shall live|et vivetis]] by grace. Of this life the Saviour says in John: [[John 6:54|except you eat the flesh of the Son of man|Nisi manducaveritis carnem Filii hominis]], [[John 6:54|you shall not have life in you|non habebitis vitam in vobis]]. And [[Luke 11:10|every one that asketh receiveth: and he that seeketh findeth: and to him that knocketh it shall be opened|Omnis autem qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur]].

paras.t: Et nolite quærere Bethel, id est accedere eos pro informatione, qui se dicunt nosse Deum, factis autem negant, si tamen convenienter et aptius possitis accedere alios. Bethel interpretatur domus Dei, quæ hoc loco pro sola fide fidelibus sumitur. Et in Galgalam, id est congregationem carnalium, nolite intrare, communicando eorum infructuosis operibus. Galgala autem interpretatur volutabrum, vel revelatio.
paras.en: [[5:5|But seek not Bethel|Et nolite quærere Bethel]]: that is, do not go for instruction to those who say they know God, [[Tit 1:16|but in their works they deny him|factis autem negant]], provided you can conveniently and more suitably go to others. Bethel is interpreted *house of God*, which here is taken for those who are faithful by faith alone. [[5:5|into Galgal|Et in Galgalam]], that is, into the congregation of the carnal, [[5:5|go not|nolite intrare]], by sharing in their unfruitful works. Now Galgala is interpreted *wallowing-place*, or *revelation*.

paras.t: Quærite Dominum, ne forte comburatur ut ignis domus Joseph, id est, ne Ecclesia, quæ dicere potest illud in Psalmo, Improperia improperantium tibi ceciderunt super me, confundatur, vel igne concupiscentiæ accendatur, aut flamma damnationis tartareæ torqueatur. Joseph vero interpretatur opprobrium, vel absque opprobrio. Qui convertitis in absinthium judicium Domini. Hoc juxta sensum præhabitum competit omnibus qui vel se ipsos, vel alios irrationabiliter judicant: quo amaritudinem sibi infernalem mercantur.
paras.en: [[5:6|Seek ye the Lord|Quærite Dominum]], [[5:6|lest the house of Joseph be burnt with fire|ne forte comburatur ut ignis domus Joseph]]: that is, lest the Church, which can say that word in the Psalm, [[Ps 68:10|the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me|Improperia improperantium tibi ceciderunt super me]][[Rom 15:3||]] [Denis's wording is that of Rom 15:3, where the Apostle quotes the Psalm], be put to confusion, or be kindled with the fire of concupiscence, or be tormented in the flame of hellish damnation. Joseph is interpreted *reproach*, or *without reproach*. [[5:7|You that turn judgment into wormwood|Qui convertitis in absinthium judicium]], the judgment of the Lord. According to the sense given above, this fits all who judge themselves or others unreasonably, whereby they purchase for themselves the bitterness of hell.

paras.t: Facientem Arcturum et Orionem. Per Arcturum, qui septem sideribus constat, et volvitur circa polum, designatur Ecclesia septemplici dono Spiritus Sancti ornata. Cujus tota intentio, cursus et actio circa Deum versatur, tanquam circa immobile bonum. Per Orionem quoque qui hieme oritur, et tempestates inducit, martyres figurantur, qui tempore infidelitatis, quasi in hieme prædicant: per quod contra se tempestates persecutionum mox provocant. Hunc ergo Arcturum et Orionem facit Deus omnipotens, a quo est omne esse naturæ et gratiæ universorum credentium.
paras.en: [[5:8|him that maketh Arcturus, and Orion|Facientem Arcturum et Orionem]]. By Arcturus, which consists of seven stars and turns about the pole, is signified the Church adorned with the sevenfold gift of the Holy Spirit, whose whole intention, course and action turns about God as about the unmoving good. By Orion, which rises in winter and brings on storms, are figured the martyrs, who preach in a time of unbelief, as it were in winter, and thereby soon stir up against themselves the storms of persecution. This Arcturus and Orion, then, almighty God makes, from whom is all the being, of nature and of grace, of all believers.

paras.t: Qui convertit mane in tenebras, dum prosperis succedunt adversa, ut illuminationi et consolationi internæ, excæcatio et afflictio cordis: dum scilicet Deus gratiam subtrahit, quo facto, aurora mentis in vitiorum convertitur nebulas. Et diem in noctem mutat, dum viros sapientes et virtuosos sinit cadere, et animi caliginem detestandam incurrere. Propter quod monet Apostolus: Qui stat, videat ne cadat. Qui vocat aquas, id est gratiam et doctrinam, maris, id est eorum qui in hoc mundo lacrimis et pœnitentiæ vacant, vel hominum perfectorum, qui velut mare abundant unda sapientiæ salutaris, et gurgite multiformis gratiæ Sancti Spiritus, et effundit eas super faciem terræ, id est, terrenis carnalibusque hominibus aquas istas annuntiat atque communicat, eos instruendo et convertendo per prædicationes justorum. Quod præsertim factum est prædicantibus sanctis Apostolis, qui aquis his omne sæculum irrigaverunt in tantum, ut in Isaia scriptum sit atque prædictum: Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes.
paras.en: [[5:8|that turneth|Qui convertit]] the morning into darkness [so Denis reads it; the Vulgate has *convertentem in mane tenebras*, "that turneth darkness into morning"]: when adversity follows prosperity, as blindness and affliction of heart follow inward light and consolation; that is, when God withdraws his grace, whereupon the dawn of the mind is turned into the fogs of vice. [[5:8|and that changeth day into night|Et diem in noctem mutat]], when he lets wise and virtuous men fall and incur a detestable darkness of soul. That is why the Apostle warns: He that standeth, [[1 Cor 10:12|let him take heed lest he fall|videat ne cadat]]. [[5:8|that calleth the waters|Qui vocat aquas]], that is, grace and doctrine, [[5:8|of the sea|maris]], that is, of those who in this world give themselves to tears and penance, or of perfect men, who like the sea abound in the wave of saving wisdom and in the flood of the manifold grace of the Holy Spirit, [[5:8|and poureth them out upon the face of the earth|et effundit eas super faciem terræ]]: that is, he announces and imparts these waters to earthly and carnal men, instructing and converting them through the preaching of the just. This was done above all when the holy Apostles preached, who watered the whole world with these waters, so much so that it is written and foretold in Isaias: [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea|Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes]].

paras.t: Qui subridet, id est, cum risu minatur, vastitatem super robustum, id est potentibus sæculi, de quibus fatetur: Ego in interitu vestro ridebo; et, Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos.
paras.en: [[5:9|He that with a smile|Qui subridet]], that is, threatens with laughter, [[5:9|bringeth destruction upon the strong|vastitatem super robustum]], that is, upon the mighty of the world, of whom he declares: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction|Ego in interitu vestro ridebo]]; and: [[Ps 2:4|He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them|Qui habitat in cœlis, irridebit eos]] [the margin gives Ps. xi, 4, a misreading of ii, 4].

paras.t: Odio habuerunt in porta corripientem. De duplici porta tractat Scriptura: Una vocatur porta vitæ; alia vero, porta mortis ac inferi. Porta mortis, peccatum; porta vitæ, virtus et gratia seu actio meritoria. Odio autem habetur justus consistens in porta virtutum, si corripit malum qui est in porta mortis ac vitiorum. Quod maxime competit Judæis persecutoribus Christi, quibus gravis erat etiam ad videndum. Propter quod ait: Odio habuerunt me et Patrem meum.
paras.en: [[5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh in the gate|Odio habuerunt in porta corripientem]]. Scripture treats of a twofold gate: one is called the gate of life, the other the gate of death and of hell. The gate of death is sin; the gate of life is virtue and grace, or meritorious action. Now the just man standing in the gate of the virtues is hated if he rebukes the wicked man who is in the gate of death and of the vices. This fits above all the Jews who persecuted Christ, to whom he was grievous even to behold[[Wis 2:15||]]. That is why he says: They have [[John 15:24|hated both me and my Father|Odio habuerunt me et Patrem meum]].

paras.t: Pro eo quod diripiebatis pauperem, id est, innocentes et simplices subvertistis, o corruptores animarum, verbo et exemplo seu comminatione aut adulatione, et prædam electam tollebatis ab eo, id est, gratia Dei hujusmodi spoliastis (Innocens enim credit omni verbo; et, Deridetur justi simplicitas); domos quadro lapide ædificabitis, id est, collectionem discipulorum vestrorum, ornatu verborum et sapientiæ vanæ, apparenti quodam decore firmabitis, et non habitabitis in eis, id est, simul cum illis in æternum peribitis, nec diu durabit cohabitatio et condelectatio vestra in sæculo isto. Vineas amantissimas, id est documenta vobis suavia et prædilecta, plantabitis in cordibus vestris et discipulorum, et non bibetis vinum earum, id est, nullum fructum percipietis ex illis, et delectatio durans ad horam, sempiterno commutabitur cruciatu. De talibus dicitur in Jeremia: Ecce ego cibabo populum istum absinthio, et potum dabo ei aquam fellis. Imo pœna pereuntium discipulorum redundabit in caput infelicium magistrorum, qui pro tot torquebuntur, quot seduxerunt.
paras.en: [[5:11|because you robbed the poor|Pro eo quod diripiebatis pauperem]], that is, you have overthrown the innocent and simple, O corrupters of souls, by word and example, or by threats or flattery, [[5:11|and took the choice prey from him|et prædam electam tollebatis ab eo]], that is, you have despoiled such men of the grace of God (for [[Prov 14:15|The innocent believeth every word|Innocens enim credit omni verbo]]; and: [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur justi simplicitas]]); [[5:11|you shall build houses with square stone|domos quadro lapide ædificabitis]], that is, you will establish the gathering of your disciples with the adornment of words and of vain wisdom, with a certain show of beauty, [[5:11|and shall not dwell in them|et non habitabitis in eis]], that is, you will perish with them for ever, and your dwelling together and delighting together in this world will not last long. [[5:11|most delightful vineyards|Vineas amantissimas]], that is, teachings sweet and dear to you, [[5:11|you shall plant|plantabitis]] in your own hearts and in those of your disciples, [[5:11|and shall not drink the wine of them|et non bibetis vinum earum]], that is, you will gather no fruit from them, and a delight that lasts an hour will be exchanged for everlasting torment. Of such it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:15|Behold I will feed this people with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink|Ecce ego cibabo populum istum absinthio, et potum dabo ei aquam fellis]]. Nay, the punishment of the disciples who perish will redound upon the head of their unhappy masters, who will be tormented for as many as they have led astray.

paras.t: Ideo prudens in tempore illo tacebit, quia tempus malum est. Unde ad Timotheum dicit Apostolus: Veniet tempus in quo sanam doctrinam non recipient, sed coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus. Denique tempus loquendi, et tempus tacendi. Dum enim non speratur emendatio, sed potius formidatur induratio delinquentis, prudens tacebit: maxime, si non sit prælatus aut judex, nec bonum commune periclitetur. Ideo dicit Psalmista: Obmutui et humiliatus sum, et silui a bonis. Hinc in Ecclesiastico legitur: Est tacens, qui invenitur sapiens; et est odibilis, qui procax est ad loquendum. Est autem tacens, non habens sensum loquelæ; et est tacens, sciens tempus aptum.
paras.en: [[5:13|Therefore the prudent shall keep silence at that time, for it is an evil time|Ideo prudens in tempore illo tacebit, quia tempus malum est]]. Hence the Apostle says to Timothy: The time will come [[2 Tim 4:3|when they will not endure sound doctrine|in quo sanam doctrinam non recipient]], but [[2 Tim 4:3|will heap to themselves teachers having itching ears|coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus]]. And again: [[Eccles 3:7|a time to speak|tempus loquendi]], and [[Eccles 3:7|a time to keep silence|tempus tacendi]]. For when amendment is not hoped for, but rather the hardening of the offender is feared, the prudent man will keep silence: above all if he is not a prelate or a judge, and the common good is not endangered. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 38:3|I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things|Obmutui et humiliatus sum, et silui a bonis]]. Hence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 20:5|There is one that holdeth his peace, that is found wise: and there is another that is hateful, that is bold in speech|Est tacens, qui invenitur sapiens; et est odibilis, qui procax est ad loquendum]]. [[Ecclus 20:6|There is one that holdeth his peace, because he knoweth not what to say: and there is another that holdeth his peace, knowing the proper time|Est autem tacens, non habens sensum loquelæ; et est tacens, sciens tempus aptum]].

paras.t: Constituite in porta, id est in operatione qua itur ad ultimum finem, judicium discretionis, ut sine consilio nil agatis, et proprios actus dijudicetis, atque in omnibus pretiosum a vili secernatis. Propter quod docet Apostolus: Sine præjudicio nihil facias, in alteram partem declinando. Tale quippe judicium diligit honor regis, estque præparatio sedis ejus, et liberat a judicio supplicioque gehennæ.
paras.en: [[5:15|establish|Constituite]] [[5:15|in the gate|in porta]], that is, in the working by which one goes to the last end, [[5:15|judgment|judicium]] of discretion, so that you may do [[Ecclus 32:24|nothing without counsel|sine consilio nil agatis]], and may judge your own acts, and in all things [[Jer 15:19|separate the precious from the vile|pretiosum a vili secernatis]]. That is why the Apostle teaches: Act [[1 Tim 5:21|without prejudice|Sine præjudicio]], [[1 Tim 5:21|doing nothing by declining to either side|nihil facias, in alteram partem declinando]]. For [[Ps 98:4|the king's honour loveth judgment|diligit honor regis]] such as this, and it is [[Ps 88:15|the preparation of thy throne|præparatio sedis ejus]] [the Psalm has "thy throne"; Denis says "his"], and it delivers from the judgment and punishment of hell.

paras.t: In omnibus plateis, id est latis viis quæ ducunt ad mortem, planctus: quia de talibus est plangendum, et ducunt ad planctum de quo ait Salvator: Ibi erit fletus, et stridor dentium, etc. Et in cunctis quæ foris sunt, id est adulterinis delectationibus, quæ metas rationis excedunt, dicetur, Væ, væ: id est, pœna atque damnatio animæ et corporis pro illis reddentur, quemadmodum scriptum est in Apocalypsi: Quantum in deliciis fuit, tantum date illi luctum et tormentum; itemque: Væ vobis qui habetis nunc consolationem vestram, quia plorabitis et flebitis. Et vocabunt agricolam, id est proprii cordis diligentem custodem ac purgatorem, ad luctum, ut lugeat aliorum facinora; et ad planctum piæ compassionis, eos qui sciunt plangere, id est homines internos, compunctos, misericordes, gratiam lacrimarum habentes. Hoc fit, dum vir ecclesiasticus sua exhortatione tales inducit ad lacrimandum pro piis causis, videlicet quod Deus a multis tam modice curatur, imo tam vehementer inhonoratur, quod status Ecclesiæ a pristino fervore prolabitur, quod tot mala contingunt quotidie.
paras.en: [[5:16|In every street|In omnibus plateis]], that is, in the broad ways that lead to death, [[5:16|there shall be wailing|planctus]]: for such are to be wailed over, and they lead to the wailing of which the Saviour says: [[Matt 8:12|there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth|Ibi erit fletus, et stridor dentium]][[Matt 13:42||]], etc. [[5:16|and in all places that are without|Et in cunctis quæ foris sunt]], that is, in adulterous delights which pass the bounds of reason, [[5:16|they shall say: Alas, alas|dicetur, Væ, væ]]: that is, punishment and damnation of soul and body shall be rendered for them, as it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 18:7|As much as|Quantum]] she [[Apoc 18:7|lived in delicacies|in deliciis fuit]], [[Apoc 18:7|so much torment and sorrow give ye to her|tantum date illi luctum et tormentum]]; and again: [[Luke 6:24|woe to you|Væ vobis]] who now [[Luke 6:24|have your consolation|habetis nunc consolationem vestram]], for [[Luke 6:25|you shall mourn and weep|plorabitis et flebitis]] [Denis joins two verses of Luke]. [[5:16|And they shall call the husbandman|Et vocabunt agricolam]], that is, the diligent keeper and cleanser of his own heart, [[5:16|to mourning|ad luctum]], that he may mourn the crimes of others; [[5:16|to lament|et ad planctum]] in loving compassion, [[5:16|such as are skilful in lamentation|eos qui sciunt plangere]], that is, men who live inwardly, compunct, merciful, having the grace of tears. This is done when a churchman by his exhortation leads such men to weep for holy causes: namely, that God is so little cared for by many, nay, so grievously dishonoured; that the state of the Church is slipping from its first fervour; that so many evils happen daily.

paras.t: Væ desiderantibus diem Domini, id est diem mortis vel futuri judicii. Hoc applicandum est incautis, et sanctis in propriis oculis, qui de sua justitia nimis confidunt, qui divinæ justitiæ rigorem non pensant, nec propriam fragilitatem efficaciter ponderantes, dicunt se mori paratos, velle dissolvi, et ad audiendam sententiam Judicis rite dispositos. Verum justus in omnibus metuit; et quoniam nescit an amore sit dignus, merito jugiter expavescit. Nec tutum est faciliter tantam securitatem admittere: præsertim quia tunc erunt securi, qui modo non sunt securi; et iterum tunc timebunt, qui jam timere nolunt. Dies Domini ista, tenebræ, et non lux, id est, amaritudine plena est talibus: qui utique fallunt se ipsos, et nequaquam effugere poterunt.
paras.en: [[5:18|Woe to them that desire the day of the Lord|Væ desiderantibus diem Domini]], that is, the day of death or of the judgment to come. This is to be applied to the incautious, and to those holy in their own eyes, who trust too much in their own justice, who do not weigh the rigour of divine justice, and, not weighing their own frailty to any purpose, say that they are ready to die, that they wish [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved|dissolvi]], and that they are duly prepared to hear the sentence of the Judge. But the just man [[Ecclus 18:27|will fear in every thing|in omnibus metuit]] [Ecclesiasticus says "a wise man"]; and since [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love|nescit an amore sit dignus]], he rightly stands in constant dread. Nor is it safe to admit so great a security lightly: above all because then they shall be secure who now are not secure, and again then they shall fear who now will not fear. [[5:18|the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light|Dies Domini ista, tenebræ, et non lux]]: that is, it is full of bitterness for such men, who indeed deceive themselves and will in no way be able to escape.

paras.t: Et festivitates vestras, etc. Christianorum qui festis diebus vitiis carnis, ludis et vanitatibus vacant, et plus solito peccant, solennitates despicit Deus. Non enim veraciter solennizant, quoniam Deo reverenter non adstant, nec diem expendunt in actibus sanctis celebriter. Et non capiam odorem cœtuum vestrorum. Preces enim et hostiæ atque obsequia talium, fœtore sunt plenæ, quum oriantur ex turpissimo fonte, puta ex anima mortalibus culpis obnoxia. Talium sacrificia et cantica non respicit Deus ex parte offerentium, ut sunt singulares personæ, quamvis sacrificium novæ legis sit per se Deo gratissimum. — Aliorum moralitas innotescit ex præinductis.
paras.en: [[5:21|your festivities|Et festivitates vestras]], etc. God despises the solemnities of Christians who on feast days give themselves to the vices of the flesh, to games and vanities, and sin more than usual. For they do not truly keep the feast, since they do not stand before God with reverence, nor spend the day in holy acts solemnly. [[5:21|and I will not receive the odour of your assemblies|Et non capiam odorem cœtuum vestrorum]]. For the prayers and victims and services of such men are full of stench, since they spring from a most foul source, namely from a soul bound by mortal sins. God does not regard the sacrifices and canticles of such men on the part of the offerers, as they are individual persons [that is, as their own act, *ex opere operantis*], although the sacrifice of the New Law is in itself most pleasing to God. The moral sense of the rest is plain from what has been said above.

6.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli sexti: Væ vobis, qui opulenti estis in Sion.
6.title_en: Literal explanation of the sixth chapter: Woe to you that are wealthy in Sion.

paras.t: Contra avaritiam, voluptatem, atque lasciviam regni Juda ac Israel, loquitur Propheta in hoc capitulo. Væ temporalis captivitatis atque æternæ damnationis debetur et imminet vobis, qui opulenti estis in Sion, id est divites et divitiarum inordinati seu cupidi amatores in regno Juda: quod nomine Sion significatur, quoniam templum et palatium erant in monte Sion sita, in urbe Jerusalem metropolitana Judæ; et confiditis in monte Samariæ, id est in fortitudine regni Israel seu decem tribuum, cujus metropolis fuit Samaria in monte locata. Interdum enim duo hæc regna pacem habuerunt ad invicem: et tunc unum confidebat in alio. Optimates capita populorum, id est principes ac judices vulgi, ingredientes pompatice domum Israel, id est, animose ambulantes in populo, ita ut cordis pompa resplendeat in incessu, quemadmodum in Isaia legitur: Ambulaverunt collo extento, et gradu composito incedebant pedibus suis.
paras.en: In this chapter the Prophet speaks against the avarice, the love of pleasure and the wantonness of the kingdom of Juda and of Israel. The [[6:1|Woe|Væ]] of temporal captivity and of eternal damnation is due, and hangs, [[6:1|to you that are wealthy in Sion|vobis, qui opulenti estis in Sion]], that is, you rich men, inordinate or covetous lovers of riches, in the kingdom of Juda: which is signified by the name of Sion, since the temple and the palace stood on mount Sion, in the city of Jerusalem, the chief city of Juda; [[6:1|and to you that have confidence in the mountain of Samaria|et confiditis in monte Samariæ]], that is, in the strength of the kingdom of Israel or of the ten tribes, whose chief city was Samaria, built upon a mountain. For at times these two kingdoms were at peace with each other, and then the one trusted in the other. [[6:1|ye great men, heads of the people|Optimates capita populorum]], that is, the princes and judges of the common people, [[6:1|that go in with state into the house of Israel|ingredientes pompatice domum Israel]], that is, walking proudly among the people, so that the pomp of the heart shines out in the gait, as we read in Isaias: They [[Is 3:16|have walked with stretched out necks|Ambulaverunt collo extento]], and [[Is 3:16|moved in a set pace|gradu composito incedebant]] with their feet.

paras.t: Transite in Chalanne: quæ secundum Hieronymum est civitas Persidis. Aliqui tamen per Chalanne intelligunt Babyloniam. Et videte urbem seu patriam illam, et ite inde in Emath magnam: quæ nunc Antiochia appellatur, civitas Syriæ; et addit, Magnam, ad differentiam alterius Emath, quæ minor est, et alio nomine dicta est Epiphania, cujus regio vocatur Reblatha, in qua, ut quarto Regum describitur, Nabuchodonosor interfecit filios Sedeciæ regis Juda, cujus ibidem oculos eruit; et descendite in Geth urbem Palæstinorum, id est Philistinorum, et ad optima quæque regna eorum, id est ad ceteras electas urbes prædictarum terrarum, quæ prædictis urbibus designantur; si latior terminus eorum termino vestro est: id est, hoc considerate, utrum terra illorum major sit terra vestra. Quasi dicat, Non, ut quidam exponunt, dummodo consideretur terra Judææ secundum illam latitudinem qua primo data est filiis Israel tempore Josue, et prædicta regna considerentur secundum latitudinem quam habuerunt in principio sui. Postmodum tamen dicuntur magis dilatata et fortificata quam regnum Judæorum, seu duodecim tribuum simul. Et sic ista dicuntur, ad ostendendum magnitudinem beneficii Dei, et ingratitudinem populi.
paras.en: [[6:2|Pass ye over to Chalane|Transite in Chalanne]]: which according to Jerome is a city of Persia. Some, however, understand Chalanne to be Babylonia. [[6:2|and see|Et videte]] that city or country, [[6:2|and go from thence into Emath the great|et ite inde in Emath magnam]]: which is now called Antioch, a city of Syria; and he adds [[6:2|the great|Magnam]] to distinguish it from the other Emath, which is the lesser, and by another name was called Epiphania, whose region is called Reblatha, in which, as is described in the fourth book of Kings, Nabuchodonosor slew the sons of Sedecias king of Juda[[4 Kings 25:6||]], and there put out his eyes[[4 Kings 25:7||]]; [[6:2|and go down into Geth|et descendite in Geth]], the city [[6:2|of the Philistines|Palæstinorum]] [Denis glosses the Vulgate's Palæstini as Philistini], [[6:2|and to all the best kingdoms of these|et ad optima quæque regna eorum]], that is, to the other chosen cities of the aforesaid lands, which are designated by the cities named; [[6:2|if their border be larger than your border|si latior terminus eorum termino vestro est]]: that is, consider this, whether their land be greater than your land. As if to say: No, as some expound it, provided the land of Judæa be considered according to the breadth with which it was first given to the children of Israel in the time of Josue, and the aforesaid kingdoms according to the breadth they had at their beginning. Afterwards, however, they are said to have been more enlarged and strengthened than the kingdom of the Jews, or of the twelve tribes together. And so these things are said to show the greatness of God's benefit and the ingratitude of the people.

paras.t: Qui separati estis, id est in præscientia Dei ab electis divisi, et a præcedentibus patribus temporaliter segregati, in diem malum, id est ad tempus afflictionis, quatenus a Chaldæis et Assyriis dira patiamini tormenta. Unde in Job libro inducitur: In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur, et de furore Omnipotentis bibet; et in Psalmo, Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus, divisi sunt ab ira vultus ejus. Et appropinquatis solio iniquitatis. Hoc tripliciter accipi potest: primo, quod regno et terra sibi concessis abusi sunt; secundo, quod regibus propriis impiis favent in malis, idololatriam et alia vitia exercendo; tertio, quod a regibus Assyriorum et Babylonis statim opprimendi exstiterint.
paras.en: [[6:3|You that are separated|Qui separati estis]], that is, divided from the elect in the foreknowledge of God, and set apart in time from the fathers who went before, [[6:3|unto the evil day|in diem malum]], that is, for a time of affliction, so that you may suffer dire torments from the Chaldeans and the Assyrians. Hence it is said in the book of Job: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur]], [[Job 21:20|and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty|et de furore Omnipotentis bibet]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 54:21|They have defiled his covenant|Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus]], [[Ps 54:22|They are divided by the wrath of his countenance|divisi sunt ab ira vultus ejus]]. [[6:3|and that approach to the throne of iniquity|Et appropinquatis solio iniquitatis]]. This can be taken in three ways: first, that they abused the kingdom and the land granted them; secondly, that they favour their own wicked kings in evil, practising idolatry and other vices; thirdly, that they were soon to be crushed by the kings of the Assyrians and of Babylon.

paras.t: Qui dormitis in lectis eburneis, id est pretiosis de ebore factis. In quo patet, quod divitias suas non pauperibus communicabant, sed inutiliter expendere soliti erant. Et lascivitis in stratis vestris delicatis et mollibus, somno libidinem copulantes, et actum matrimonii non propter prolem ad Dei cultum educandam, vel ad reddendum debitum, sed ob turpissimam delectationem exercentes, aliisque meretriciis voluptatibus in contactu vacantes: quod prorsus damnabile est. Qui comeditis agnum de grege, id est teneras ac delicatissimas carnes agnorum de grege electorum, et vitulos de medio armenti acceptos comeditis, non necessitatem naturæ, sed voluptatem sensualitatis quærentes: quia et ista cibaria luxuriæ præbent materiam.
paras.en: [[6:4|You that sleep upon beds of ivory|Qui dormitis in lectis eburneis]], that is, costly ones made of ivory. From this it is plain that they did not share their riches with the poor, but were wont to spend them uselessly. [[6:4|and are wanton on your couches|Et lascivitis in stratis vestris]], soft and delicate, joining lust to sleep, and performing the act of marriage not for the sake of offspring to be brought up for the worship of God, nor to render the debt [that is, the marriage debt, which each spouse owes the other], but for the sake of the foulest pleasure, and giving themselves up to other harlots' pleasures in touching: which is altogether damnable. [[6:4|that eat the lambs out of the flock|Qui comeditis agnum de grege]], that is, the tender and most delicate flesh of lambs chosen from the flock, [[6:4|and the calves out of the midst of the herd|et vitulos de medio armenti]]: you eat calves taken from the midst of the herd, seeking not what nature needs but the pleasure of the senses: for these foods too give matter for lust.

paras.t: Qui canitis ad vocem psalterii, id est, cum modulatione musici instrumenti sic dicti simul cantatis. Consequenter Propheta mutans personam, et aliis illorum vanitatem demonstrans, adjecit: Sicut David putaverunt se habere vasa, id est instrumenta, cantici, id est musicarum modulationum: hoc est, quemadmodum David laudatur de hoc, quod in divino cultu musicis usus est instrumentis; sic isti reputabant se laudandos de hoc, quod talia habebant ad oblectandum auditum in suis vanitatibus, ludis atque conviviis. Est autem idiomatis Hebræi proprietas, ut omne illud dicatur vas, quod aliquo modo continet aliud: juxta quem modum habetur in Psalmo, Et in eo paravit vasa mortis; et, Ego confitebor tibi in vasis psalmi veritatem tuam, Deus; in Jeremia quoque, Aperuit Dominus thesaurum suum, et protulit vasa iræ suæ.
paras.en: [[6:5|You that sing to the sound of the psaltery|Qui canitis ad vocem psalterii]], that is, who sing together to the melody of the musical instrument so called. Then the Prophet, changing the person and pointing out their vanity to others, added: [[6:5|like David|Sicut David]] [[6:5|they have thought themselves to have instruments|putaverunt se habere vasa]] [the Latin vasa is literally “vessels”], that is, instruments, [[6:5|of music|cantici]], that is, of musical melodies: that is, just as David is praised because he used musical instruments in the worship of God[[2 Kings 6:15||]][[1 Par 13:8||]][[1 Par 15:16||]] [the margin gives II Reg. vi, 15; I Par. xiii, 8; xv, with the last verse number lost; 1 Par 15:16 fits], so these men reckoned themselves worthy of praise because they had such things to delight the ear in their vanities, games and banquets. Now it is a property of the Hebrew idiom that everything that in any way contains something else is called a vessel: in which way we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 7:14|And in it he hath prepared to instruments of death|Et in eo paravit vasa mortis]]; and: [[Ps 70:22|I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery|Ego confitebor tibi in vasis psalmi veritatem tuam]], [[Ps 70:22|O God|Deus]]; and in Jeremias too: [[Jer 50:25|The Lord hath opened his armoury, and hath brought forth the weapons of his wrath|Aperuit Dominus thesaurum suum, et protulit vasa iræ suæ]] [in each of these the Latin has vasa, “vessels”, where the Douay-Rheims has “instruments” or “weapons”].

paras.t: Bibentes vinum in phialis, id est in vasis seu scyphis pretiosis, non ad reficiendum, sed deliciandum, et optimo unguento delibuti, id est uncti, non contenti oleo puro pro corporalis doloris seu laboris mitigatione, sed pretioso unguento utentes pro carnis suæ bono odore. Sicque in omnibus superfluitatem secuti sunt, divitiis abutendo. Et nihil patiebantur super contritione Joseph, id est, vastitati et destructioni populi decem tribuum non condoluerunt, vulgum despicientes tanquam jumenta. Viscera enim impiorum crudelia.
paras.en: [[6:6|That drink wine in bowls|Bibentes vinum in phialis]], that is, in costly vessels or cups, not to refresh themselves but for delight, [[6:6|and anoint themselves with the best ointments|et optimo unguento delibuti]], that is, anointed, not content with pure oil to ease bodily pain or toil, but using costly ointment for the sweet smell of their flesh. And so in all things they pursued superfluity, abusing their riches. [[6:6|and they are not concerned for the affliction of Joseph|Et nihil patiebantur super contritione Joseph]], that is, they did not grieve over the wasting and destruction of the people of the ten tribes, despising the common people as beasts. For [[Prov 12:10|the bowels of the wicked are cruel|Viscera enim impiorum crudelia]].

paras.t: Quapropter nunc migrabunt, id est, ob vitia memorata statim captivi ducentur ab Assyriis seu Chaldæis, optimates principesque præfati, in capite transmigrantium, id est in principio populi capti, qui transferentur ad terram alienam: ita quod principes primi erunt inter captivos, quatenus qui primi fuerunt in culpis, sint primi in pœnis, et potentes potenter tormenta patiantur; et auferetur factio lascivientium, id est, finem habebit operatio lascivorum luxuriantium prædictorum.
paras.en: [[6:7|Wherefore now they shall go captive|Quapropter nunc migrabunt]], that is, for the vices mentioned the aforesaid great men and princes shall soon be led captive by the Assyrians or the Chaldeans, [[6:7|at the head of them that go into captivity|in capite transmigrantium]], that is, at the front of the captive people who shall be carried off to a foreign land: so that the princes shall be first among the captives, in order that those who were first in guilt may be first in punishment; and [[Wis 6:7|the mighty shall be mightily tormented|potentes potenter tormenta patiantur]]; [[6:7|and the faction of the luxurious ones shall be taken away|et auferetur factio lascivientium]], that is, the doings of the aforesaid wanton revellers shall have an end.

paras.t: Juravit, id est, irrevocabiliter statuit, Dominus in anima sua, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum, id est in se ipso, seu affectu et zelo interno. Non quod Deus in propria natura habeat animam, sed loquitur more et affectu humano. Nec mirum si animam habere dicatur, qui corporis membra, aures, ventrem, oculos, manus et pedes habere asseritur, per quæ divinæ efficientiæ diversitas designatur. Sic quoque ait per Jeremiam: Numquid super his non visitabo, et in gente hujuscemodi non ulciscetur anima mea? et per Isaiam, Festivitates vestras odivit anima mea. Imo alibi scriptum est: Juravit Dominus per animam suam. Jurat autem hoc loco Dominus, ut duros et incredulos terreat. Detestor ego superbiam Jacob, id est duodecim tribuum. Odibilis enim coram Deo et hominibus est superbia; et, Superbis Deus resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam. Propter quod in Isaia sciscitatur: Super quem requiescet spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? Et domos ejus, id est familiam populi hujus, odi, quantum ad culpam. Odio nempe sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Et tradam civitatem Jerusalem vel Samariam, vel generaliter civitates utriusque regni, cum habitatoribus suis manibus hostium.
paras.en: [[6:8|The Lord God hath sworn|Juravit]], that is, has irrevocably decreed, [[6:8|by his own soul, saith the Lord the God of hosts|Dominus in anima sua, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum]], that is, in himself, or with inward affection and zeal. Not that God in his own nature has a soul, but he speaks after the manner and feeling of men. Nor is it strange that he should be said to have a soul, who is declared to have the members of a body, ears, belly, eyes, hands and feet, by which the diversity of God's working is signified. So too he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 5:29|Shall I not visit for these things|Numquid super his non visitabo]], [[Jer 5:29|or shall not my soul take revenge on such a nation?|et in gente hujuscemodi non ulciscetur anima mea]]? and through Isaias: [[Is 1:14|My soul hateth your new moons, and your solemnities|Festivitates vestras odivit anima mea]]. Indeed it is written elsewhere: [[Jer 51:14|The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself|Juravit Dominus per animam suam]] [the Latin is per animam suam, “by his soul”]. And the Lord swears here to strike fear into the hard and unbelieving. [[6:8|I detest the pride of Jacob|Detestor ego superbiam Jacob]], that is, of the twelve tribes. For [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful before God and men|Odibilis enim coram Deo et hominibus est superbia]]; and: [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Superbis Deus resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]][[1 Pet 5:5||]]. For which reason he asks in Isaias: Upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon him that is quiet and humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the margin gives “Cf. Is. lxvi, 1, 2”; Denis's wording is an older form of Is 66:2, which in the Vulgate reads “to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little”]. [[6:8|his houses|Et domos ejus]], that is, the household of this people, [[6:8|I hate|odi]], as to their guilt. For [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio nempe sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]. [[6:8|and I will deliver up the city|Et tradam civitatem]] of Jerusalem or of Samaria, or in general the cities of both kingdoms, [[6:8|with the inhabitants thereof|cum habitatoribus suis]], into the hands of the enemy.

paras.t: Quod si reliqui fuerint, id est remanserint, decem viri in domo una, evadentes occulte manus Assyriorum, seu Chaldæorum, et ipsi morientur in loco suæ absconsionis, fame, fumo, seu peste. Et tollet eum, id est unumquemque defunctorum illorum, propinquus suus, qui cum eo habitavit, vel vicinus, et comburet eum, id est cadavera exstincta, ut efferat ossa de domo ad tumulum: quia præ multitudine morientium, non sibi vacabit integra corpora ferre ad monumentum. Et dicet combustor ei qui in penetralibus domus est, id est locis interioribus; Numquid adhuc est penes te aliquis mortuus, ut ejus comburam cadaver?
paras.en: [[6:9|And if there remain|Quod si reliqui fuerint]], that is, be left, [[6:9|ten men in one house|decem viri in domo una]], escaping in secret the hands of the Assyrians or of the Chaldeans, [[6:9|they also shall die|et ipsi morientur]] in the place where they hid, by famine, smoke or pestilence. And [[6:10|a man's kinsman|propinquus suus]] [[6:10|shall take him up|Et tollet eum]], that is, each one of those dead (the kinsman being one who lived with him, or a neighbour), [[6:10|and shall burn him|et comburet eum]], that is, the lifeless corpses, [[6:10|that he may carry the bones out of the house|ut efferat ossa de domo]] to the tomb: because, for the multitude of the dying, he will have no leisure to carry whole bodies to the grave. [[6:10|and he shall say|Et dicet]], the burner, [[6:10|to him that is in the inner rooms of the house|ei qui in penetralibus domus est]], that is, in the inmost places: [[6:10|Is there yet any with thee|Numquid adhuc est penes te]], any dead man, that I may burn his corpse?

paras.t: Et respondebit: Finis est corporum mortuorum in domo hac. Et dicet combustor ei qui fuit in penetralibus domus: Tace a laude Dei, et non recorderis nominis Domini, id est, Deum non invoces, laudes, vel exprimas, nec jures per eum, sed oblivioni trade eum, qui tanta super nos mala induxit. Per hoc Propheta insinuat, quod non essent flagellis emendandi, sed obstinandi, atque ad impatientiam contra Deum movendi.
paras.en: [[6:11|And he shall answer: There is an end|Et respondebit: Finis est]] of the dead bodies in this house. [[6:11|And he shall say to him|Et dicet combustor ei]], the burner, to him who was in the inner rooms of the house: [[6:11|Hold thy peace|Tace a laude Dei]], cease from the praise of God [Denis's text reads Tace a laude Dei, “be silent from the praise of God”; the Vulgate has Tace alone], [[6:11|and mention not the name of the Lord|et non recorderis nominis Domini]], that is, do not call upon God, nor praise him, nor name him, nor swear by him, but give him over to oblivion, who has brought such evils upon us. By this the Prophet hints that they were not to be amended by the scourges, but hardened, and moved to impatience against God.

paras.t: Quia ecce Dominus mandavit, id est, prænuntiavit, vel fieri jussit, seu voluntatem hostibus inspiravit, et percutiet, id est, Assyriis virtutem percutiendi donabit, domum majorem, id est populum decem tribuum, ruinis, id est omnimoda demolitione, ita quod non reducentur, sed usque in finem mundi capti tenebuntur; et domum minorem, id est regnum duarum tribuum, percutiet per Chaldæos, scissionibus, id est quibusdam fracturis, quæ post septuaginta annos reparabuntur. Scissio enim recuperatur potius quam ruina. Per quod distinctio utriusque captivitatis innuitur.
paras.en: [[6:12|For behold the Lord hath commanded|Quia ecce Dominus mandavit]], that is, has foretold, or has ordered it to be done, or has inspired the will to the enemy, [[6:12|and he will strike|et percutiet]], that is, he will give the Assyrians the power to strike, [[6:12|the greater house|domum majorem]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, [[6:12|with breaches|ruinis]] [ruinis, literally “with ruins”], that is, with utter demolition, so that they shall not be brought back but shall be held captive until the end of the world; [[6:12|and the lesser house|et domum minorem]], that is, the kingdom of the two tribes, he will strike through the Chaldeans [[6:12|with clefts|scissionibus]], that is, with certain fractures, which shall be repaired after seventy years. For a cleft is more easily mended than a ruin. By this the difference between the two captivities is suggested.

paras.t: Numquid currere queunt in petris equi? quasi dicat: Contra naturam hoc est, ut equi currant in saxis, quia non cedunt currenti, nec dividuntur faciliter. Aut arari potest in bubalis? id est, boves silvestres, quum sint feroces atque indomiti, non possunt ligari ad arandum in aratro. Cur autem hoc dixerit, subditur: Quoniam convertistis in amaritudinem judicium: id est, quum bruta servent suam naturam, vos contra naturam egistis, judicium subvertendo, et ad amaritudinem innocentes perducendo, quemadmodum per Ezechielem Dominus ait: Mœrere fecistis justum, quem ego non contristavi; et fructum, id est delectationem seu operationem, justitiæ, ex sua natura suavem, convertistis in absinthium, id est in magnam amaricationem: quia vos ipsi in vitiis justitiæ contrariis, amaris, et pœnam promerentibus occupati fuistis, et alios propter justitiam persequendo, ad amaritudinem induxistis. Vel sensus est, secundum Hieronymum, quod suis peccatis Deum naturaliter dulcem et pium ad iracundiam provocaverunt, et ejus judicium contra se exacerbaverunt, quemadmodum scriptum est: Exacerbastis eum qui fecit vos, Deum æternum.
paras.en: [[6:13|Can horses run upon the rocks|Numquid currere queunt in petris equi]]? As if to say: It is against nature for horses to run on stones, since these do not yield to the runner nor are easily parted. [[6:13|or can any one plough with buffles|Aut arari potest in bubalis]]? That is, wild oxen, being fierce and untamed, cannot be yoked to the plough for ploughing. Why he has said this is added: [[6:13|for you have turned judgment into bitterness|Quoniam convertistis in amaritudinem judicium]]: that is, while the brute beasts keep their nature, you have acted against nature, overturning judgment and bringing the innocent to bitterness, as the Lord says through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 13:22|you have made the heart of the just to mourn, whom I have not made sorrowful|Mœrere fecistis justum, quem ego non contristavi]]; [[6:13|and the fruit|et fructum]], that is, the delight or the working, [[6:13|of justice|justitiæ]], sweet by its nature, you have turned [[6:13|into wormwood|in absinthium]], that is, into great bitterness: because you yourselves have been taken up with vices contrary to justice, bitter and deserving punishment, and by persecuting others for justice' sake you have brought them to bitterness. Or the sense is, according to Jerome, that by their sins they provoked God, by nature sweet and kind, to anger[[Deut 9:18||]][[Deut 32:16||]], and embittered his judgment against themselves, as it is written: [[Bar 4:7|you have provoked him who made you, the eternal God|Exacerbastis eum qui fecit vos, Deum æternum]].

paras.t: Qui lætamini in nihili, id est aureis vitulis seu idolis, de quibus scriptum est in libro Esther: Ne tradas, Domine, sceptrum tuum his qui non sunt. Vel, In nihili, id est mendaciis et vana gloria mundi. Hinc in Isaia habetur: Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates. Idolum enim, secundum Apostolum, nihil est: non quoad materiam, sed quantum ad id quod esse putatur. Qui dicitis jactanter: Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua? id est, imo propria potestate sortiti sumus excellentiam, potentiam et gloriam mundi, seu reges, quibus ventilavimus hostes. Quod autem per cornua intelligantur reges, patet in Apocalypsi et Daniele.
paras.en: [[6:14|You that rejoice in a thing of nought|Qui lætamini in nihili]], that is, in the golden calves or idols, of which it is written in the book of Esther: [[Esth 14:11|Give not, O Lord, thy sceptre to them that are not|Ne tradas, Domine, sceptrum tuum his qui non sunt]]. Or [[6:14|in a thing of nought|In nihili]], that is, in lies and the vain glory of the world. Hence we have in Isaias: [[Is 59:4|they trust in a mere nothing, and speak vanities|Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates]]. For according to the Apostle [[1 Cor 8:4|an idol is nothing|Idolum enim, secundum Apostolum, nihil est]]: not as to its matter, but as to what it is thought to be. [[6:14|you that say|Qui dicitis]] boastfully: [[6:14|Have we not taken unto us horns by our own strength?|Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua?]] That is: nay, by our own power we have obtained excellence, might and the glory of the world, or kings, with whom we have scattered our enemies. That kings are understood by horns is plain in the Apocalypse and in Daniel.

paras.t: Ob hanc igitur præsumptionem: Ecce ego, qui superbos humilio, suscitabo super vos, domus Israel, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, o domus major et domus minor, seu regnum utrumque, gentem Assyriorum super decem tribus, et Chaldæorum super duas; et conteret, id est destruet, vos diversis temporibus, ab introitu Emath, id est a principio terræ promissionis ex una parte, usque ad torrentem deserti, id est usque ad finem terræ istius ex alia parte. Porro torrens deserti, secundum Hieronymum, est rivus Nili de eremo veniens, et mare intrans in Emath. Per Emath vero Glossa intelligit Antiochiam, quæ est in principio Terræ sanctæ.
paras.en: For this presumption, therefore: [[6:15|behold|Ecce ego]], I who humble the proud [[6:15|will raise up|suscitabo]] against you, [[6:15|O house of Israel, saith the Lord the God of hosts|domus Israel, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, O greater house and lesser house, or both kingdoms, [[6:15|a nation|gentem]], that of the Assyrians against the ten tribes and that of the Chaldeans against the two; [[6:15|and they shall destroy you|et conteret]], that is, lay you waste, at different times, [[6:15|from the entrance of Emath|ab introitu Emath]], that is, from the beginning of the promised land on the one side, [[6:15|even to the torrent of the desert|usque ad torrentem deserti]], that is, to the end of that land on the other side. Now the torrent of the desert, according to Jerome, is a stream of the Nile coming from the wilderness and entering the sea in Emath. But by Emath the Gloss understands Antioch, which is at the beginning of the Holy Land.

6.title: Expositio moralis ejusdem capituli sexti.
6.title_en: Moral exposition of the same sixth chapter.

paras.t: Væ vobis, qui opulenti estis, id est avariter divites, in Sion, id est populo christiano, qui speculando divina dicitur Sion, quod interpretatur speculatio. Istis, nisi pœniteant, imminet væ æterni supplicii, Christo testante : Possibilius est camelum transire per foramen acus, quam divitem intrare in regnum cœlorum. Quod certum est dici de avaris divitibus, terrena magis quam cœlestia quærentibus atque amantibus. Affectus ergo, non ipsa res, reprobatur. Qui enim volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli. Ceterum in utroque Testamento multi electi et justi opulenti fuerunt, quemadmodum de se ipso Job ait : Ego quondam ille opulentus. Sed hi impleverunt illud Psalmistæ : Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere ; et illud Apostoli ad Timotheum : Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe, non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo, dives fieri in operibus bonis, facile tribuere. — Denique alia quædam opulentia est, non vera, sed præsumpta, qua vani, arrogantes et præsumptuosi arbitrantur se ceteris justiores ac sapientiores, gratia plenos, meritis abundantes ; qui sperant in multitudine divitiarum suarum, quum tamen re vera sint pauperrimi atque miserrimi, semetipsos fallentes ac pereuntes, quibus sub persona unius dicitur in Apocalypsi : Dicis, Quia dives sum, et nullius egeo ; et nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus. Non ergo arbitremur nos apprehendisse, nec putemus nos aliquid esse ; sed cum metu, timore et tremore nostram operemur salutem.
paras.en: [[6:1|Woe to you that are wealthy|Væ vobis, qui opulenti estis]], that is, avariciously rich, [[6:1|in Sion|in Sion]], that is, in the Christian people, which from its contemplation of divine things is called Sion, which is interpreted *watch-tower* [that is, *speculatio*, a looking-out, which Denis takes as contemplation]. Over these, unless they repent, hangs the woe of eternal punishment, as Christ bears witness: [[Matt 19:24|It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven|Possibilius est camelum transire per foramen acus, quam divitem intrare in regnum cœlorum]][[Luke 18:25||]]. This is certainly said of the avaricious rich, who seek and love the things of earth more than those of heaven. It is the affection, then, not the thing itself, that is condemned. For [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui enim volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli]]. For the rest, in both Testaments many elect and just men were wealthy, as Job says of himself: [[Job 16:13|I that was formerly so wealthy|Ego quondam ille opulentus]]. But these fulfilled that saying of the Psalmist: [[Ps 61:11|if riches abound, set not your heart upon them|Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere]]; and that of the Apostle to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe, non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo]], [[1 Tim 6:18|to be rich in good work, to give easily|dives fieri in operibus bonis, facile tribuere]]. — Lastly, there is a certain other wealth, not true but presumed, by which the vain, the arrogant and the presumptuous reckon themselves juster and wiser than others, full of grace, abounding in merits; who trust in the abundance of their riches[[Ps 51:9||]] [the margin reads Ps. lii, 9; the words are those of Ps 51:9], although in very truth they are most poor and most wretched, deceiving themselves and perishing; to whom it is said in the Apocalypse, under the person of one: [[Apoc 3:17|thou sayest: I am rich|Dicis, Quia dives sum]], and [[Apoc 3:17|have need of nothing: and knowest not that thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|nullius egeo ; et nescis quia tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus]]. Let us not, then, reckon that we have apprehended[[Phil 3:13||]], nor think ourselves to be something[[Gal 2:6||]][[Gal 6:3||]]; but let us work out our salvation with fear, dread and trembling[[Phil 2:12||]].

paras.t: Optimates capita populorum, id est prælati ac principes populi christiani, religiosi et sæculares, ingredientes pompatice domum Israel, id est animose inter inferiores et subditos conversantes, imo et materialem ecclesiam cum tumore superbiæ ingredientes, magis ut videamini quam Deum devote precemini. O quam multi sunt jam tales, qui se in cogitatione sua extollunt velut taurus, nec attendunt quod scriptum est : Quid superbit terra et cinis? Verum quid de unoquoque tali ait Scriptura ? Si ascenderit, inquit, usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit, quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur.
paras.en: [[6:1|ye great men, heads of the people|Optimates capita populorum]], that is, prelates and princes of the Christian people, religious and secular, [[6:1|that go in with state into the house of Israel|ingredientes pompatice domum Israel]], that is, bearing yourselves haughtily among your inferiors and subjects, and even going into the material church with swelling pride, more that you may be seen than that you may devoutly pray to God. O how many such there are now, who extol themselves in their thoughts like a bull[[Ecclus 6:2||]], and do not heed what is written: [[Ecclus 10:9|Why is earth, and ashes proud?|Quid superbit terra et cinis?]] But what does Scripture say of each such man? ‘[[Job 20:6|If his pride mount up|Si ascenderit]],’ it says, ‘[[Job 20:6|even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds|usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit]], [[Job 20:7|In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill|quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur]].’

paras.t: Transite in Chalanne, etc., id est, omnium sectarum et superstitiosarum religionum terras et regna adspicite ; et videte si fuit aliquando secta aliqua in tantum divulgata, dilatata, et confortata, sicut religio christiana. Non utique : in omnem enim terram exivit, et in fines orbis terræ processit. Unde in Isaia inducitur : A finibus terræ audivimus laudes et gloriam Justi ; et in Daniele, Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei.
paras.en: [[6:2|Pass ye over to Chalane|Transite in Chalanne]], etc., that is, look upon the lands and kingdoms of all the sects and superstitious religions, and see whether there was ever any sect so widely spread, enlarged and strengthened as the Christian religion. Not at all: for it [[Ps 18:5|hath gone forth into all the earth|in omnem enim terram exivit]], and has advanced [[Ps 18:5|unto the ends of the world|in fines orbis terræ]]. Hence it is brought in in Isaias: [[Is 24:16|From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|A finibus terræ audivimus laudes et gloriam Justi]]; and in Daniel: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]].

paras.t: Qui separati estis in diem malum, id est ab electis divisi, ita quod in die infernalis vindictæ, sempiterna recipietis tormenta. Hoc omnibus reprobis competit, qui non manent in ecclesiastica unitate mystici corporis Christi; sed a Christo capite per culpam divisi, non recipiunt vitam gratiæ et motum virtutum ab eo. Qui in die judicii separabit electos a reprobis loco et præmio, sicut separat pastor agnos ab hœdis. Denique alia est separatio bona ac appetenda, de qua ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus, loquens de Christo, Segregatus a peccatoribus; et de se ipso Paulus, Segregatus in Evangelium Dei. Et appropinquatis per consensum et opera mala, solio iniquitatis, id est diabolo, qui est rex super omnes filios superbiæ : de quo dicit Salvator, Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus.
paras.en: [[6:3|You that are separated unto the evil day|Qui separati estis in diem malum]], that is, divided from the elect, so that in the day of hell's vengeance you shall receive everlasting torments. This fits all the reprobate, who do not abide in the ecclesiastical unity of the mystical body of Christ, but, divided by guilt from Christ the head, do not receive from him the life of grace and the movement of the virtues. And he in the day of judgement will separate the elect from the reprobate in place and in reward, [[Matt 25:32|as the shepherd separateth the sheep from the goats|sicut separat pastor agnos ab hœdis]] [Denis has *agnos*, lambs, for the Vulgate's *oves*, sheep]. Lastly, there is another separation, good and to be desired, of which the Apostle speaks to the Hebrews, saying of Christ: [[Heb 7:26|separated from sinners|Segregatus a peccatoribus]]; and Paul says of himself: [[Rom 1:1|separated unto the gospel of God|Segregatus in Evangelium Dei]]. [[6:3|and that approach|Et appropinquatis]] by consent and evil works [[6:3|to the throne of iniquity|solio iniquitatis]], that is, to the devil, who is [[Job 41:25|king over all the children of pride|rex super omnes filios superbiæ]]; of whom the Saviour says: There cometh to me [[John 14:30|the prince of this world|princeps mundi hujus]].

paras.t: Qui dormitis in lectis eburneis, et lascivitis in stratis vestris. Hoc plane cum versu sequenti de luxuriosis atque gulosis, qui bestiis decies millies turpiores deterioresque sunt, convenienter accipitur. Et maxime competit magnatibus sæculi, carnalibusque prælatis, qui quanto abundant divitiis, tantum se exponunt deliciis. Quocontra dicit Apostolus : Non in comessationibus et ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus et impudicitiis; sed induimini Dominum Jesum.
paras.en: [[6:4|You that sleep upon beds of ivory, and are wanton on your couches|Qui dormitis in lectis eburneis, et lascivitis in stratis vestris]]. This, together with the following verse, is fittingly taken of the lustful and gluttonous, who are ten thousand times fouler and worse than beasts. And it fits above all the great men of the world and carnal prelates, who give themselves to delights as much as they abound in riches. Against which the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:13|not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and impurities|Non in comessationibus et ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus et impudicitiis]]; [[Rom 13:14|But put ye on the Lord Jesus|sed induimini Dominum Jesum]].

paras.t: Qui canitis ad vocem psalterii. Hoc convenit his qui musicis instrumentis utuntur in choreis et epulis, ut carnalis affectus et vanitas inflammetur in eis. De quibus scriptum est in Job : Tenent tympanum et chorum, et gaudent ad vocem psalterii. Verum, ut in Ecclesiastico legitur : Vinum et musica lætificant cor; et super utraque dilectio sapientiæ. Et iterum : Tibiæ et psalterium suavem faciunt melodiam; et super utraque lingua suavis.
paras.en: [[6:5|You that sing to the sound of the psaltery|Qui canitis ad vocem psalterii]]. This fits those who use musical instruments at dances and feasts, so that carnal affection and vanity may be kindled in them. Of whom it is written in Job: [[Job 21:12|They take the timbrel, and the harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ|Tenent tympanum et chorum, et gaudent ad vocem psalterii]] [Denis reads *chorum* and *ad vocem psalterii*, ‘the dance’ and ‘at the sound of the psaltery’, where the Vulgate has *citharam* and *ad sonitum organi*]. But, as we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 40:20|Wine and music rejoice the heart, but the love of wisdom is above them both|Vinum et musica lætificant cor; et super utraque dilectio sapientiæ]]. And again: [[Ecclus 40:21|The flute and the psaltery make a sweet melody, but a pleasant tongue is above them both|Tibiæ et psalterium suavem faciunt melodiam; et super utraque lingua suavis]].

paras.t: Bibentes vinum in phialis, et optimo unguento delibuti; et nihil patiebantur super contritione Joseph. Hoc de pastoribus verificatur, qui pascunt se ipsos, non gregem dominicum, operientes se lana ovium, et lac earum edentes, ipsas vero oves Christi non custodientes ab invisibilium hostium morsibus. Imo videntes quod sibi commissi quotidie peccant, deteriorantur, et a dæmonibus absorbentur, non dolent nec auxiliantur, quum et ipsi similiter pereant. Quocontra Salomon ait : Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera; et Paulus, Ego, inquit, libentissime impendam, et superimpendar ipse pro animabus vestris. Sed et princeps pastorum : Ego, inquit, sum pastor bonus; et cognosco oves meas, et cognoscunt me meæ; et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Insuper multi sunt principes et prælati, pleni privato amore, qui subditorum suorum temporalibus persecutionibus, corporalibus nocumentis atque penuriis ac prædationibus non compatiuntur, sed voluptatibus et vanitatibus æqualiter vacant, quasi contritio domus Joseph (id est Ecclesiæ Christi per Joseph significati) non pertineret ad eos. Et tamen de manu pastorum requiret Dominus sanguinem pereuntium subditorum. Contra hujusmodi præsidentes loquitur Dominus copiose per Ezechielem.
paras.en: [[6:6|That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the best ointments: and they are not concerned for the affliction of Joseph|Bibentes vinum in phialis, et optimo unguento delibuti; et nihil patiebantur super contritione Joseph]]. This is verified of the shepherds who feed themselves, not the Lord's flock, covering themselves with the wool of the sheep and eating their milk[[Ezech 34:2||]][[Ezech 34:3||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxxiv, 2–6], but not guarding Christ's sheep themselves from the bites of invisible enemies. Nay, seeing that those committed to them sin daily, grow worse and are swallowed up by the demons, they neither grieve nor help, since they themselves likewise perish. Against which Solomon says: [[Prov 27:23|Be diligent to know the countenance of thy cattle, and consider thy own flocks|Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera]]; and Paul: ‘I,’ he says, ‘[[2 Cor 12:15|most gladly will spend and be spent myself for your souls|libentissime impendam, et superimpendar ipse pro animabus vestris]].’ And the prince of shepherds too: ‘I,’ he says, ‘[[John 10:14|am the good shepherd: and I know mine, and mine know me|sum pastor bonus; et cognosco oves meas, et cognoscunt me meæ]]; [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]].’ Moreover, there are many princes and prelates full of private love, who have no compassion on the temporal persecutions, bodily harms, wants and plunderings of their subjects, but give themselves just as before to pleasures and vanities, as though the affliction of the house of Joseph (that is, of the Church of Christ, signified by Joseph) did not concern them. And yet the Lord will require at the hand of the shepherds the blood of the subjects who perish[[Ezech 3:20||]] [the margin reads Ezech. xiii, 20, which does not fit; the words are those of Ezech 3:20 (and 3:18)]. Against such rulers the Lord speaks at length through Ezechiel[[Ezech 34:2||]].

paras.t: Quapropter nunc migrabunt, id est, statim ad infernum ducentur, in capite transmigrantium, id est in principio damnatorum qui per eorum negligentiam perierunt. Tales enim præsidentes sunt primi in pœnis, et omnium damnatio retorquetur in eos. Et auferetur factio lascivientium, id est, voluptas lubricorum mox finietur, atque gehennali ardore ulciscetur.
paras.en: [[6:7|Wherefore now they shall go captive|Quapropter nunc migrabunt]], that is, they shall straightway be led to hell, [[6:7|at the head of them that go into captivity|in capite transmigrantium]], that is, at the head of the damned who perished through their negligence. For such rulers are first in punishment, and the damnation of all is turned back upon them. [[6:7|and the faction of the luxurious ones shall be taken away|Et auferetur factio lascivientium]], that is, the pleasure of the lewd shall soon be ended, and shall be avenged with the burning of Gehenna.

paras.t: Juravit Dominus : Detestor ego superbiam Jacob, id est omnium Christianorum, quorum est vitia supplantare, et domos ejus odi, id est, congregationes arrogantium sperno. Ideo Tobias jubet filio suo : Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in tuo animo dominari permittas : in ipsa enim sumpsit initium omnis perditio. Humiliemur igitur sub potenti manu Dei, quia ut dicitur in Isaia, Dies Domini super omnem superbum, et excelsum, et arrogantem; et humiliabitur. Hinc in Numerorum libro fertur : Anima quæ per superbiam aliquid commiserit, quoniam adversus Dominum rebellis fuit, peribit de populo suo : verbum enim Domini contempsit. Et tradam civitatem, id est ecclesiam hujusmodi superborum, cum habitatoribus suis, id est his qui manent in vitiis, manibus dæmonum.
paras.en: [[6:8|The Lord God hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]]: [[6:8|I detest the pride of Jacob|Detestor ego superbiam Jacob]], that is, of all Christians, whose part it is to supplant vices [that is, to trip them up and overthrow them, as *Jacob* means ‘supplanter’], [[6:8|and I hate his houses|et domos ejus odi]], that is, I spurn the gatherings of the arrogant. Therefore Tobias bids his son: [[Tob 4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind, or in thy words: for from it all perdition took its beginning|Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu aut in tuo animo dominari permittas : in ipsa enim sumpsit initium omnis perditio]] [Denis has *in tuo animo*, ‘in thy mind’, where the Vulgate has *in tuo verbo*, ‘in thy words’]. Let us therefore be humbled [[1 Pet 5:6|under the mighty hand of God|sub potenti manu Dei]], since, as is said in Isaias, [[Is 2:12|the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and highminded, and upon every one that is arrogant, and he shall be humbled|Dies Domini super omnem superbum, et excelsum, et arrogantem; et humiliabitur]]. Hence it is said in the book of Numbers: [[Num 15:30|the soul that committeth any thing through pride|Anima quæ per superbiam aliquid commiserit]], [[Num 15:30|because he hath been rebellious against the Lord|quoniam adversus Dominum rebellis fuit]], [[Num 15:30|shall be cut off from among his people|peribit de populo suo]]: [[Num 15:31|For he hath contemned the word of the Lord|verbum enim Domini contempsit]]. [[6:8|and I will deliver up the city|Et tradam civitatem]], that is, the church of such proud men, [[6:8|with the inhabitants thereof|cum habitatoribus suis]], that is, those who abide in vices, into the hands of the demons.

paras.t: Quod si reliqui fuerint decem viri superbi in domo una, et ipsi morientur morte culpæ in via, et morte miseriæ in gehenna. Nullus enim talium manus Omnipotentis potest evadere.
paras.en: [[6:9|And if there remain ten men|Quod si reliqui fuerint decem viri]] that are proud [[6:9|in one house, they also shall die|in domo una, et ipsi morientur]], by the death of guilt on the way, and by the death of misery in Gehenna. For none of such men can escape the hand of the Almighty.

paras.t: Et tollet eum propinquus suus : unus enim perversus, malo exemplo interimit alium. Et qui virtuosum pertrahit ad peccata, comburet ossa ipsius ; virtutes enim significantur per ossa.
paras.en: [[6:10|And a man's kinsman shall take him up|Et tollet eum propinquus suus]]: for one perverse man kills another by his bad example. And he who draws a virtuous man into sins [[6:10|shall burn|comburet]] his bones; for the virtues are signified by the bones.

paras.t: Quidam interea ita incorrigibiles sunt, et ita indurantur dum castigantur a Deo, ut vix possent nomen Dei audire, vel ejus honorationem videre, cupiuntque omnes averti ab ipso, sicut ipsi aversi sunt. Quibus convenit quod subjungitur : Dicet : Tace, et non recorderis nominis Domini.
paras.en: Some, meanwhile, are so incorrigible, and are so hardened while they are chastised by God, that they can scarcely bear to hear the name of God or to see him honoured, and they desire all men to be turned away from him, as they themselves are turned away. To these fits what is added: [[6:11|he shall say to him: Hold thy peace, and mention not the name of the Lord|Dicet : Tace, et non recorderis nominis Domini]].

paras.t: Ecce Dominus percutiet et domum majorem, id est multitudinem prælatorum ac principum injuste præsidentium, ruinis, id est, penitus deseret eos perire, gratiam subtrahendo in via, et gloriam in patria. Talium enim peccata quum sint gravissima, extrema ultione plectuntur frequenter.
