Et domum minorem, id est, subditos percutiet, scissionibus, id est plagis paternæ correctionis, ne penitus pereant, sed per flagella temporalium tribulationum in æternum salventur. Tales enim interdum purgantur per adversitates et damna quæ eis a superioribus, potentibus ac divitibus infliguntur. Exiguo quippe conceditur misericordia ; sed judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, peragitur. Vel domus major, sunt reprobi; domus vero minor, electi. Reprobi autem prorsus intereunt, electi vero per multas tribulationes ac tentationes exercitati, reformantur et beatitudinem sortiuntur.
paras.en: [[6:12|behold the Lord|Ecce Dominus]] [[6:12|will strike the greater house|percutiet et domum majorem]], that is, the multitude of prelates and princes who rule unjustly, [[6:12|with breaches|ruinis]], that is, he will leave them utterly to perish, withdrawing grace on the way and glory in the fatherland. For since the sins of such men are most grievous, they are often punished with the utmost vengeance. [[6:12|and the lesser house|Et domum minorem]], that is, he will strike the subjects, [[6:12|with clefts|scissionibus]], that is, with the strokes of fatherly correction, lest they perish utterly, but that through the scourges of temporal tribulations they may be saved for eternity. For such are sometimes purged through the adversities and losses inflicted on them by their superiors, by the powerful and the rich. For [[Wis 6:7|to him that is little, mercy is granted|Exiguo quippe conceditur misericordia]]; but on those that bear rule [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment|judicium durissimum]] is executed. Or the greater house is the reprobate, and the lesser house the elect. The reprobate perish altogether, but the elect, exercised by many tribulations and temptations, are made new and obtain beatitude.

paras.t: Numquid currere queunt in petris equi? id est, prædicatores velut equi per fervorem caritatis veloces ac agiles, in cordibus induratis habere non possunt processum. Unde oportet ut Deus auferat cor lapideum, præstetque carneum. Aut arari potest in bubalis? id est, per crudeles rebellesque homines, corda aliorum disponi non possunt ad receptionem seminis, quod est verbum Dei. Tales enim magis obesse quam prodesse consueverunt. Idcirco necesse est prælatum atque doctorem esse benignum, et Deo subjectum. Potest quoque trahi ad sensum oppositum, ita quod equi, id est adversariæ potestates indomitæ, non possunt currere seu proficere in petris, id est in cordibus per virtutes firmatis, quæ dicere valent cum Paulo : Neque mors, neque vita, neque creatura aliqua poterit nos separare a caritate Dei.
paras.en: [[6:13|Can horses run upon the rocks|Numquid currere queunt in petris equi]]? that is, preachers, swift and nimble like horses through the fervour of charity, can make no headway in hardened hearts. Hence God must take away the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh[[Ezech 11:19||]][[Ezech 36:26||]]. [[6:13|or can any one plough with buffles|Aut arari potest in bubalis]]? that is, through cruel and rebellious men the hearts of others cannot be made ready to receive the seed, which is [[Luke 8:11|the word of God|verbum Dei]]. For such men are wont to do more harm than good. Therefore a prelate and teacher must be kindly, and subject to God. It can also be drawn to the opposite sense: that the horses, that is, the untamed adverse powers, cannot run or make headway upon the rocks, that is, in hearts made firm by the virtues, which can say with Paul: [[Rom 8:38|neither death, nor life|Neque mors, neque vita]], [[Rom 8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God|neque creatura aliqua poterit nos separare a caritate Dei]].

paras.t: Quoniam convertistis in amaritudinem judicium. De hoc dicta sunt multa. Omnes autem iniqui, Deum naturaliter dulcem, faciunt sibi ipsis severum.
paras.en: [[6:13|for you have turned judgment into bitterness|Quoniam convertistis in amaritudinem judicium]]. Much has been said of this. But all the wicked make God, who is by nature sweet, severe towards themselves.

paras.t: Qui dicitis : Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua? Hoc dicunt, qui se propria industria, potestate aut studio jactant ad magna promotos, et aliis sapientiores, potentiores, ditiores, aut sublimiores effectos : qui non attendunt quod omne bonum a Deo donetur, et quod ex se ipsis non habeant nisi defectibilitatem et vitia; quod item nihil periculosius est, majusque reprobationis indicium, quam in hac vita in omnibus bonis sæculi prosperari, a Deo non castigari, nec humiliari. Quæ si pensarent, nequaquam præsumerent, sed timerent, scientes quod cui plus donatum est, plus requiretur ab eo.
paras.en: [[6:14|you that say: Have we not taken unto us horns by our own strength?|Qui dicitis : Numquid non in fortitudine nostra assumpsimus nobis cornua?]] This is said by those who boast that by their own industry, power or zeal they have been raised to great things, and made wiser, mightier, richer or loftier than others: who do not heed that every good is given by God[[Jas 1:17||]], and that of themselves they have nothing but defectibility [that is, the liability to fail and fall away] and vices; and again, that nothing is more dangerous, and no sign of reprobation greater, than to prosper in this life in all the goods of the world, and not to be chastised or humbled by God. If they weighed these things, they would by no means presume, but would fear, knowing that [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|cui plus donatum est, plus requiretur ab eo]].

paras.t: Ecce ego suscitabo super vos, dicit Dominus, gentem. Gens ista, sunt dæmones, quos Deus permittit tentando prævalere superbis et præsumptuosis, in suis viribus inaniter infeliciterque sperantibus. Unde de diabolo ait Salvator in Evangelio : Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Et conteret vos ab introitu Emath, id est ab exordio iniquitatis vestræ, quæ velut murus inter Deum et vos separat, et bonum a vobis prohibet : Emath enim murus seu murata interpretatur; usque ad torrentem deserti, id est aquas tribulationis inferni ab omni gratia derelicti. A culpa enim, quæ tollit esse gratiæ, usque ad pœnam, quæ aufert esse gloriæ, pertrahuntur iniqui.
paras.en: [[6:15|behold, I will raise up|Ecce ego suscitabo]] [[6:15|a nation|gentem]] [[6:15|against you|super vos]], [[6:15|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. This nation is the demons, whom God permits to prevail in tempting the proud and presumptuous, who hope vainly and unhappily in their own strength. Hence the Saviour says of the devil in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:28|An enemy hath done this|Inimicus homo hoc fecit]]. [[6:15|and they shall destroy you from the entrance of Emath|Et conteret vos ab introitu Emath]], that is, from the beginning of your iniquity, which like a wall separates between God and you and keeps good from you: for *Emath* is interpreted ‘wall’ or ‘walled’; [[6:15|even to the torrent of the desert|usque ad torrentem deserti]], that is, to the waters of the tribulation of hell, forsaken of all grace. For from guilt, which takes away the being of grace, to punishment, which takes away the being of glory, the wicked are dragged along.

7.title: Declaratio litteralis capituli septimi: Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus.
7.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventh chapter: These things the Lord God shewed to me.

paras.t: […] locustæ, id est, Deus omnipotens formator locustarum, venit seu per ultionem visitavit populum regni Juda, vel Israel, aut utrumque, in principio germinantium, id est terræ nascentium, florentium et fructum producentium, serotini imbris, id est terræ nascentium quæ serotina pluvia irrigantur. Dicitur autem serotinus imber, qui fructus ad maturitatem deducit; temporaneus vero seu matutinus, qui semina jactata in terra coalescere facit. Porro Prophetæ huic in prædicta imaginaria visione apparuit, quod Deus in principio germinantium, secundum sensum jam dictum, id est verno tempore, dum omnia virent atque fructificant, locustas condidit et adduxit super terram Hebræorum.
paras.en: […] [[7:1|the locust|locustæ]], that is, God almighty, the former of the locusts [Denis reads *fictor locustæ*, “the former of the locust”, where the Douay-Rheims has “the locust was formed”], came, or visited the people of the kingdom of Juda, or of Israel, or both, in vengeance, [[7:1|in the beginning of the shooting up|in principio germinantium]], that is, of the things growing out of the earth, flowering and bearing fruit, [[7:1|of the latter rain|serotini imbris]], that is, of the things growing out of the earth that are watered by the latter rain. Now the latter rain is the one that brings the fruits to ripeness; the early or morning rain [*temporaneus* or *matutinus*] is the one that makes the seeds cast into the earth take root. So it appeared to this Prophet in the imaginary vision [that is, a vision seen in the imagination, in images] spoken of, that God, in the beginning of the shooting up, in the sense just given, that is, in springtime, while all things are green and bearing fruit, made locusts and brought them upon the land of the Hebrews.

paras.t: Et ecce serotinus post tonsorem regis. Littera ista est intricata, dumque Propheta brevitati studuit, obscuritatem reliquit. Sic ergo ordinanda sunt verba : Et ecce : per quod significatur magnum et considerabile esse quod subditur; post tonsorem regis, id est post adventum prædictæ locustæ fictæ a Deo regnante, vel significante exercitum regis Assyriorum seu Chaldæorum, sicut dicetur : quæ locusta venit in principio imbris serotini, et velut tonsor seu rasor bona terræ consumpsit; venit serotinus, id est tonsor sequens tonsorem præfatum. Quem tonsorem serotinum, Septuaginta interpretes nominant bruchum : qui venit post principium imbris serotini, et ea voravit quæ non devoravit locusta. Per locustam vero ad litteram, non intelliguntur bestiolæ, sed exercitus Assyriorum, qui decem tribus devoravit pro magna parte ; per bruchum autem sequentem, exercitus Chaldæorum, qui postea duarum tribuum demolitus est regnum. Qui vero locustam et bruchum vellet ad idem regnum reducere, faciliter invenit modum, quia Sennacherib rex Assyriorum, deinde Nabuchodonosor rex Chaldæorum duas tribus est persecutus. Regnum vero decem tribuum cœpit vastari a Phul rege Assyriorum, deinde a Theglathphalasar, postremo a Salmanasar.
paras.en: [[7:1|and lo, it was the latter rain after the king's mowing|Et ecce serotinus post tonsorem regis]] [Denis reads *tonsorem*, “the king's mower”, where the Vulgate has *tonsionem*, “mowing”]. This text is tangled: while the Prophet studied brevity, he left obscurity. The words, then, are to be put in this order: [[7:1|and lo|Et ecce]]: by which it is signified that what follows is great and worth considering; [[7:1|after the king's mowing|post tonsorem regis]], that is, after the coming of the aforesaid locust formed by God who reigns, or signifying the army of the king of the Assyrians or of the Chaldeans, as will be said: which locust came in the beginning of the latter rain, and like a mower or shaver consumed the goods of the land; there came [[7:1|the latter rain|serotinus]], that is, a mower following the mower already spoken of. This latter mower the Seventy translators name the *bruchus*: it came after the beginning of the latter rain, and devoured what the locust had not devoured. By the locust, in the literal sense, are understood not little beasts but the army of the Assyrians, which devoured the ten tribes for the greater part; and by the bruchus that follows, the army of the Chaldeans, which afterwards destroyed the kingdom of the two tribes. But anyone who wished to refer the locust and the bruchus to the same kingdom easily finds a way, for Sennacherib king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 18:1||]][[4 Kings 19:1||]], and afterwards Nabuchodonosor king of the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 24:1||]][[4 Kings 25:1||]], persecuted the two tribes. The kingdom of the ten tribes, again, began to be laid waste by Phul king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 15:19||]], then by Theglathphalasar[[4 Kings 15:29||]], and last of all by Salmanasar[[4 Kings 17:3||]][[4 Kings 17:6||]].

paras.t: Alius quidam hanc improbat expositionem, quia prædicti exercitus populum utriusque regni vastarunt. Sed de prædictis plagis statim subjungetur : Misertus est Dominus super hoc : Non erit, dixit Dominus Deus. Exponit ergo præhabita de multitudine locustarum, ita quod Deus monstravit Prophetæ se velle locustas super terram inducere ad terræ nascentia destruenda. Tamen non fecit propter precem Prophetæ. — Sed huic dicto repugnat quod immediate subjungitur : Et factum est, quum consummasset comedere herbam terræ, dixit : Domine Deus, propitius esto. Non ergo fuit comminatio tantum, sed et veritas seu effectus, post quem secuta est Prophetæ oratio. Rursus innotescit ex dictis, et idem ait Hieronymus, quod Amos et Joel eodem tempore prophetaverunt. Quod autem apud Joelem de locusta et bruchum annuntiatur, iste non solum de bestiolis, sed et de hominibus per illas significatis, exponit. Ergo et hoc loco idem poterit dici. Præterea Joel dicit terram Israel a bestiolis dictis corrosam : quomodo ergo nunc dicitur, quod comminatio præinducta non venit ad rem?
paras.en: A certain other writer rejects this explanation, because the armies spoken of did lay waste the people of both kingdoms. But of the plagues spoken of it is added straight away: [[7:3|The Lord had pity upon this: It shall not be, said the Lord|Misertus est Dominus super hoc : Non erit, dixit Dominus Deus]]. He therefore explains what went before of a multitude of locusts, in this way: God showed the Prophet that he willed to bring locusts upon the land to destroy what grows from the earth, yet did not do it because of the Prophet's prayer. — But against this saying stands what is added immediately: [[7:2|And it came to pass, that when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land, I said: O Lord God, be merciful|Et factum est, quum consummasset comedere herbam terræ, dixit : Domine Deus, propitius esto]]. So it was not a threat only, but also the truth, or the effect, after which the Prophet's prayer followed. Again, it is known from what has been said, and Jerome says the same, that Amos and Joel prophesied at the same time. Now what is foretold in Joel of the locust and the bruchus[[Joel 1:4||]], he [Jerome] explains not only of little beasts but also of the men signified by them. So the same can be said in this place too. Moreover, Joel says that the land of Israel was gnawed by these little beasts[[Joel 1:4||]]: how then is it now said that the threat put forward did not come to pass?

paras.t: Et factum est, quum consummasset comedere herbam terræ, id est, postquam in spiritu vidi et intellexi quid dicta visio significaret, et præcognovi quod prædictæ gentes vastaturæ essent utriusque regni terram ac populum, prout in visione mihi fuerat notificatum, dixi orando : Domine Deus, propitius esto, obsecro, id est, noli totum populum utriusque regni hostibus tradere, sive destruere, sed reliquiæ aliquæ salvæ fiant. Et merito oro te : nam, quis suscitabit Jacob? id est, quis præter te poterit filios Israel ab imminente pressura eripere? quia parvulus est, id est, sæpe jam minorati sunt potestate ac numero, ab hostibusque dejecti : idcirco sua virtute non valent resistere. Misertus est Dominus super hoc, id est, plagam præfatam mitigavit placatus precibus meis ac lacrimis. Non erit, dixit Dominus Deus, id est, totum utriusque regni non destruam populum, sed reliquiæ salvabuntur. Translatis enim decem tribubus, multi ex tribubus illis remanserunt in terra Israel. Quod vero translatis duabus tribubus, quidam evaserunt Chaldæos, patet quarto Regum et in Jeremia.
paras.en: [[7:2|And it came to pass, that when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land|Et factum est, quum consummasset comedere herbam terræ]], that is, after I had seen in the spirit and understood what the said vision signified, and had foreknown that the nations spoken of would lay waste the land and people of both kingdoms, as had been made known to me in the vision, I said in prayer: [[7:2|O Lord God, be merciful, I beseech thee|Domine Deus, propitius esto, obsecro]], that is, do not hand over to the enemy, or destroy, the whole people of both kingdoms, but let some remnant be saved. And rightly do I pray thee: for [[7:2|who shall raise up Jacob|quis suscitabit Jacob]]? that is, who but thou can rescue the children of Israel from the distress that threatens them? [[7:2|for he is very little|quia parvulus est]], that is, they have often been lessened already in power and number, and cast down by enemies; therefore they cannot resist by their own strength. [[7:3|The Lord had pity upon this|Misertus est Dominus super hoc]], that is, he softened the plague spoken of, appeased by my prayers and tears. [[7:3|It shall not be, said the Lord|Non erit, dixit Dominus Deus]], that is, I will not destroy the whole people of both kingdoms, but a remnant shall be saved. For when the ten tribes were carried away, many of those tribes remained in the land of Israel. And that when the two tribes were carried away some escaped the Chaldeans is plain from the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 25:12||]][[4 Kings 25:22||]] and from Jeremias[[Jer 52:16||]].

paras.t: Sequitur visio alia. Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus, secundum sensum prætactum. Et ecce vocavit Dominus judicium, id est sententiam suæ æquitatis, vel exsecutorem suæ justitiæ, per quem alios judicavit, puta Nabuchodonosor regem, ad ignem, dando ei voluntatem comburendi urbes Juda et Jerusalem; et devoravit abyssum multam, id est populum copiosissimum, qui ob suam multitudinem pelago comparatur. Vel sensus est, quod Chaldæi cum tanto tumultu ac strepitu terram Juda ingressi sunt, velut si ipsum mare absorberent. Sicque videtur locutio hyperbolica. Et comedit simul partem, id est, ignis iste incendit atque destruxit templum Jerusalem : quod fuit pars Domini, tanquam ejus deputatum obsequio.
paras.en: Another vision follows. [[7:4|These things the Lord God shewed to me|Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus]], in the sense touched on before. [[7:4|and behold the Lord called for judgment|Et ecce vocavit Dominus judicium]], that is, the sentence of his equity, or the executor of his justice, through whom he judged others, namely king Nabuchodonosor, [[7:4|unto fire|ad ignem]], by giving him the will to burn the cities of Juda and Jerusalem; [[7:4|and it devoured the great deep|et devoravit abyssum multam]], that is, a most numerous people, which for its multitude is compared to the sea. Or the sense is that the Chaldeans entered the land of Juda with such tumult and din as if they were swallowing up the sea itself; and so the expression seems to be a hyperbole. [[7:4|and ate up a part at the same time|Et comedit simul partem]], that is, this fire burned and destroyed the temple of Jerusalem[[4 Kings 25:9||]], which was the Lord's part, as set apart for his service.

paras.t: Et dixi, devote orando : Domine Deus, quiesce, obsecro, id est, cessa a pœnis istis propter sanctam tuam bonitatem ac pietatem. Dicendo autem, Quiesce, innuit quod plaga ista, sicut præcedens, fuit incepta. Quis suscitabit Jacob, quia parvulus est? Misertus est Dominus super hoc ; sed et istud non erit, ait Dominus Deus. Omnia verba ista jam semel exposita sunt; et impleta fuerunt quando Chaldæos evaserunt multi ex regno Juda, qui ad tempus habitaverunt cum Godolia, et post cum Jeremia introierunt Ægyptum.
paras.en: [[7:5|And I said|Et dixi]], praying devoutly: [[7:5|O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee|Domine Deus, quiesce, obsecro]], that is, cease from these punishments for the sake of thy holy goodness and mercy. And by saying *Cease* he hints that this plague, like the one before it, had already begun. [[7:5|who shall raise up Jacob, for he is a little one|Quis suscitabit Jacob, quia parvulus est]]? [[7:6|The Lord had pity upon this. Yea this also shall not be, said the Lord God|Misertus est Dominus super hoc ; sed et istud non erit, ait Dominus Deus]]. All these words have been explained once already; and they were fulfilled when many of the kingdom of Juda escaped the Chaldeans, who dwelt for a time with Godolias[[4 Kings 25:22||]][[Jer 40:5||]][[Jer 40:7||]], and afterwards went into Egypt with Jeremias[[4 Kings 25:26||]].

paras.t: Sequitur alia visio. Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus. Et ecce Dominus stans super murum litum, id est linitum, plastratum, et fortiter junctum. Apparuit autem Prophetæ in visu imaginario, quod Dominus staret supra hujuscemodi murum; sed visio ista formata fuit ministerio angeli, qui apparuit in persona Domini. Propter quod Dominus apparuisse narratur, sicut et in visione imaginaria qua Isaias vidit Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum et elevatum. Ibi enim angelus apparuit in persona Dei, secundum Dionysium. Et in manu ejus dextera trulla cœmentarii. Per murum litum intelligitur Judaicus populus, multiplici beneficio Dei olim roboratus et adornatus; per trullam vero seu linitionem, auxilium Dei.
paras.en: Another vision follows. [[7:7|These things the Lord shewed to me|Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus]]. [[7:7|and behold the Lord was standing upon a plastered wall|Et ecce Dominus stans super murum litum]], that is, smeared, plastered and firmly joined. Now it appeared to the Prophet in an imaginary vision that the Lord was standing upon such a wall; but this vision was formed by the ministry of an angel, who appeared in the person of the Lord. For that reason the Lord is said to have appeared, as also in the imaginary vision in which Isaias saw [[Is 6:1|the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated|Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum et elevatum]]: for there an angel appeared in the person of God, according to Dionysius. [[7:7|and in his hand a mason's trowel|Et in manu ejus dextera trulla cœmentarii]] [Denis reads *dextera*, “in his right hand”]. By the plastered wall is understood the Jewish people, strengthened and adorned of old by many benefits of God; and by the trowel, or the plastering, the help of God.

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad me allocutione interna per angelum : Quid tu vides, Amos? Nomine tenus exprimit sanctum Prophetam, quasi amicum, familiarem ac notum per approbationem et prædestinationem, quemadmodum ait ad Moysen in Exodo : Te ipsum novi ex nomine. Novit enim Dominus qui sunt ejus. Interrogat autem Dominus, non quasi ignorans, sed ut erudiat, et ad responsionem convenienter adjiciat. Et dixi : Trullam cæmentarii. Vidit enim similitudinem trullæ, et utebatur similitudine quasi re ipsa. Est autem trulla instrumentum quo murus calce linitur. Et dixit Dominus : Ecce ego ponam, id est deponam, trullam in medio populi mei Israel, id est, auxilium meum et protectionem tollam ab eo. Non adjiciam ultra superinducere eum, id est adornare atque defendere populum istum, ducendo trullam meam prædictam super eum.
paras.en: [[7:8|And the Lord said to me|Et dixit Dominus ad me]], by an inward speaking through the angel: [[7:8|What seest thou, Amos?|Quid tu vides, Amos?]] He names the holy Prophet by his name, as a friend, an intimate, and one known by approval and predestination, as he says to Moses in Exodus: [[Ex 33:17|thee I have known by name|Te ipsum novi ex nomine]]. For [[2 Tim 2:19|the Lord knoweth who are his|Novit enim Dominus qui sunt ejus]]. Now the Lord asks, not as if he did not know, but to teach, and so as fittingly to add something to the answer. [[7:8|And I said: A mason's trowel|Et dixi : Trullam cæmentarii]]. For he saw the likeness of a trowel, and used the likeness as if it were the thing itself. A trowel is the tool with which a wall is plastered with lime. [[7:8|And the Lord said: Behold, I will lay down|Et dixit Dominus : Ecce ego ponam]], that is, I will put down [*ponam*, “I will put”, glossed as *deponam*, “I will put down”], [[7:8|the trowel in the midst of my people Israel|trullam in medio populi mei Israel]], that is, I will take my help and protection away from it. [[7:8|I will plaster them over no more|Non adjiciam ultra superinducere eum]], that is, adorn and defend this people, by drawing my trowel spoken of over it.

paras.t: Et demolientur excelsa idoli, id est, loca sublimia et profana in quibus idola colebantur, ab Assyriis destruentur; et sanctificationes Israel, id est obsequia quibus idola honorabant, seque sanctificari putabant, desolabuntur, id est, punientur et finem jam obtinebunt, quoad hoc quod in terra propria decem tribus ista ultra non facient. Et consurgam super domum Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel in gladio, id est, posteritatem et familiam ejus gladio adversariorum exponam. Unde quarto Regum habetur, quod Sellum interfecit Zachariam filium hujus Jeroboam pronepotis Jehu, cui Dominus dixit quod filii ejus usque ad quartam generationem sederent in solio Israel. Quod in Zacharia prædicto impletum est : quo occiso, Sellum regnavit. Jeroboam vero non fuit occisus.
paras.en: [[7:9|And the high places of the idol shall be thrown down|Et demolientur excelsa idoli]], that is, the lofty and profane places in which idols were worshipped shall be destroyed by the Assyrians; [[7:9|and the sanctuaries of Israel|et sanctificationes Israel]], that is, the services with which they honoured the idols and thought themselves sanctified, [[7:9|shall be laid waste|desolabuntur]], that is, shall be punished and now come to an end, in that the ten tribes will no longer perform them in their own land. [[7:9|and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam|Et consurgam super domum Jeroboam]], son of Joas king of Israel[[4 Kings 14:16||]], [[7:9|with the sword|in gladio]], that is, I will expose his posterity and household to the sword of their adversaries. Hence it is related in the fourth book of Kings that Sellum slew Zacharias[[4 Kings 15:10||]], the son of this Jeroboam, great-grandson of Jehu, to whom the Lord said that his sons should sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation[[4 Kings 10:30||]]. This was fulfilled in the said Zacharias: when he was slain, Sellum reigned. But Jeroboam was not slain.

paras.t: Et misit Amasias sacerdos Bethel, id est urbis sic dictæ, et aurei vituli in ea repositi, ad Jeroboam regem Israel. Eratque Amasias iste, secundum Hieronymum, pontifex sacerdotum idololatrarum, ideo audenter mittit legatos ad regem. Dicens : Rebellavit contra te Amos, id est, tibi inobediens est, idololatriam reprobando quam jubes exerceri, in medio domus Israel, id est in medio decem tribuum, quas pro viribus suis avertit ab idolis. Amasias iste cupidus oblationum quæ vitulis immolabantur, suam malitiam dissimulat, de injuria regi oblata principaliter dolere se fingens, et regem ad persequendum Prophetam provocare desiderans. Forte enim non audebat per se malum facere Amos, quoniam multi de populo confluxerunt ad eum. Unde pro eo quod nostra translatio continet, Rebellavit contra te Amos, Septuaginta transtulerunt, Congregationes contra te facit Amos, id est, populum contra te incitat. Non poterit terra sustinere universos sermones ejus, id est, tanta minatur et vaticinatur, quod populus regni Israel non poterit ea tolerare, nisi per violentiam compellatur : quemadmodum Salomon ait, Non arguas derisorem, ne oderit te. Et teste Chrysostomo, odium incurrit, qui criminosos redarguit. Hinc Amasias videns se argui, succensus est odio contra Prophetam.
paras.en: [[7:10|And Amasias the priest of Bethel sent|Et misit Amasias sacerdos Bethel]], that is, of the city so called, and of the golden calf placed in it[[3 Kings 12:29||]], [[7:10|to Jeroboam king of Israel|ad Jeroboam regem Israel]]. This Amasias, according to Jerome, was the chief of the idolatrous priests, and so he boldly sends envoys to the king, [[7:10|saying: Amos hath rebelled against thee|Dicens : Rebellavit contra te Amos]], that is, he is disobedient to thee, condemning the idolatry which thou commandest to be practised, [[7:10|in the midst of the house of Israel|in medio domus Israel]], that is, in the midst of the ten tribes, which he turns away from idols as far as he can. This Amasias, greedy for the offerings sacrificed to the calves, hides his malice, pretending to grieve chiefly over the wrong done to the king, and wishing to stir the king up to persecute the Prophet. For perhaps he did not dare to do Amos harm by himself, since many of the people flocked to him. Hence, where our translation has *Amos hath rebelled against thee*, the Seventy translated *Amos makes gatherings against thee*, that is, he stirs the people up against thee. [[7:10|the land is not able to bear all his words|Non poterit terra sustinere universos sermones ejus]], that is, he threatens and prophesies such things that the people of the kingdom of Israel cannot bear them unless forced by violence; as Solomon says: [[Prov 9:8|Rebuke not a scorner, lest he hate thee|Non arguas derisorem, ne oderit te]]. And, as Chrysostom witnesses, he who rebukes the guilty incurs hatred. So Amasias, seeing himself rebuked, was inflamed with hatred against the Prophet.

paras.t: Hæc enim dicit Amos : In gladio morietur Jeroboam. In hoc mentitus est Amasias. Amos enim non dixit, Jeroboam, sed domum ejus gladio dandam. Et in hoc Amasias tenet speciem invidorum et callidorum discordiam seminantium, imo et adulatorum. Hi enim recitando verba aliorum, aliquid miscent de proprio, et aliter repetunt quam dictum est : per quod mutuam amantium caritatem inficiunt, quemadmodum scriptum est : Qui alio sermone repetit, separat fœderatos. Et Israel, id est populus decem tribuum, captivus migrabit de terra sua, id est, ad Assyrios perducetur. Verum est quod Amos prædixit hoc.
paras.en: [[7:11|For thus saith Amos: Jeroboam shall die by the sword|Hæc enim dicit Amos : In gladio morietur Jeroboam]]. In this Amasias lied: for Amos did not say that Jeroboam, but that his house, would be given to the sword. And in this Amasias bears the likeness of the envious and of the crafty who sow discord, and indeed of flatterers too. For in repeating the words of others they mix in something of their own, and repeat them otherwise than they were said; and by this they poison the mutual charity of those who love one another, as it is written: [[Prov 17:9|he that repeateth it again, separateth friends|Qui alio sermone repetit, separat fœderatos]] [*alio sermone*, literally “in other words”]. [[7:11|and Israel|Et Israel]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, [[7:11|shall be carried away captive out of their own land|captivus migrabit de terra sua]], that is, shall be led away to the Assyrians. It is true that Amos foretold this.

paras.t: Et dixit Amasias ad Amos. Utrum verba sequentia dixerit Amasias ad Amos ex parte Jeroboam, an ex se ipso, non habeo certum. Hieronymus tamen manifeste testatur, quod Jeroboam nihil ad verba Amasiæ respondit, vanissima legationis suæ verba contemnens. Sic ergo nihil respondit, quia aliunde agnovit quod Amasias falsa mandavit, vel quia ipsum Amos reputavit quasi arrepticium et insanum, et verba ejus frivola, reputatione indigna. Qui vides, id est tu Amos, videns, id est propheta. Qui enim nunc appellatur Propheta, olim dicebatur Videns, ut legitur primo Regum. Vocat itaque Amasias Amos prophetam, vel irrisorie, quemadmodum quarto Regum servi Ochoziæ dixerunt Eliæ : Homo Dei, hæc dicit rex. Vel propter multitudinem populi audientis sanctum Amos, non audet apertam irrogare injuriam. Vel loquitur blande, quatenus facilius inclinet ipsum Amos ad ea quæ suggerit. Gradere, id est, vade hinc, fuge in terram Juda, id est ad populum duarum tribuum, ubi Prophetæ Dei libentius audiuntur, quum ibi sit templum et cultus Dei. Vel ideo dicit hoc, quoniam natus fuit hic Amos de terra Juda, ad quam pertinuit Thecue civitas Amos. Et comede ibi panem : ibi enim datur a populo sustentaculum vitæ Prophetis ; vel, pasce ibi pecora tua, et vive. Quasi dicat : Rex tibi minatur, ideo consulo tibi ut fugias. Et prophetabis ibi populo tuo.
paras.en: [[7:12|And Amasias said to Amos|Et dixit Amasias ad Amos]]. Whether Amasias spoke the following words to Amos on Jeroboam's behalf or of himself, I do not know for certain. Jerome, however, plainly testifies that Jeroboam made no answer to the words of Amasias, despising the most empty words of his embassy. He made no answer, then, either because he knew from elsewhere that Amasias had sent him falsehoods, or because he thought Amos a man possessed and mad, and his words frivolous and unworthy of regard. [[7:12|Thou seer|Qui vides]] [literally “thou who seest”], that is, thou Amos, the seer, that is, the prophet. For [[1 Kings 9:9|he that is now called a prophet, in time past was called a seer|Qui enim nunc appellatur Propheta, olim dicebatur Videns]], as we read in the first book of Kings. So Amasias calls Amos a prophet, either mockingly, as in the fourth book of Kings the servants of Ochozias said to Elias: [[4 Kings 1:11|Man of God: Thus saith the king|Homo Dei, hæc dicit rex]]; or, because of the multitude of people listening to holy Amos, he does not dare to do him open injury; or he speaks smoothly, so as the more easily to bend Amos to what he urges. [[7:12|go|Gradere]], that is, go away from here, [[7:12|flee away into the land of Juda|fuge in terram Juda]], that is, to the people of the two tribes, where the Prophets of God are more gladly heard, since the temple and the worship of God are there. Or he says this because this Amos was born of the land of Juda, to which Thecue, the city of Amos, belonged[[Amos 1:1||]]. [[7:12|and eat bread there|Et comede ibi panem]]: for there the people give the Prophets their living; or, feed thy flocks there, and live. As if he were saying: the king threatens thee, so I advise thee to flee. [[7:12|and prophesy there|Et prophetabis ibi]] to thy people.

paras.t: Et in Bethel non adjicies ultra ut prophetes, quia sanctificatio regis est, id est urbs electa a rege ad vacandum cultui dei nostri, quo sanctificamur, videlicet aurei vituli, et domus regni est, id est regiam domum seu palatium habens.
paras.en: [[7:13|But prophesy not again any more in Bethel: because it is the king's sanctuary|Et in Bethel non adjicies ultra ut prophetes, quia sanctificatio regis est]], that is, the city chosen by the king for giving ourselves to the worship of our god, by whom we are sanctified, namely the golden calf, [[7:13|and it is the house of the kingdom|et domus regni est]], that is, having the royal house or palace.

paras.t: Et respondit Amos, et dixit ad Amasiam : Non sum propheta. Hoc, secundum Hieronymum et Glossam, est humilitatis, quod se negat prophetam. Sed quum humilitas non in falsitate, sed in veritate fundetur, sicut amor in cognitione, quomodo intelligendum est hoc, præsertim quum nequaquam sit mentiendum ? Ad hoc Glossa respondet, quod non semper Spiritus Sanctus administrat prophetiam Prophetis, sed ad tempus. Et tunc recte dicuntur prophetæ, quum illuminantur. Quod ergo ait, Non sum propheta, intellexit modo, ut sit sensus : Non sum propheta, id est, actualiter tactus non sum spiritu prophetiæ.
paras.en: [[7:14|And Amos answered and said to Amasias: I am not a prophet|Et respondit Amos, et dixit ad Amasiam : Non sum propheta]]. That he denies he is a prophet is, according to Jerome and the Gloss, a mark of humility. But since humility is founded not on falsehood but on truth, as love is on knowledge, how is this to be understood, especially since one must never lie? To this the Gloss answers that the Holy Ghost does not always minister prophecy to the Prophets, but for a time; and they are then rightly called prophets when they are enlightened. So when he says *I am not a prophet*, he understood *now*, so that the sense is: I am not a prophet, that is, I am not actually touched by the spirit of prophecy.

paras.t: Huic autem dicto alii quidam objiciunt : primo, quia in utroque Testamento Prophetæ vocantur, non solum qui actu tanguntur, sed etiam qui tangi consueverunt spiritu prophetiæ ; secundo, quia ut subditur, Amos quando hæc verba protulit, statim prædixit Amasiæ per spiritum prophetiæ, quid esset passurus. Hi itaque dicunt, quod sicut Amasias ironice dixit ad Amos, Qui vides, sic Amos respondet ironice, vel ironiæ sibi illatæ, Non sum, inquiens, propheta, videlicet talis qualem me reputas, qui putas me falsum prophetam, pro temporali commodo prophetantem. — Sed istis objicitur, quod Amos sub eadem serie sermonis et uno verborum contextu adjecit, Et non sum filius Prophetæ, etc., quod utique seriose assertiveque dicitur. Præterea præinductæ duæ instantiæ fieri possent contra verba Joannis Baptistæ, qui sacerdotibus et Levitis quærentibus, Propheta es tu? respondit : Non sum.
paras.en: Against this saying, however, certain others object: first, that in both Testaments those are called Prophets who are not only actually touched by the spirit of prophecy but also are wont to be touched by it; secondly, that, as follows, Amos, when he uttered these words, at once foretold to Amasias by the spirit of prophecy what he was to suffer. These therefore say that, as Amasias said ironically to Amos, [[7:12|Thou seer|Qui vides]], so Amos answers ironically, or to the irony aimed at him: *I am not*, says he, *a prophet*, that is, such a one as thou takest me for, who thinkest me a false prophet, prophesying for temporal gain. — But it is objected to these that Amos, in the same train of speech and in one connected sentence, added [[7:14|nor am I the son of a prophet|Et non sum filius Prophetæ]], etc., which is certainly said seriously and as an assertion. Besides, the two objections put forward could be made against the words of John the Baptist, who, when the priests and Levites asked, [[John 1:21|Art thou the prophet?|Propheta es tu?]] answered: I am not [Denis gives the answer as *Non sum*, “I am not”, which in the Gospel is the answer to “Art thou Elias?”; to this question the Douay-Rheims has “No”].

paras.t: Est itaque respondendum, quia ut Thomas et alii dicunt, prophetia non dicit donum habituale, sed actuale. Ideo responsio Glossæ jam assignata, conveniens est, et quod primo objicitur, faciliter solvitur. Propheta enim dicitur dupliciter, scilicet ab actu et usu seu habitu. Sed Amos loquitur de Propheta primo modo. Rursus verba Sanctorum, quibus se ipsos profunde humiliant, pie interpretanda sunt, et sufficit quod secundum aliquam considerationem verificentur, quamvis absolute vera non sunt, ut quum ait Salvator in Psalmo : Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo; Paulus quoque, Ego sum minimus Apostolorum, qui non sum dignus vocari Apostolus. Ad secundum argumentum dicendum, quod homo actualiter non intelligit nisi unum, secundum Philosophum. Ideo quando Amos dicebat, Non sum propheta, non in eodem momento actualiter intuebatur quod postea dixit. Et forte jam dudum audivit a Domino quod post verba hæc prænuntiavit Amasiæ. Postremo, translatio Septuaginta interpretum habet : Non eram propheta. Et tunc facilius solvitur dubium istud, quia refertur ad tempus præcedens revelationes sancto Amos infusas.
paras.en: The answer, then, is this: as Thomas and others say, prophecy denotes not a habitual gift but an actual one [that is, not a lasting quality of the soul but a passing act, given at the moment of revelation]. Therefore the answer of the Gloss already given is fitting, and the first objection is easily resolved. For a man is called a Prophet in two ways, namely from the act, and from use or habit; but Amos speaks of a Prophet in the first way. Again, the words of the Saints by which they humble themselves deeply are to be interpreted with reverence, and it is enough that they be true in some respect, though they are not true absolutely: as when the Saviour says in the Psalm, [[Ps 21:7|But I am a worm, and no man|Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo]]; and Paul too, [[1 Cor 15:9|I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle|Ego sum minimus Apostolorum, qui non sum dignus vocari Apostolus]]. To the second argument it must be said that a man actually understands only one thing at a time, according to the Philosopher. So when Amos said [[7:14|I am not a prophet|Non sum propheta]], he was not at that same moment actually beholding what he said afterwards. And perhaps he had heard long before from the Lord what he foretold to Amasias after these words. Lastly, the translation of the Seventy has: *I was not a prophet*. And then this difficulty is more easily resolved, since it refers to the time before the revelations poured into holy Amos.

paras.t: Et non sum filius Prophetæ. Unde nec pater hujus Amos ponitur in principio seu titulo libri præsentis. Qui enim in titulis Prophetarum ponuntur ut patres vel avi, erant prophetæ secundum regulam Hebræorum. Sed armentarius ego sum, id est pastor pecorum, scilicet ovium. Secundum Hieronymum, et secundum Glossam, fuit pastor pecorum aliorum : in quo patet paupertas Prophetæ. Vellicans sycomoros, id est frondes sycomori discerpens ad pecorum pastum. Sycomorus vero est arbor quæ dicitur rubus, afferens mora quæ famem pastorum depellunt, et folia esuriem pecorum. Et tulit me Dominus, id est, in prophetam clementer assumpsit, atque ad loca hæc destinavit, quum sequerer gregem, quem in deserto Thecuæ pavi; et dixit Dominus ad me : Vade et propheta ad populum meum Israel. Quasi dicat Amos : Quum ego ex tam vili servitio ad tam sublime officium Deo miserante promotus sum, obedire debeo Deo magis quam tibi aut alicui homini. In quibus verbis humilitas et obedientia Prophetæ commendatur, qui ad altiora promotus, non erubuit prioris status declivitatem.
paras.en: [[7:14|nor am I the son of a prophet|Et non sum filius Prophetæ]]. Hence neither is the father of this Amos set down at the beginning, or in the title, of the present book[[Amos 1:1||]]. For those who are set down in the titles of the Prophets as fathers or grandfathers were prophets, according to a rule of the Hebrews. [[7:14|but I am a herdsman|Sed armentarius ego sum]], that is, a keeper of beasts, namely of sheep. According to Jerome, and according to the Gloss, he was a keeper of other men's beasts: in which the Prophet's poverty is plain. [[7:14|plucking wild figs|Vellicans sycomoros]], that is, tearing off the leaves of the sycamore to feed the beasts [*vellicans sycomoros*, literally “plucking sycamores”; the Douay-Rheims has “wild figs”]. Now the sycamore is a tree that is called the bramble [*rubus*], bearing berries [*mora*] which drive away the hunger of the shepherds, and leaves which drive away the hunger of the beasts. [[7:15|And the Lord took me|Et tulit me Dominus]], that is, mercifully took me up to be a prophet, and sent me to these places, [[7:15|when I followed the flock|quum sequerer gregem]], which I fed in the desert of Thecua; [[7:15|and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel|et dixit Dominus ad me : Vade et propheta ad populum meum Israel]]. As if Amos were saying: since by God's mercy I have been raised from so mean a service to so high an office, I must obey God rather than thee or any man. In these words the humility and obedience of the Prophet are commended, who, raised to higher things, was not ashamed of the lowliness of his former state.

paras.t: Et nunc audi verbum Domini tu, Amasia, qui vetas me vaticinari hoc loco. Tu dicis mihi : Non prophetabis super Israel, id est populo decem tribuum, et non stillabis super domum idoli, id est, verba prophetiæ non fundes, sicut nubes stillat guttas, Israeliticæ plebi idola veneranti.
paras.en: [[7:16|And now hear thou the word of the Lord|Et nunc audi verbum Domini]], thou, Amasias, who forbiddest me to prophesy in this place. [[7:16|Thou sayest|Tu dicis mihi]] [Denis adds *mihi*, “to me”]: [[7:16|thou shalt not prophesy against Israel|Non prophetabis super Israel]], that is, to the people of the ten tribes, [[7:16|and thou shalt not drop thy word upon the house of the idol|et non stillabis super domum idoli]], that is, thou shalt not pour out the words of prophecy, as a cloud lets fall drops, on the Israelite people that worships idols.

paras.t: Propter hoc, hæc dicit Dominus, id est, propter hanc tuam prohibitionem mereris audire ac pati quæ dicam : Uxor tua in civitate Bethel fornicabitur, non sponte, sed ab Assyriis urbem ingressis violabitur, atque invita stuprabitur, te cernente, nec prohibere valente; et filii tui et filiæ tuæ in gladio cadent, id est, ab Assyriis trucidabuntur, et gravius punientur quam alii, quia et tuis consenserunt peccatis gravissimis. Et humus tua, id est terra quam possides, funiculo metietur, id est, ab hostibus mensurabitur, et alienis in certas partes dividetur ac dabitur. Rex enim Assyriorum, translatis decem tribubus, misit ad terram earum gentiles, qui eam possederunt, ut legitur quarto Regum. Et tu in terra polluta morieris, id est in regione Assyriorum vitiis idololatriæ plena; et Israel captivus migrabit de terra sua : ut dictum est sæpe.
paras.en: [[7:17|Therefore thus saith the Lord|Propter hoc, hæc dicit Dominus]], that is, for this thy forbidding thou deservest to hear and to suffer what I shall say: [[7:17|Thy wife shall play the harlot in the city|Uxor tua in civitate Bethel fornicabitur]] [Denis adds *Bethel*], not willingly, but she shall be violated by the Assyrians when they enter the city, and defiled against her will, while thou lookest on and canst not prevent it; [[7:17|and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword|et filii tui et filiæ tuæ in gladio cadent]], that is, shall be slaughtered by the Assyrians, and punished more heavily than others, because they consented to thy most grievous sins. [[7:17|and thy land|Et humus tua]], that is, the land thou possessest, [[7:17|shall be measured by a line|funiculo metietur]], that is, shall be measured out by the enemy, and divided into set portions and given to strangers. For the king of the Assyrians, when the ten tribes had been carried away, sent gentiles to their land, who possessed it, as we read in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:24||]]. [[7:17|and thou shalt die in a polluted land|Et tu in terra polluta morieris]], that is, in the country of the Assyrians, full of the vices of idolatry; [[7:17|and Israel shall go into captivity out of their land|et Israel captivus migrabit de terra sua]], as has often been said.

paras.t: Dicit hoc loco Hieronymus : Non est tantus dolor in filia stuprata, quantus in uxore polluta; nec tantus dolor in uxore violata, quantus in filiis trucidatis. Maritus uxorem mallet interfici, quam pollui. Grandis dolor incredibilisque ignominia, quando maritus in media civitate, cunctis præsentibus, uxoris injuriam prohibere non potest. — Denique ex his patet insuperabilis fortitudo, justitia, fiducia atque constantia sancti Prophetæ, qui pontificem tam districte tamque audacter corripuit, implens quod jubet Salvator : Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt.
paras.en: Jerome says on this place: The grief is not so great over a daughter defiled as over a wife polluted; nor so great over a wife violated as over sons slaughtered. A husband would rather his wife were killed than polluted. Great is the grief and unbelievable the shame when a husband, in the midst of the city, with all present, cannot prevent the wrong done to his wife. — Lastly, from these things is plain the unconquerable fortitude, justice, confidence and constancy of the holy Prophet, who rebuked the high priest so severely and so boldly, fulfilling what the Saviour commands: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]].

paras.t: Moraliter docemur ex isto capitulo, quod Dominus ad instantiam servorum suorum minas remittit, miseretur et salvat eos pro quibus oratur. Et sicut Amasias correptus, studuit regem contra corripientem incitare; sic multi impatientes dum corripiuntur, contra correptores faciunt querelas, apud prælatos vel principes diversa crimina objicientes, et correptores a se repellentes. Horum uxor, id est caro, fornicatur, dum rationi reluctans, sensualitati substernitur, concupiscentiisque deservit. Filii quoque eorum et filiæ, id est actus et passiones, in gladio tentationis cadunt, damnationem promerendo; et ipsi in terra polluta, id est corpore vitioso ac sordido, moriuntur.
paras.en: Morally, we are taught by this chapter that the Lord, at the urging of his servants, remits his threats, has mercy, and saves those for whom prayer is made. And as Amasias, when rebuked, strove to stir up the king against the one who rebuked him, so many who are impatient, when they are rebuked, make complaints against those who rebuke them, laying various charges before prelates or princes, and driving their correctors away from them. Their wife, that is, the flesh, plays the harlot, when, struggling against reason, she lies down under sensuality and serves the concupiscences. Their sons too and daughters, that is, their acts and passions, fall by the sword of temptation, earning damnation; and they themselves die in a polluted land, that is, in a body vicious and unclean.

8.title: Expositio litteralis capituli octavi: Hæc ostendit mihi Dominus Deus.
8.title_en: Literal exposition of the eighth chapter: These things the Lord God shewed to me.

paras.t: Rursus ostendit Dominus proximum esse tempus captivitatis populi Israel.
paras.en: Again the Lord shows that the time of the captivity of the people of Israel is near.

paras.t: Hæc quæ sequuntur, ostendit mihi Dominus Deus in visione imaginaria : prout in præcedenti dicebatur articulo. Et ecce uncinus pomorum, id est lignum curvum seu uncus, quo rami arborum remotiores attrahuntur, ut poma dependentia, quæ cum manu attingi non poterunt, colligantur. Et dixit Dominus : Quid tu vides, Amos ? Et dixi : Uncinum pomorum. Et dixit Dominus ad me, declarando mihi intellectualiter quid visio illa imaginaria designaret : Venit finis super populum meum Israel : id est, quemadmodum unco rami trahuntur, et proximi fiunt trahenti, sic proximum feci tempus captivitatis Israeliticæ plebis. Non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum, id est, impunitum eum diutius non relinquam, sed vindicans stabo, donec dispereat. Vel sensus est, quod non consolabor eum de cetero, redimendo decem tribus a captivitate.
paras.en: [[8:1|These things|Hæc]], namely those that follow, [[8:1|the Lord shewed to me|ostendit mihi Dominus Deus]] in an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination, as distinct from a bodily or a purely intellectual vision], as was said in the preceding article. [[8:1|and behold a hook to draw down the fruit|Et ecce uncinus pomorum]], that is, a curved stick or hook, by which the more distant branches of trees are drawn in, so that the hanging fruit, which cannot be reached by hand, may be gathered. [[8:2|And he said: What seest thou, Amos? And I said: A hook to draw down fruit|Et dixit Dominus : Quid tu vides, Amos ? Et dixi : Uncinum pomorum]]. [[8:2|And the Lord said to me|Et dixit Dominus ad me]], declaring to me intellectually what that imaginary vision signified: [[8:2|The end is come upon my people Israel|Venit finis super populum meum Israel]]: that is, as branches are drawn by a hook and come close to the one who draws them, so have I brought near the time of the captivity of the Israelite people. [[8:2|I will not again pass by them any more|Non adjiciam ultra ut pertranseam eum]], that is, I will no longer leave them unpunished, but will stand by taking vengeance until they perish. Or the sense is that I will not console them henceforth by redeeming the ten tribes from captivity.

paras.t: Et stridebunt cardines templi in die illa, dicit Dominus Deus, id est, fragorem quemdam facient, quum destruentur, quemadmodum ædificia cadentia. Vel per stridorem templi, metaphorice insinuatur molestissima anxietas populi. Quidam per templum hoc loco intelligunt fanum in quo aureus vitulus adorabatur : et hi dicunt Prophetam jam loqui ad decem tribus dumtaxat. Hieronymus vero exponit de templo Domini in Jerusalem : ideo secundum eum, ista dicuntur contra utrumque regnum. Multi morientur. Assyrii enim multos ex decem tribubus occiderunt, et multos transtulerunt. Simili modo fecerunt Chaldæi populo Juda. Et in omni loco projicietur silentium, id est, habitatoribus occisis vel reclamare non audentibus, erit silentium in locis et domibus duodecim tribuum. Hæc autem præsertim impleta sunt in populo Judæorum, propter Christi occisionem a Romanis dejecto : qui finaliter sunt relicti, nec habent quod rationabiliter Christianis respondeant.
paras.en: [[8:3|And the hinges of the temple shall screak in that day, saith the Lord God|Et stridebunt cardines templi in die illa, dicit Dominus Deus]], that is, they will make a kind of crash when they are destroyed, like falling buildings. Or by the creaking of the temple the most grievous anguish of the people is hinted at metaphorically. Some understand by the temple in this place the shrine in which the golden calf was worshipped, and these say that the Prophet is now speaking to the ten tribes only. But Jerome expounds it of the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem; and so, according to him, these things are said against both kingdoms. [[8:3|many shall die|Multi morientur]]: for the Assyrians slew many of the ten tribes and carried many away, and the Chaldeans did the same to the people of Juda. [[8:3|silence shall be cast in every place|Et in omni loco projicietur silentium]], that is, the inhabitants being slain or not daring to cry out against it, there will be silence in the places and houses of the twelve tribes. These things were fulfilled above all in the people of the Jews, cast down by the Romans for the slaying of Christ: they have been left behind at the last, and have nothing to answer the Christians with reason.

paras.t: Audite hoc quod minando prædico, qui conteritis pauperem, id est vos, pauperum oppressores, et deficere facitis, id est, ad penuriam perducitis, pauperes terræ vestræ, quum tamen in Deuteronomio jusserit Deus : Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos. Tales sunt, qui tempora cara inducunt, et necessaria carius vendunt.
paras.en: [[8:4|Hear this|Audite hoc]], which I preach as a threat, [[8:4|you that crush the poor|qui conteritis pauperem]], that is, you oppressors of the poor, [[8:4|and make|et deficere facitis]] to fail, that is, bring to penury, [[8:4|the needy of the land|pauperes terræ]] of yours [Denis's text reads *pauperes*, "the poor"; the margin gives the Vulgate's *egenos*, "the needy"], although God commanded in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 15:4|there shall be no poor nor beggar among you|Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos]]. Such are those who bring on times of dearness and sell what is needed for life at a higher price.

paras.t: Dicentes : Quando transibit messis Israel? id est, optamus ut tempus messionis et abundantiæ transeat, et venundabimus merces, id est, blada atque similia, quæ tempore messis pro parvo pretio dantur, care vendemus; et sabbatum quando transibit, in quo secundum legem non fit venditio? et aperiemus frumentum, id est, blada clausa deducemus ad publicum tempore caristiæ. Hoc faciunt cupidi, qui frumenta reservant, ut postmodum pretiosius venundentur : de quibus scriptum est in Proverbiis, Qui abscondunt frumentum in tempore, maledicentur. Ut imminuamus mensuram, id est, mensurando aliquid fraudulenter subtrahamus ementibus, et augeamus siclum, id est pretium, vendendo carius quo poterimus, et supponamus stateras dolosas : quemadmodum fertur in Psalmo : Mendaces filii hominum in stateris, ut decipiant de vanitate in id ipsum. Hæc faciunt avari et injusti mercatores. Contra quos Dominus in Levitico jussit : Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura.
paras.en: [[8:5|Saying: When will the month be over|Dicentes : Quando transibit messis]] of Israel? [Denis reads *messis*, "harvest", where the Vulgate has *mensis*, "month"; his gloss follows his reading] That is, we wish the time of harvest and plenty to pass, [[8:5|and we shall sell our wares|et venundabimus merces]], that is, we shall sell dear the corn and the like, which at harvest time go for a small price; [[8:5|and the sabbath|et sabbatum]], when will it be over, on which according to the law no selling is done? [[8:5|and we shall open the corn|et aperiemus frumentum]], that is, we shall bring the corn we have shut up out to the market in a time of dearth. This the covetous do, who hold back corn so that it may be sold later at a higher price; of whom it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 11:26|He that hideth up corn, shall be cursed|Qui abscondunt frumentum in tempore, maledicentur]]. [[8:5|that we may lessen the measure|Ut imminuamus mensuram]], that is, in measuring, fraudulently keep back something from the buyers, [[8:5|and increase the sicle|et augeamus siclum]], that is, the price, selling as dear as we can, [[8:5|and may convey in deceitful balances|et supponamus stateras dolosas]]: as is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 61:10|the sons of men are liars in the balances: that by vanity they may together deceive|Mendaces filii hominum in stateris, ut decipiant de vanitate in id ipsum]]. This is what greedy and unjust merchants do. Against them the Lord commanded in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:35|Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure|Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura]].

paras.t: Ut possideatis in argento egenos, id est, inopes per usuram in vestram potestatem redigatis, vel in tantam deducatis penuriam, quod cogantur se vobis in servos vendere et ancillas, et pauperes pro calceamentis, id est, pro rebus vilibus acquiramus, possideamus, vendamus; et quisquilias frumenti, id est purgamenta, paleas et pulverem, vendamus una cum tritico, talia fraudulenter miscendo cum bladis, quum tamen Jeremias dicat : Quid paleis cum tritico?
paras.en: [[8:6|That we may possess the needy for money|Ut possideatis in argento egenos]] [Denis's text has *possideatis*, "that you may possess"; the margin gives the other reading, *possideamus*, "that we may possess", as in the Vulgate], that is, that you may bring the needy into your power through usury, or drive them into such penury that they are forced to sell themselves to you as menservants and maidservants, [[8:6|and the poor for a pair of shoes|et pauperes pro calceamentis]], that is, that we may acquire, possess and sell them for worthless things; and [[8:6|the refuse of the corn|et quisquilias frumenti]], that is, the sweepings, chaff and dust, let us sell together with the wheat, fraudulently mixing such things with the grain; although Jeremias says: [[Jer 23:28|what hath the chaff to do with the wheat|Quid paleis cum tritico]]?

paras.t: Juravit Dominus in superbiam Jacob, id est contra arrogantiam populi Israel : Si oblitus fuero usque in finem, id est, nunquam tradam oblivioni, omnia opera eorum mala. Deus enim tamdiu recordari dicitur peccatorum, quamdiu ulciscitur vel non dimittit ea. Hi vero indurati erant in vitiis, ideo æternaliter puniuntur. Vel sensus est, quod Deus usque in finem mundi deseret decem tribus, et etiam duas, et tunc indulgebit ac miserebitur eis. Huic quoque simile est illud in Jeremia : Peccatum Juda scriptum est stilo ferreo in lapide adamantino.
paras.en: [[8:7|The Lord hath sworn against the pride of Jacob|Juravit Dominus in superbiam Jacob]], that is, against the arrogance of the people of Israel: [[8:7|surely I will never forget|Si oblitus fuero usque in finem]] [literally "if I forget them unto the end", a Hebrew form of oath], that is, I will never consign to oblivion [[8:7|all their works|omnia opera eorum]], evil as they are. For God is said to remember sins as long as He punishes them or does not forgive them. And these men were hardened in their vices, and so they are punished eternally. Or the sense is that God will forsake the ten tribes, and the two as well, until the end of the world, and then will pardon them and have mercy on them. Like this too is that saying in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:1|The sin of Juda is written with a pen of iron, with the point of a diamond|Peccatum Juda scriptum est stilo ferreo in lapide adamantino]] [Denis has *in lapide adamantino*, "on a stone of diamond", where the Vulgate has *in ungue adamantino*, "with the point of a diamond"].

paras.t: Numquid super isto non commovebitur terra? id est, nonne pro tantis peccatis habitatores terræ Israel turbabuntur? Et lugebit omnis habitator ejus, id est omnes populi tribuum Israel captivitate jam ingruente, et ascendet in captivitatem et debitam pœnam, quasi fluvius, id est copiose atque celeriter, universus habitator seu populus Israel. Non quod nullus evasit, sed quia comparatione aliorum paucissimi evaserunt. Hinc in Jeremia habetur : Numquid super his non visitabo, et in gente tali non ulciscetur anima mea? In Ezechiele quoque : Terra quum peccaverit, interficiam de ea hominem et jumentum. Et in Psalmo : Hæc fecisti, et tacui : existimasti inique quod ero tui similis; arguam te, et statuam contra faciem tuam. Et ejicietur et defluet quasi rivus Ægypti.
paras.en: [[8:8|Shall not the land tremble for this|Numquid super isto non commovebitur terra]]? That is, will not the inhabitants of the land of Israel be troubled for such great sins? [[8:8|and every one mourn that dwelleth therein|Et lugebit omnis habitator ejus]], that is, all the peoples of the tribes of Israel, now that captivity is coming upon them, [[8:8|and rise up|et ascendet]] into captivity and due punishment [[8:8|as a river|quasi fluvius]], that is, in great numbers and swiftly, [[8:8|altogether|universus]]: every inhabitant, that is, the whole people of Israel. Not that none escaped, but because very few escaped in comparison with the rest. Hence it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:9|Shall I not visit for these things|Numquid super his non visitabo]], [[Jer 5:9|and shall not my soul take revenge on such a nation|et in gente tali non ulciscetur anima mea?]][[Jer 5:29||]]? And in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 14:13|when a land shall sin|Terra quum peccaverit]], I [[Ezech 14:13|will destroy man and beast out of it|interficiam de ea hominem et jumentum]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:21|These things hast thou done, and I was silent. Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face|Hæc fecisti, et tacui : existimasti inique quod ero tui similis; arguam te, et statuam contra faciem tuam]]. [[8:8|and be cast out, and run down as the river of Egypt?|Et ejicietur et defluet quasi rivus Ægypti]].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus, id est in die captivitatis populi Israel : Occidet sol in meridie, id est, omnia prospera et jucunda vertentur eis in adversa ac tristia; et tenebrescere faciam terram, id est, habitatores terræ Israel operiam tenebris calamitatis, in die luminis, id est, quum aliis prospera succedent. Iste quippe est modus loquendi Scripturæ, ut dictum est plenius Joelis secundo.
paras.en: [[8:9|And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord God|Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus]], that is, in the day of the captivity of the people of Israel: [[8:9|the sun shall go down at midday|Occidet sol in meridie]], that is, all that is prosperous and joyful will be turned for them into adversity and sorrow; [[8:9|and I will make the earth dark|et tenebrescere faciam terram]], that is, I will cover the inhabitants of the land of Israel with the darkness of calamity, [[8:9|in the day of light|in die luminis]], that is, when others are prospering. For this is the way Scripture speaks, as was said more fully on the second chapter of Joel[[Joel 2:10||]].

paras.t: Et convertam festivitates vestras in luctum, et omnia cantica vestra in planctum. Venientibus namque Chaldæis atque Assyriis, cessaverunt festa et cantica duodecim tribuum, et aliud non noverunt nisi contristari et lamentari. Et inducam super omne dorsum vestrum saccum. Hoc dicitur, vel quia in afflictione positi, induerunt se sacco sive cilicio, quemadmodum Ninivitæ, vel quia in captivitatem ducebantur sacco induti. Et super omne caput vestrum inducam calvitium. Consuetudo enim veterum fuit, ut in tristitia positi raderent capita, sicut et Job, qui tonso capite sedit in sterquilinio. Vel hoc ideo dictum est, quoniam captorum capita ab hostibus radebantur, juxta illud Deuteronomii : De captivitate nudati inimicorum capitis. Et ponam eam, videlicet terram Juda ac Israel, quasi luctum unigeniti, id est habitatores ejus in tanto mœrore et planctu, quantus est planctus matris unici filii mortem deflentis, et novissima ejus, id est extremam populi hujus captivitatem et punitionem, ponam quasi diem amarum, id est similem amaritudini mortis.
paras.en: [[8:10|And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation|Et convertam festivitates vestras in luctum, et omnia cantica vestra in planctum]]. For when the Chaldeans and Assyrians came, the feasts and songs of the twelve tribes ceased, and they knew nothing but grief and lamentation. [[8:10|and I will bring up sackcloth upon every back of yours|Et inducam super omne dorsum vestrum saccum]]. This is said either because, being in affliction, they clothed themselves in sackcloth or haircloth, like the Ninivites[[Jon 3:5||]], or because they were led into captivity clad in sackcloth. [[8:10|and baldness upon every head|Et super omne caput vestrum inducam calvitium]]. For it was the custom of the ancients, when in sorrow, to shave their heads, as Job too did, who with his head shorn[[Job 1:20||]] sat on the dunghill[[Job 2:8||]]. Or this is said because the heads of captives were shaved by the enemy, according to that of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:42|of the captivity, of the bare head of the enemies|De captivitate nudati inimicorum capitis]]. [[8:10|and I will make it|Et ponam eam]], namely the land of Juda and Israel, [[8:10|as the mourning of an only son|quasi luctum unigeniti]], that is, its inhabitants in as great grief and wailing as is the wailing of a mother weeping for the death of her only son, [[8:10|and the latter end thereof|et novissima ejus]], that is, the final captivity and punishment of this people, I will make [[8:10|as a bitter day|quasi diem amarum]], that is, like the bitterness of death.

paras.t: Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et emittam famem in terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Domini, Christo testante : Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur. Desiderium autem audiendi verbum Dei ad emendationem, est esurire et sitire justitiam : hoc ergo non prædicitur per modum comminationis. Quod autem nunc dicitur, est comminatio dura. Quidam igitur exponunt hæc de decem tribubus, quæ frequenter spreverunt verba Dei per Prophetas prolata. Idcirco imminente earum captivitate, quando a Prophetis quærebant consilium, meruerunt privari verbo Dei per Prophetas.
paras.en: [[8:11|Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will send forth a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst of water, but of hearing the word of the Lord|Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et emittam famem in terram : non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Domini]]. Christ bears witness: [[Matt 5:6|Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill|Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur]]. Now the desire to hear the word of God for one's amendment is to hunger and thirst after justice; that, then, is not foretold by way of threat. But what is said here is a hard threat. Some, then, expound these words of the ten tribes, which often spurned the words of God spoken through the Prophets. Therefore, when their captivity was at hand and they sought counsel from the Prophets, they deserved to be deprived of the word of God through the Prophets.

paras.t: Et commovebuntur a mari usque ad mare, et ab aquilone usque ad orientem circumibunt, id est, a mari Mediterraneo usque ad mare Galilææ, et a plaga terræ suæ aquilonari usque ad partem terræ suæ orientalem, videlicet per omnes partes territorii sui pergent, quærentes verbum Domini, id est consilium a Prophetis, et non invenient consolationem.
paras.en: [[8:12|And they shall move from sea to sea, and from the north to the east|Et commovebuntur a mari usque ad mare, et ab aquilone usque ad orientem]], [[8:12|they shall go about|circumibunt]], that is, from the Mediterranean Sea to the Sea of Galilee, and from the northern quarter of their land to its eastern part, that is, they will go through every part of their territory, [[8:12|seeking the word of the Lord|quærentes verbum Domini]], that is, counsel from the Prophets, [[8:12|and shall not find|et non invenient]] consolation.

paras.t: Alii autem exponunt ista pro tempore Christi, quando Judæis ablata est spiritualis intelligentia Scripturarum, ita quod famem habent audiendi spiritualem sensum paginæ sanctæ. Quod non est intelligendum, quasi ipsi vere cupiant spiritualem hunc sensum, sed quod habent defectum hujus spiritualis cibi et potus a quibus reficitur anima, quamvis ipsi ignorent se tam defectuosos et vacuos : et hic defectus vocatur nunc fames et sitis. Certum est etiam quod Judæi a tempore captivitatis suæ a Romanis, desideraverunt audire verbum consolatorium per Prophetas, sed nullus interim missus est eis. Moventur ergo a mari Britannico usque ad mare Atlanticum, id est ab occidente ad meridiem, et ab aquilone usque ad orientem; sed nihil proficiunt, quoniam unigenitum Filium Dei, Verbum quod erat in principio, obstinato corde repellunt.
paras.en: Others expound these words of the time of Christ, when the spiritual understanding of the Scriptures was taken away from the Jews, so that they have a famine of hearing the spiritual sense of the sacred page. This is not to be understood as if they truly longed for this spiritual sense, but that they lack this spiritual food and drink by which the soul is refreshed, though they do not know that they are so lacking and empty: and this lack is here called hunger and thirst. It is certain also that the Jews, from the time of their captivity by the Romans, have desired to hear a word of consolation through the Prophets, but none has been sent to them in the meantime. So they move from the British Sea to the Atlantic, that is, from west to south, and from the north to the east; but they gain nothing, since with obstinate heart they reject the only-begotten Son of God, the Word that was in the beginning[[John 1:1||]].

paras.t: In die illa deficient virgines pulchræ et adolescentes in siti. Hoc dupliciter explanatur. Primo, quod tempore captivitatis Israel ab Assyriis, vel duarum tribuum a Chaldæis, virgines et adolescentes corporali siti afflicti sunt. Secundo, quod synagogæ, quæ significantur per virgines, sicut Ecclesia dicitur virgo et sponsa, et adolescentes, id est doctores Synagogæ, olim per sapientiam floridi, defecerunt in siti verbi Dei. Primæ vero expositioni magis videntur consonare verba sequentia : Qui jurant in delicto Samariæ, id est per vitulos aureos, in quibus provincia tota decem tribuum gravissime deliquit, et dicunt : Vivit dominus deus tuus, Dan, id est vitulus aureus positus in Dan, cui vitulo divinitatem adscripserunt, et vivit via Bersabee, id est deus seu idolum, ob cujus adorationem imus usque ad locum Bersabee, ubi idola colebantur. Quemadmodum enim cultores veri Dei jurabant dicendo, Vivit Dominus : sic isti per idola vitulosque jurabant. Et cadent coram hostibus, et non resurgent ultra ad pristinum statum.
paras.en: [[8:13|In that day the fair virgins, and the young men shall faint for thirst|In die illa deficient virgines pulchræ et adolescentes in siti]]. This is explained in two ways. First, that at the time of the captivity of Israel by the Assyrians, or of the two tribes by the Chaldeans, virgins and young men were afflicted with bodily thirst. Second, that the synagogues, which are signified by the virgins (as the Church is called virgin and bride), and the young men, that is, the teachers of the Synagogue, once flourishing in wisdom, fainted for thirst of the word of God. But the words that follow seem to agree better with the first explanation: [[8:14|They that swear by the sin of Samaria|Qui jurant in delicto Samariæ]], that is, by the golden calves, in which the whole province of the ten tribes sinned most grievously, [[8:14|and say|et dicunt]]: [[8:14|Thy God, O Dan, liveth|Vivit dominus deus tuus, Dan]], that is, the golden calf set up in Dan, to which calf they ascribed divinity, [[8:14|and the way of Bersabee liveth|et vivit via Bersabee]], that is, the god or idol for whose worship we go as far as the place Bersabee, where idols were worshipped. For as the worshippers of the true God swore by saying, "The Lord liveth", so these swore by idols and calves. [[8:14|and they shall fall|Et cadent]] before their enemies, [[8:14|and shall rise no more|et non resurgent ultra]] to their former state.

paras.t: Mystice sol occidit in meridie, dum tempore gratiæ vel in dimidio dierum nostrorum non illuminamur a Christo, qui est sol intelligentiæ atque justitiæ. Unde in Sapientiæ libro perditi conqueruntur : Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis. Et tenebrescere faciam permissive, id est vitiis obcæcari, terram, id est homines carnales terrenis immersos, in die luminis, id est, dum electi ac spirituales gratiæ perfunduntur fulgore. Super horum carnalium dorsum inducitur saccus, id est contemptibilis ac deformis vitiorum amictus. De quibus cantamus : Operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua. Sicut enim est amictus virtutum, ita et vitiorum. Et super omne caput calvitium. Per caput ratio designatur : cui infertur calvitium, dum septiformi donorum Spiritus Sancti decore privatur, et nuda, bonoque virtutum colore spoliata conspicitur. Et ponam eam quasi luctum unigeniti, quoniam maxime deploranda est miseria hujuscemodi rationis.
paras.en: Mystically, [[8:9|the sun shall go down at midday|sol occidit in meridie]] when, in the time of grace or in the midst of our days, we are not enlightened by Christ, who is the sun of understanding and of justice. Hence in the book of Wisdom the lost complain: [[Wis 5:6|the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us|Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis]]. [[8:9|and I will make the earth dark|Et tenebrescere faciam]] by permission, that is, [I will let it] be blinded by vices: [[8:9|the earth|terram]], that is, carnal men sunk in earthly things, [[8:9|in the day of light|in die luminis]], that is, while the elect and spiritual are bathed in the brightness of grace. Upon the back of these carnal men is brought [[8:10|sackcloth|saccus]], that is, the contemptible and ugly garment of vices, of whom we sing: [[Ps 72:6|they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness|Operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua]]. For as there is a garment of virtues, so there is one of vices. [[8:10|and baldness upon every head|Et super omne caput calvitium]]. By the head reason is signified, on which baldness is brought when it is stripped of the beauty of the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost, and is seen naked and despoiled of the fair colour of the virtues. [[8:10|and I will make it as the mourning of an only son|Et ponam eam quasi luctum unigeniti]], since the misery of such a reason is most of all to be lamented.

paras.t: Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et emittam famem in terram, etc. Hæc pœnalis atque damnosa missio famis est, dum Christiani optant audire verbum Dei, sed exigente justitia Dei, non merentur illud sortiri, quoniam ex timore pœnarum, ex pressura adversitatum, ex privato prorsus amore, non ordinato affectu, hoc appetunt, et aptum tempus audiendi verbum Dei spreverunt. Unde et quidam instante jam hora mortis, quærunt inducias vel unius diei, nec exaudiuntur.
paras.en: [[8:11|Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will send forth a famine into the land|Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et emittam famem in terram]], etc. This sending of famine is penal and ruinous when Christians wish to hear the word of God but, as God's justice requires, do not deserve to obtain it, because they seek it out of fear of punishment, under the pressure of adversity, from a wholly private love [that is, love of self] and not from ordered affection, and they spurned the fitting time for hearing the word of God. Hence some, when the hour of death is already upon them, ask for a respite of even one day, and are not heard.

paras.t: In die illa deficient virgines pulchræ, id est animæ vel particulares Ecclesiæ, olim gratiarum pulchritudine adornatæ, quæ per negligentiam suam a gratia exciderunt, et adolescentes, id est, qui dudum fortiter vicerunt malignum, quorum renovabatur juventus ut aquilæ, in siti, id est in carentia et defectu verbi Dei, quo ex sua ruina, inconstantia atque ignavia qua prolapsi sunt, merentur non refici.
paras.en: [[8:13|In that day the fair virgins|In die illa deficient virgines pulchræ]] shall faint, that is, souls or particular Churches once adorned with the beauty of graces, which through their negligence have fallen from grace, [[8:13|and the young men|et adolescentes]], that is, those who once valiantly overcame the wicked one[[1 John 2:13||]][[1 John 2:14||]], whose youth was renewed like the eagle's[[Ps 102:5||]], [[8:13|for thirst|in siti]], that is, in the want and lack of the word of God, by which, because of their fall, their inconstancy and the sloth through which they lapsed, they deserve not to be refreshed.
